estates.label: Estates & Land
estates.desc: The estates here and land for sale

lodging.label: Rooms & Services
lodging.desc: Take a room for the night, a meal, a bath

stable_horse.label: Sell Horses
stable_horse.desc: Sell your mount or tamed horses

innerMapRenderer._note_characters: LPC character presets — each defines compositing layers drawn bottom-to-top. Paths are relative to assets/lpc/Characters/. Walk.png and Idle.png are appended automatically.

npcAppearanceMap._note: Maps NPC type keys to arrays of valid character preset IDs. NPC picks one by seeded index.

militaristic.label: Militaristic
militaristic.summary: Keeps a 15% larger standing army that rebuilds 50% faster; marches only when at least as strong as the foe, and rarely sues for peace

peaceful.label: Peaceful
peaceful.summary: Rarely expands or fights; trades widely

aggressive.label: Aggressive
aggressive.summary: Expands and declares war often, sometimes recklessly

defaults.name: Kingdom of Valdoria
defaults.description: A proud and ancient kingdom known for its disciplined armies and grand cities.

defaults.name: Kingdom of Sylvaris
defaults.description: Forest dwellers who live in harmony with nature, masters of archery and herbal lore.

defaults.name: Khanate of Kharzun
defaults.description: Fierce horse riders of the steppes, united under a mighty Khan.

defaults.name: Theocracy of Azurath
defaults.description: A nation governed by faith, where priests hold more power than warriors.

defaults.name: Republic of Merathis
defaults.description: Expert sailors and traders who dominate the coastal trade routes.

defaults.name: Holds of Durheim
defaults.description: Dwarven-built strongholds carved into mountain peaks. Masters of siege craft and mineral wealth.

defaults.name: Dominion of Miregloom
defaults.description: Reclusive marsh-dwellers who command dark alchemy and know poisons no healer can cure.

defaults.name: Conclave of Luminara
defaults.description: A magocracy ruled by a council of sorcerers. Knowledge and arcane power are currency here.

defaults.name: Jarldom of Frostmark
defaults.description: Hardy northern clans who worship the storm and raid southern shores each thaw season.

defaults.name: Sultanate of Ashkari
defaults.description: Oasis lords who control the great desert trade routes and guard ancient buried treasures.

realmStyles._doc: How a realm's ruler is styled (Kingdom.rulerStyle: the player's crowned title, a player ruler's display name). The realm's type is read off its name ('Khanate of Kharzun', 'the Kharzun Khanate'); its ruler takes the type's title for their gender, or, for a type with none (Dominion, Realm, ...) or a name with no type, the culture's. 'of': 'land' styles the ruler of the land ('King of Valdoria'); 'realm' of the realm itself ('Khan of the Kharzun Khanate').

market._taxGuide: What the Royal Treasury's Taxes tab (src/ui/ui/techTreasury.js via src/ui/actionMenu/taxGuide.js) says your settlement tax is. {perHead} is Taxation.TAX_PER_HEAD; the per-level happiness target, growth and welfare numbers are computed from taxRates. Keep each line to what systems/marketDynamics.js Taxation and systems/labour.js read.

taxGuide.what: Your own tax: one rate for every settlement you rule (towns you founded or conquered, and holdings granted you). It is not the crown's land, hearth and excise taxes: those are the realm's, set by its ruler in the Crown's Treasury.
taxGuide.who: The people of your settlements, out of their town's purse, every 7 days.
taxGuide.how: {perHead}g a head a week × the rate × the town's mood (×0.75 at happiness 0 to ×1.25 at 100) × the harvest (×0.4 to ×1.4) × its development (markets, harbours, a good or a skimming steward) × events × your office's tax perk.
effects: Happiness: each collection it moves a quarter of the way toward 50 + 1.5 × the rate's happiness bonus (plus its peoples, buildings and patronage).
Growth: the rate's yearly growth (or decline) is applied each week; a town never falls below 10.
Welfare and migration: every class's welfare falls by (rate − 15%) × its weight (peasants feel it most), so people leave a heavily taxed town for its trade partners, and come to a lightly taxed one.
Loyalty: a conquered town gains or loses (happiness − 50) / 25 loyalty a week; a disloyal colony rebels.
The council: sworn to a crown, you need the council's vote to raise the rate; the Guilds and the Commons like low taxes.

CROSSBOWMAN.name: Crossbowman
CROSSBOWMAN.description: Heavy ranged unit with armor-piercing bolts

WAR_ELEPHANT.name: War Elephant
WAR_ELEPHANT.description: Massive war beasts that trample enemy formations

SIEGE_ENGINE.name: Siege Engine
SIEGE_ENGINE.description: Catapults and trebuchets for breaching walls: +40% army power when raiding or besieging a settlement (max +100%)

BERSERKER.name: Berserker
BERSERKER.description: Frenzied warriors who fight with reckless fury

ASSASSIN.name: Assassin
ASSASSIN.description: Shadow operatives: each gives a 15% chance (max 60%) to slay the enemy commander before battle, breaking their morale

BATTLE_MAGE.name: Battle Mage
BATTLE_MAGE.description: Sorcerers hurling area spells: each weakens the enemy host by 5% (max 30%)

LONGBOWMAN.name: Longbowman
LONGBOWMAN.description: Elite archers with extended range: opening volleys add up to +6% power against melee-heavy foes

SHIELD_WALL.name: Shield Wall
SHIELD_WALL.description: Heavily armored defensive formation: +10% army power when you are attacked (max +50%)

WAR_GALLEY.name: War Galley
WAR_GALLEY.description: Oared warship. Never fights on land: it escorts your ships at sea and blockades coastal settlements you raid or besiege. Recruited only at ports.

SCOUT.name: Scout
SCOUT.description: Fast reconnaissance: +1 vision radius and +1 movement per day while in your army

navalRules._doc: How much of each domain fights in each theatre. land = inland battles, coastal = raids/sieges on a port settlement, sea = fights on water. escortShare = part of the war-galley squadron strength added to every fight your own ships take on at sea.

kingdomNavy._doc: Royal fleets of the AI kingdoms (src/world/kingdomNavy.js). A realm keeps perPort strength per port settlement (+capitalPort if its capital is a port), x the best traitMultiplier, and never more than treasury / reservePerStrength. It builds buildRate of the gap a day at buildCost gold per point and pays upkeep gold per point a day. In a war fleets meet (battle.chance a day); a fleet with blockade.superiority over the enemy's blockades its ports: income falls by incomeLoss x the realm's port share, the attacker storms its ports with +siegeBonus, and its port markets pay marketSell / charge marketBuy, or close when the blockader is tightRatio times stronger. Hostile fleets intercept the player's ships within intercept.radius of their ports. liegeService: galleys a sworn player lends the liege's fleet in war.

BANDIT_HUNT.name: Bandit Hunt
BANDIT_HUNT.description: Hunt down bandits threatening trade routes

SIEGE_SUPPORT.name: Siege Support
SIEGE_SUPPORT.description: Support a kingdom in a siege

MONSTER_HUNT.name: Monster Hunt
MONSTER_HUNT.description: Track and slay a dangerous creature terrorizing the land

PATROL_ROADS.name: Patrol Roads
PATROL_ROADS.description: Keep the trade roads safe from bandits and wild beasts

BORDER_DEFENSE.name: Border Defense
BORDER_DEFENSE.description: Defend a kingdom's border from encroaching enemies

PIRATE_RAID.name: Raid Pirate Cove
PIRATE_RAID.description: Assault a pirate stronghold and recover stolen goods

RUIN_CLEARANCE.name: Ruin Clearance
RUIN_CLEARANCE.description: Clear dangerous creatures from ancient ruins

REBEL_SUPPRESSION.name: Rebel Suppression
REBEL_SUPPRESSION.description: Quell a peasant rebellion in a troubled province

ASSASSINATION_CONTRACT.name: Assassination Contract
ASSASSINATION_CONTRACT.description: Eliminate a high-value target — extremely dangerous

sieges._doc: Sieges as operations (src/systems/sieges.js). Investing a settlement starts a siege; each day the defenders eat their stores, lose morale and may fall sick, while the camp forages and eats from the packs, may fall sick and desert. Stances: blockade (tighten the cordon), works (build an engine), sap (dig a mine under the walls). Storm, negotiate terms, fight a relief host or lift the siege.

ram.name: Battering ram
ram.effect: Breaks the gate: the defence is 15% weaker when you storm.

tower.name: Siege tower
tower.effect: Carries men over the walls: walls count half when you storm.

trebuchet.name: Trebuchet
trebuchet.effect: Batters the walls every day (-6 integrity a day).

fieldBattle._doc: Phased field battles (player/fieldBattle.js): three phases, a stance before each, withdraw between them. Built-in defaults; keys here override them.

aggressive.name: Aggressive
aggressive.text: Press hard: more blows struck and taken.

hold.name: Hold the line
hold.text: Shields locked: fewer losses; pikemen and defenders stand firmer.

feint.name: Feigned retreat
feint.text: Fall back to draw them out of formation, then turn on them. Needs horse or a practised commander; fails badly if they don't bite.

reserves.name: Commit reserves
reserves.text: Throw in the reserve and the horse at once. Once per battle; the men tire after.

battlefield._doc: Battles fought on the hex's own inner map (player/battlefield.js, ui/innerMapBattle.js): companies of figures, real-time with pause. Every power and loss reuses fieldBattle's numbers (the phases' lossBase, the stances, rout.lossMult, ambushPower); these keys tune the field itself. Built-in defaults; keys here override them. 'looks' are the LPC layer recipes the figures are composited from ({skin} {hair} {shirt} {legs} {paint} {plume} filled per figure).
battlefield._balance: Tuned so the field fought out by both sides' captains gives the phased battle's odds (src/__tests__/battlefieldBalance.test.js): horse are worth a little less on the field (power), bowmen who close fight as hard as their counter over pikes says (melee, archerMeleeCounter), an army mostly of bowmen joins the press (ai.archerJoin within ai.archerJoinShare), each side's luck of the day (fieldLuck).

looks._doc: Layer recipes per look (paths under assets/lpc/Characters). A company's look: its unit type's recipe when there is one ('militia', 'knight'), else '<kind>', and '<kind>_rabble' for bandits, raiders and pirates. Liveries: the player's from 'player', a realm's from 'realms' (picked by the realm's id), the rest from 'rabble'. Gear: a recipe's weapon, shield, helm and armour lines are what an enemy company shows; your own companies' lines are swapped for the arms each man was issued (systems/arms.js lookLayers; data/arms.json sprite).
looks._spacing: How far apart the men are DRAWN (tiles between files, across the facing, and between ranks, along it), per kind. The battle itself keeps kinds.along / kinds.across (its frontages, reaches and odds are tuned on them); ui/innerMapBattle.js _at opens each formation out to these on screen so a man is not hidden behind the man in front of him.

encounters._doc: Hostile encounters on the road (player/roadEncounters.js): flee, pay toll / throw food, parley / drive off with fire, hide, or stand and fight. Odds shown before you choose.
encounters._graceDays: After any encounter on the road, no band waylays you again (nor sets off after you) for this many days.
encounters._pursuit: A band in sight of you (world/units.js updateRaider) sets off after you with this chance a day: alone, against an army it outmatches 3 to 1, against one at least half its match (evenly), else otherwise; a light purse (under poorGold coin and poorGoods goods) is chased poorMult as often.

ironborn.name: Ironborn
ironborn.ancestralMemory: The Ironborn remember the First Forge, deep in the Ashpeak mountains, where their ancestors tamed fire and steel.

crownlanders.name: Crownlanders
crownlanders.proverb: "A crown is earned at the table, not the battlefield."
crownlanders.ancestralMemory: The Crownlanders trace their line to the River Council, where seven chieftains broke bread and swore the First Compact.

shieldfolk.name: Shieldfolk
shieldfolk.ancestralMemory: The Shieldfolk were born from the Wardens who stood against the Shadow Tide, holding the passes when all seemed lost.

mosswalkers.name: Mosswalkers
mosswalkers.proverb: "The forest speaks to those who learn to be still."
mosswalkers.ancestralMemory: The Mosswalkers believe they were the first to hear the Heartwood sing — the deep vibration of the oldest tree in creation.

canopiers.name: Canopiers
canopiers.proverb: "Those who fear falling never learn to fly."
canopiers.ancestralMemory: The Canopiers say their first mother climbed the World-Tree and never came down, building the first sky-village among its branches.

rootkeepers.name: Rootkeepers
rootkeepers.proverb: "Every oak was once an acorn with the courage to grow."
rootkeepers.ancestralMemory: The Rootkeepers guard the Seed Vaults — ancient caches of every plant that ever lived, hidden in root caverns.

windrunners.name: Windrunners
windrunners.proverb: "A Windrunner tied down is a Windrunner already dead."
windrunners.ancestralMemory: They say the first Windrunner caught the tail of a cyclone and rode it across the steppe, mapping every horizon.

sandshapers.name: Sandshapers
sandshapers.proverb: "The desert gives nothing freely — and teaches everything."
sandshapers.ancestralMemory: The Sandshapers remember the Year of Glass, when lightning struck the great dunes and their ancestors forged the first desert-glass mirrors.

bonecarvers.name: Bonecarvers
bonecarvers.proverb: "Honor the beast, and its spirit will run with you forever."
bonecarvers.ancestralMemory: The Bonecarvers carry the Great Tusk — a mammoth bone inscribed with the names of every tribe elder for a thousand years.

sunweavers.name: Sunweavers
sunweavers.proverb: "Every dawn is proof that darkness cannot last."
sunweavers.ancestralMemory: The Sunweavers tell of a time when the sun died for three days, and their ancestor wove a cloth of pure light to call it back.

ashpilgrims.name: Ashpilgrims
ashpilgrims.ancestralMemory: The Ashpilgrims were born when a volcano buried their village. The survivors walked through the ash for forty days and emerged enlightened.

starcallers.name: Starcallers
starcallers.proverb: "We are all stardust, remembering where we came from."
starcallers.ancestralMemory: The Starcallers claim their founder once climbed a tower so high she touched the stars and brought back a fragment of cosmic truth.

tidecallers.name: Tidecallers
tidecallers.proverb: "The tide waits for no one, but rewards those who know its rhythm."
tidecallers.ancestralMemory: The Tidecallers built the first sea-wall — a living barrier of coral and stone that protected their village from the Great Tsunami.

deepdivers.name: Deepdivers
deepdivers.proverb: "The greatest treasures are found where others fear to go."
deepdivers.ancestralMemory: The Deepdivers discovered the Sunken City — an ancient civilization beneath the waves — and traded its secrets for generations.

sailweavers.name: Sailweavers
sailweavers.proverb: "A good ship and a fair wind — what more could the heart desire?"
sailweavers.ancestralMemory: The Sailweavers built the Eternal Fleet — ships so masterfully crafted that some still sail, crewed by the descendants of their original builders.

lorekeepers.name: Lorekeepers
lorekeepers.proverb: "A people without records are a people without roots."
lorekeepers.ancestralMemory: The Lorekeepers descend from the Archivists of the Sunken Library, who saved ten thousand scrolls from the Great Flood by carrying them on their backs across the mountains.

thornwardens.name: Thornwardens
thornwardens.proverb: "Beauty and pain grow from the same stem."
thornwardens.ancestralMemory: The Thornwardens grew the Great Briar Wall — a living barrier of thorns a hundred feet high — that held back an invading army for a generation.

frostborn.name: Frostborn
frostborn.proverb: "The cold does not care. And neither shall we."
frostborn.ancestralMemory: The Frostborn survived the Long Winter — seven years of endless snow — by building cities inside glaciers and learning to farm the frost itself.

icewalkers.name: Icewalkers
icewalkers.proverb: "Walk softly on the ice, for the world is thin beneath us."
icewalkers.ancestralMemory: The Icewalkers once followed a white elk across a frozen ocean for forty days, discovering a hidden land of hot springs where they built their sacred winter refuge.

aurorans.name: Aurorans
aurorans.proverb: "The lights above are the dreams of the earth."
aurorans.ancestralMemory: The Aurorans believe their ancestors once spoke with the aurora itself, learning the language of light, and that each color carries a different truth.

deepdelvers.name: Deepdelvers
deepdelvers.proverb: "Dig deep enough and you will find the bones of the world."
deepdelvers.ancestralMemory: The Deepdelvers carved the Underhall — a cathedral-sized cavern deep beneath the mountains — where every surface glitters with embedded gems left by ancient rivers.

glowkin.name: Glowkin
glowkin.proverb: "In the deepest dark, we became our own light."
glowkin.ancestralMemory: The Glowkin were once surface dwellers who fled a great catastrophe underground, and over generations learned to cultivate the living lights of the deep caves.

crystalsmiths.name: Crystalsmiths
crystalsmiths.proverb: "Perfection is not achieved — it is revealed, facet by facet."
crystalsmiths.ancestralMemory: The Crystalsmiths discovered the Singing Cavern — a place where crystals of impossible size hum in perfect harmony, said to be the heartbeat of the world itself.

runespeakers.name: Runespeakers
runespeakers.proverb: "Every word carved in stone outlasts the hand that carved it."
runespeakers.ancestralMemory: The Runespeakers claim their founder discovered the First Rune — a symbol of such power it split a mountain in two — and swore to guard it and all runes that followed.

veilwalkers.name: Veilwalkers
veilwalkers.proverb: "The veil is thin for those with eyes to see."
veilwalkers.ancestralMemory: The Veilwalkers arose at a place where the world is thin — a misty bog where the living and the dead can speak. They serve as intermediaries between realms.

dreamweavers.name: Dreamweavers
dreamweavers.proverb: "What we dream tonight, the world becomes tomorrow."
dreamweavers.ancestralMemory: The Dreamweavers learned to weave shared dreams — a single night where an entire tribe dreams together — and from those visions, they built their first city.

skyherders.name: Skyherders
skyherders.proverb: "From the heights, all borders are illusions."
skyherders.ancestralMemory: The Skyherders followed the great eagles to the roof of the world, where they discovered hidden valleys above the clouds and built the Sky Roads — mountain paths only they can navigate.

reefbuilders.name: Reefbuilders
reefbuilders.proverb: "Build with the sea, not against it, and your walls will outlast stone."
reefbuilders.ancestralMemory: The Reefbuilders grew an entire island from living coral over seven generations — a testament to patience and cooperation that stands to this day.

embersmiths.name: Embersmiths
embersmiths.proverb: "We do not fear the fire — we are the fire."
embersmiths.ancestralMemory: The Embersmiths were born when a volcano's heart cracked open and their ancestors dared to reach inside, pulling out the first Everflame — a fire that has never gone out.

marshborn.name: Marshborn
marshborn.proverb: "The swamp swallows the proud and shelters the humble."
marshborn.ancestralMemory: The Marshborn fled into the deepest bogs when invaders came, and the swamp hid them so well that their enemies believed them vanished. They have never left.

evolutionStages.name: Nomadic Band
evolutionStages.description: Small kinship groups wandering the land

evolutionStages.name: Tribal Camp
evolutionStages.description: Seasonal camps where tribes gather for trade and marriage

evolutionStages.name: Chiefdom
evolutionStages.description: A powerful chief unites several bands under one rule

evolutionStages.name: Village
evolutionStages.description: Settled communities with shared governance and craft specialization

evolutionStages.name: Town
evolutionStages.description: A thriving hub where multiple peoples have intermingled for generations

evolutionStages.name: City
evolutionStages.description: A great city where diverse subcultures form distinct quarters and guilds

evolutionStages.name: Metropolis
evolutionStages.description: A cosmopolitan center where cultures fuse into something new

FESTIVAL.name: Joint Festival
FESTIVAL.description: Celebrating together builds bonds across cultural lines

SHARED_DEFENSE.name: Shared Defense
SHARED_DEFENSE.description: Standing together against a common threat forges deep unity

RIVALRY.name: Cultural Rivalry
RIVALRY.description: Old grudges and competing traditions cause friction

CUISINE_FUSION.name: Cuisine Fusion
CUISINE_FUSION.description: Blending culinary traditions creates beloved new dishes

ART_EXCHANGE.name: Artistic Exchange
ART_EXCHANGE.description: Artists from different traditions inspire each other

KNOWLEDGE_SHARING.name: Knowledge Sharing
KNOWLEDGE_SHARING.description: Scholars and elders exchange ancient wisdom across cultural lines

BLOOD_FEUD.name: Blood Feud
BLOOD_FEUD.description: An ancient wrong festers into open hostility between peoples

MIGRATION.name: Migration
MIGRATION.description: A displaced people arrives, straining local resources and trust

SHARED_HARVEST.name: Shared Harvest
SHARED_HARVEST.description: Working the land together forges bonds of mutual dependence

LANGUAGE_BLEND.name: Language Blending
LANGUAGE_BLEND.description: Pidgin tongues and shared phrases emerge from daily contact

MYSTICAL_CONVERGENCE.name: Mystical Convergence
MYSTICAL_CONVERGENCE.description: A shared supernatural experience unites peoples in awe

effects._doc: What a settlement's peoples DO. Each group's values, traits, art forms and diaspora status add (share x weight) to an aspect; aspect score x scale is the effect, clamped to +/-max. Read by src/systems/peoples/effects.js.

trade.label: Commerce
trade.describe: trade-route profit (half that on your market prices here)

stability.label: Order
stability.describe: mood if you rule it, and the realm's stability

martial.label: Martial
martial.describe: recruits available (half that off recruit cost); realm military

festive.label: Revelry
festive.describe: festivals held here (+1 renown at 4% or more)

FARM.name: Farm
FARM.description: Produces grain that can be milled or sold. Upkeep: 6g/day

MINE.name: Mine
MINE.description: Extracts valuable resources for sale (iron, gold, gems, stone or coal). Upkeep: 15g/day

WORKSHOP.name: Workshop
WORKSHOP.description: Processes raw materials into goods. Upkeep: 10g/day

FISHING_WHARF.name: Fishing Wharf
FISHING_WHARF.description: Send boats to collect fish from nearby waters. Upkeep: 10g/day

BREWERY.name: Brewery
BREWERY.description: Brews beer from grain or distills liquor. Sells well at taverns. Upkeep: 8g/day

TAVERN.name: Tavern
TAVERN.description: A place for drink, gambling, and gossip. Earns gold daily from patrons. Upkeep: 8g/day

GUEST_HOUSE.name: Guest House
GUEST_HOUSE.description: A bed & breakfast: a few rooms and breakfast included. Guests from the town's travellers, shared with its other houses by stars, price and reputation. Hire staff and set prices from its panel. Upkeep: 3g/day

INN.name: Inn
INN.description: A coaching inn: a common room and private rooms, suppers, baths and stabling. Competes with the town's other houses for its travellers. Upkeep: 6g/day

HOTEL.name: Grand Hotel
HOTEL.description: Suites, fine dining, a bathhouse and a valet for the wealthy few. Only a city or capital has the custom. Upkeep: 14g/day

ROADHOUSE.name: Roadhouse
ROADHOUSE.description: A wayside house on an open road between towns: bunks, cheap rooms and a stable yard. Its guests are the road's traffic. Upkeep: 2g/day

GRAIN_MILL.name: Mill
GRAIN_MILL.description: Grinds grain into flour. Built on a river, its water wheel adds +50% output. Build it beside your farm and it mills the harvest automatically. Upkeep: 6g/day

BAKERY.name: Bakery
BAKERY.description: Bakes bread from flour. Requires flour supply. Upkeep: 8g/day

FORGE.name: Forge
FORGE.description: A dedicated smithy. Forges tools or weapons from iron, or casts bronze ware from copper. Upkeep: 12g/day

TANNERY.name: Tannery
TANNERY.description: Tans animal hides into leather, leather armor or parchment. Upkeep: 8g/day

SAWMILL.name: Sawmill
SAWMILL.description: Processes timber into firewood and lumber. Upkeep: 7g/day

QUARRY.name: Quarry
QUARRY.description: Cuts stone blocks from rocky outcrops. Essential for construction. Upkeep: 8g/day

SALT_PANS.name: Salt Pans
SALT_PANS.description: Evaporates seawater to harvest salt. A vital food preservative. Upkeep: 6g/day

APIARY.name: Apiary
APIARY.description: Keeps beehives for honey. Used in mead and candle-making. Upkeep: 6g/day

ORCHARD.name: Orchard
ORCHARD.description: Cultivates fruit trees for winemaking or fresh trade. Upkeep: 6g/day

HEMP_FARM.name: Hemp Farm
HEMP_FARM.description: Grows hemp fiber for rope-making. Vital for ships and construction. Upkeep: 5g/day

CLAY_PIT.name: Clay Pit
CLAY_PIT.description: Digs raw clay from riverbeds. Used for pottery. Upkeep: 4g/day

DAIRY.name: Dairy
DAIRY.description: Raises dairy cattle to produce aged cheese. Popular with traders. Upkeep: 6g/day

SMOKEHOUSE.name: Smokehouse
SMOKEHOUSE.description: Smokes fish and cures meat for long-term preservation. Upkeep: 6g/day

BUTCHER.name: Butcher
BUTCHER.description: Processes hunted game and livestock into dried provisions. Upkeep: 5g/day

ROPE_WALK.name: Rope Walk
ROPE_WALK.description: Twists hemp fiber into rope. Vital for ships and construction. Upkeep: 5g/day

POTTERY_KILN.name: Pottery Kiln
POTTERY_KILN.description: Fires clay pots and vessels for households and traders. Upkeep: 5g/day

WEAVER.name: Weaver
WEAVER.description: Weaves wool into cloth and sews fine garments. Upkeep: 6g/day

WINERY.name: Winery
WINERY.description: Ferments fruit into wine and honey into mead. Premium beverages. Upkeep: 8g/day

APOTHECARY.name: Apothecary
APOTHECARY.description: Prepares herbal remedies and alchemical potions. Upkeep: 8g/day

FLETCHER.name: Fletcher
FLETCHER.description: Crafts arrows and bows for hunters and archers. Upkeep: 6g/day

JEWELER.name: Jeweler
JEWELER.description: Cuts gems and crafts fine jewelry for nobility. Upkeep: 10g/day

DYE_WORKS.name: Dye Works
DYE_WORKS.description: Extracts natural dyes from berries and plants. Upkeep: 6g/day

CHANDLERY.name: Chandlery
CHANDLERY.description: Renders beeswax into candles. An essential light source. Upkeep: 5g/day

GLASSWORKS.name: Glassworks
GLASSWORKS.description: Melts stone into glass and blows glass into lanterns. Upkeep: 10g/day

SCRIPTORIUM.name: Scriptorium
SCRIPTORIUM.description: Monks and scribes prepare parchment and copy rare texts. Upkeep: 8g/day

BLACKSMITH.name: Blacksmith
BLACKSMITH.description: Versatile smithy producing shields, tools, and weapons. Upkeep: 10g/day

PERFUMERY.name: Perfumery
PERFUMERY.description: Distils flowers and resins into perfumes and incense. Upkeep: 8g/day

HUNTING_LODGE.name: Hunting Lodge
HUNTING_LODGE.description: Hunters bring back hides for tanneries and scriptoriums. Upkeep: 5g/day

CATTLE_RANCH.name: Cattle Ranch
CATTLE_RANCH.description: Raises cattle for meat. Pair with a Smokehouse or Butcher for dried provisions. Built on or beside a cattle herd it yields 30% more. Upkeep: 6g/day

HERB_GARDEN.name: Herb Garden
HERB_GARDEN.description: Grows medicinal and aromatic herbs for apothecaries and perfumeries. Upkeep: 4g/day

HORSE_RANCH.name: Horse Ranch
HORSE_RANCH.description: Breeds horses — slow to raise but prized by every army and merchant. Upkeep: 12g/day

PITCH_WORKS.name: Pitch Works
PITCH_WORKS.description: Skims rock oil from a desert seep. Sell it, or refine it into lamp oil at a Chandlery. Upkeep: 8g/day

FORAGER_HUT.name: Forager's Hut
FORAGER_HUT.description: Gathers wild berries and mushrooms. Supplies Dye Works. Upkeep: 3g/day

GRAIN.name: Grain
GRAIN.description: Threshed wheat, barley or rye: what the farmers carry to the granary. Ground into flour, brewed into beer, or eaten as pottage in a lean year.

FLOUR.name: Flour
FLOUR.description: Grain ground at the mill. The baker turns it into bread; it keeps longer than the loaf.

BREAD.name: Bread
BREAD.description: Baked loaves, the staple of every table. Filling and cheap, but it goes stale within days.

FISH.name: Raw Fish
FISH.description: Fresh-caught fish. Eat it soon, grill it, or smoke it to make it keep.

PRESERVED_FISH.name: Smoked Fish
PRESERVED_FISH.description: Fish smoked or salted to keep for months: ships' stores, soldiers' rations and Lenten fare.

WOOD.name: Wood
WOOD.description: Felled timber. Burnt, sawn into planks, or worked by joiners, wheelwrights and shipwrights.

FIREWOOD.name: Firewood
FIREWOOD.description: Split logs for hearths and ovens. Every household burns it, most of all in winter.

WOOL.name: Wool
WOOL.description: Shorn fleece, washed and carded. Spun and woven into cloth, or felted into cloaks.

TEXTILES.name: Textiles
TEXTILES.description: Bolts of woven cloth, the tailor's stock. Most of the realm's clothes start here.

FLAX.name: Flax
FLAX.description: Retted and scutched flax from the fields, ready for the spinning wheel.

LINEN.name: Linen
LINEN.description: Linen cloth: shirts, shifts, sheets and altar cloths. Woven in town shops, or spun and woven in cottages for a merchant's piece rate.

CLOTHES.name: Clothes
CLOTHES.description: Plain made garments: tunics, hose and hoods. Clean clothes keep you presentable.

STONE.name: Stone
STONE.description: Quarried and dressed stone for walls, towers, bridges and the finer houses.

IRON.name: Iron
IRON.description: Bar iron from the bloomery. The smith's raw stuff for tools, nails and blades.

TOOLS.name: Tools
TOOLS.description: Axes, saws, hammers and ploughshares. Workshops and farms use them up and need more.

WEAPONS.name: Weapons
WEAPONS.description: Munition swords, axes and spearheads from the armourer, by the dozen. Armies and town watches buy them in war, and every recruit wants one.

GOLD_ORE.name: Gold Ore
GOLD_ORE.description: Gold-bearing rock from the mines, to be smelted into bars.

COPPER.name: Copper
COPPER.description: Smelted copper from the hill mines. The founders cast it into bronze; tinkers and coppersmiths use the rest.

BRONZE.name: Bronze Ware
BRONZE.description: Pots, bells, lamps, buckles and ship's fittings, cast from the copper of these hills (its own arsenic hardens it: no tin needed).

IRON_INGOT.name: Iron Ingot
IRON_INGOT.description: Refined iron cast in ingots, cleaner than bar iron: wanted for good steel and fine work.

GOLD_BAR.name: Gold Bar
GOLD_BAR.description: Smelted gold. Mints strike it into coin; goldsmiths make it into jewellery.

SILVER_ORE.name: Silver Ore
SILVER_ORE.description: Argentiferous ore from the hill mines. Silversmiths work a little of it; the realms' mints buy the rest and strike it into coin.

GEMS.name: Gems
GEMS.description: Cut and uncut stones: rubies, garnets, amethysts. Small, light and very valuable.

IVORY.name: Ivory
IVORY.description: Tusk ivory from distant lands, carved into combs, caskets and chess pieces for the rich.

SPICES.name: Spices
SPICES.description: Pepper, cumin and cinnamon from the trade routes. A little goes a long way in a lord's kitchen.

HORSES.name: Horses
HORSES.description: A string of horses for sale or trade: farm horses, pack animals and remounts.

BEER.name: Beer
BEER.description: Ale brewed from grain. Safer than water, and drunk by everyone, morning to night.

LIQUOR.name: Liquor
LIQUOR.description: Distilled spirits. Strong, costly, and quick to start a brawl.

LUXURIES.name: Luxuries
LUXURIES.description: Fine goods for great households: glass, silver plate, carpets and the like.

SMALL_FISH.name: Small Fry
SMALL_FISH.description: Small fry from the shallows. Cheap food, or bait for bigger catches.

LARGE_FISH.name: Large Cod
LARGE_FISH.description: A big cod, enough for a family supper. Sells well fresh, better smoked.

CRAB.name: Crab
CRAB.description: A live crab from the rocks. Boiled, it fetches a fair price at a coastal market.

SWORDFISH.name: Swordfish
SWORDFISH.description: A deep-water fighter, hard to land and prized at any fishmonger's.

LOBSTER.name: Lobster
LOBSTER.description: A lobster from the pots, a delicacy on noble tables.

GOLDEN_FISH.name: Golden Fish
GOLDEN_FISH.description: A rare golden fish. Collectors and lords pay far more than its weight in silver.

BOOT.name: Old Boot
BOOT.description: An old boot pulled from the water. Worth nothing, but it proves you were fishing.

SEAWEED.name: Seaweed
SEAWEED.description: Wrack from the shore: spread on fields as manure, burnt for potash, or eaten in a hard winter.

MUSSELS.name: Mussels
MUSSELS.description: Blue-black mussels prised off the rocks and the river bed. Steamed, a cheap and filling supper.

OYSTERS.name: Oysters
OYSTERS.description: Oysters brought up from the sea floor. Eaten raw at a lord's table, and now and then one holds a pearl.

CRAYFISH.name: Crayfish
CRAYFISH.description: Freshwater crayfish caught by hand under the stones of a river or lake. Boiled, they make a fair meal.

SEA_SPONGE.name: Sea Sponge
SEA_SPONGE.description: A soft sponge cut from the deep rocks. Bathhouses, physicians and scribes pay for it.

ORE.name: Iron Ore
ORE.description: Iron-bearing rock from the mines. Smelted in a bloomery with coal or charcoal it gives bar iron.

HERBS.name: Herbs
HERBS.description: Gathered wild herbs for physicians, apothecaries and the cooking pot.

PELTS.name: Pelts
PELTS.description: Furs from the hunt: fox, beaver, marten. Furriers make them into trims and coats.

BERRIES.name: Berries
BERRIES.description: Wild berries picked from the hedgerows. A handful staves off hunger; they spoil fast.

MUSHROOMS.name: Mushrooms
MUSHROOMS.description: Forest mushrooms. Good eating, if whoever picked them knew which ones.

MEAT.name: Meat
MEAT.description: Fresh meat from the hunt or the butcher. Cook it, or dry it before it turns.

HIDE.name: Hide
HIDE.description: A raw animal skin. The tannery turns it into leather.

LEATHER.name: Leather
LEATHER.description: Tanned hide. Townsfolk wear it out as boots, belts and harness; tanneries make it from hides.

ANTLER.name: Antler
ANTLER.description: Shed or taken antler, carved into handles, combs and buttons.

FEATHER.name: Feather
FEATHER.description: Flight feathers, for fletching arrows and for quills.

HORSE.name: Horse
HORSE.description: A riding horse: faster travel on the world map, and more room in your packs.

AGRI_PARTS.name: Agricultural Implements
AGRI_PARTS.description: Ploughs, harrows and mill gear. Raise the yield of farms that use them.

INDUSTRY_PARTS.name: Industrial Components
INDUSTRY_PARTS.description: Bellows, gears and fittings for forges, mills and workshops.

MILITARY_PARTS.name: Military Supplies
MILITARY_PARTS.description: Arms, harness and camp gear for raising and keeping troops.

INFRA_PARTS.name: Engineering Plans
INFRA_PARTS.description: Surveys and engineers' drawings for roads, bridges and public works.

COMMERCE_PARTS.name: Trade Documents
COMMERCE_PARTS.description: Contracts, bills and charters: the paperwork trade houses run on.

EXOTIC_SPICES.name: Exotic Spices
EXOTIC_SPICES.description: Saffron, cloves and nutmeg from the far edge of the trade routes. Worth their weight in silver.

SILK.name: Silk Cloth
SILK.description: Silk cloth from distant looms. Only the rich wear it.

PERFUME.name: Perfume
PERFUME.description: Scents in small glass vials, a gift that wins favour at court.

TEA.name: Tea Leaves
TEA.description: Dried tea leaves, a costly import that a few great houses have taken to.

WINE.name: Fine Wine
WINE.description: Good wine in casks, served at feasts and given as gifts between lords.

CHEESE.name: Aged Cheese
CHEESE.description: Aged hard cheese. Keeps for months and travels well.

MILK.name: Milk
MILK.description: Fresh milk from your cows and goats. Drink it, or sell it in town before it turns.

EGGS.name: Eggs
EGGS.description: Eggs from your hens and ducks. Cheap, filling, and every kitchen wants them.

DRIED_MEAT.name: Dried Meat
DRIED_MEAT.description: Salted and dried meat. Light and lasting: soldiers' and travellers' food.

HONEY.name: Honey
HONEY.description: Honey from the hives: sweetener, preserver, and the makings of mead.

SALT.name: Salt
SALT.description: Salt from pans or mines. Without it no meat or fish keeps through the winter.

ROPE.name: Rope
ROPE.description: Hemp rope for ships, wells, cranes and farms.

CANDLES.name: Candles
CANDLES.description: Tallow candles for light after dark. Beeswax ones go to churches and the rich.

POTTERY.name: Pottery
POTTERY.description: Fired pots, jugs and bowls for every kitchen and storeroom.

LEATHER_ARMOR.name: Leather Armour
LEATHER_ARMOR.description: A boiled-leather jerkin. Light, quiet and cheap; it turns a glancing blow.

SHIELD.name: Round Shield
SHIELD.description: Glued boards faced with rawhide, an iron boss over the grip: the common soldier's shield.

BOW.name: Bow
BOW.description: A hunting or war bow of yew or ash. Useless without arrows.

ARROWS.name: Arrows
ARROWS.description: Fletched arrows, sold by the each: every shot at game uses one, and a hunter gets some back.

BOLTS.name: Crossbow Bolts
BOLTS.description: Short, heavy iron-headed bolts for the crossbow, sold by the each. Crossbowmen spend them in every battle; a crossbow hunter uses them on game.

FISHING_SPEAR.name: Fishing Spear
FISHING_SPEAR.description: A light barbed spear for taking fish underwater. It wears with use.

SINEW.name: Sinew
SINEW.description: Dried tendon from a butchered beast: twisted into bowstrings and lashings.

CURED_FURS.name: Cured Furs
CURED_FURS.description: Fleshed, salted and stretched pelts, ready for the furrier.

BEAR_RUG.name: Bear-skin Rug
BEAR_RUG.description: A cured bear's pelt, head and all, to lie before a lord's hearth.

LEATHER_GOODS.name: Leather Goods
LEATHER_GOODS.description: Belts, pouches, purses and straps: every traveller wants one.

CARVINGS.name: Carvings
CARVINGS.description: Whittled spoons, bowls, toys and antler combs.

IVORY_CARVING.name: Ivory Carving
IVORY_CARVING.description: A figure or casket panel carved in ivory, for the luxury trade.

QUILLS.name: Quills
QUILLS.description: Cut and hardened feather pens. Scribes, clerks and monasteries buy them.

HEALING_SALVE.name: Healing Salve
HEALING_SALVE.description: An ointment of herbs and fat that cleans and closes wounds.

POTION.name: Strange Potion
POTION.description: A murky brew from a hedge-witch. Nobody quite knows what it does.

ELIXIR.name: Elixir of Vigor
ELIXIR.description: An apothecary's tonic that restores strength and wards off fatigue.

ANTIDOTE.name: Antidote
ANTIDOTE.description: A remedy against poisons and the bites of venomous beasts.

TREASURE_MAP.name: Treasure Map
TREASURE_MAP.description: A weathered map marking something buried. It may be real.

ANCIENT_COIN.name: Ancient Coin
ANCIENT_COIN.description: A coin from a fallen empire. Collectors and scholars pay well for it.

RARE_BOOK.name: Rare Book
RARE_BOOK.description: A precious manuscript. Scholars, monasteries and libraries want it.

COMPASS.name: Compass
COMPASS.description: A lodestone needle in a brass case. Sailors and explorers swear by it.

LANTERN.name: Lantern
LANTERN.description: A horn-paned lantern that lights the road at night and keeps the flame out of the wind.

AMULET.name: Amulet
AMULET.description: A charm said to ward off ill luck. Some believe in it more than others.

ENCHANTED_RING.name: Enchanted Ring
ENCHANTED_RING.description: A ring with a strange glimmer. Its owner swears it brings fortune.

DYES.name: Dyes
DYES.description: Woad, madder and weld: the colours that make cloth worth more.

INCENSE.name: Incense
INCENSE.description: Fragrant resins burnt in temples and in the chambers of the wealthy.

HEMP.name: Hemp Fiber
HEMP.description: Hemp fibre, twisted into rope and woven into sacking and sailcloth.

CLAY.name: Raw Clay
CLAY.description: Dug clay for the potter's wheel and the brick kiln.

FRUIT.name: Fresh Fruit
FRUIT.description: Apples, pears and plums fresh from the orchard. Eat them, or press them for cider.

VEGETABLES.name: Vegetables
VEGETABLES.description: Cabbages, turnips and carrots from a kitchen garden. Plain fare that fills a pot.

WHEAT_SEED.name: Seed Wheat
WHEAT_SEED.description: A measure of seed corn: sow it on tilled ground in spring or summer (data/crops.json).

CABBAGE_SEED.name: Cabbage Seed
CABBAGE_SEED.description: Sow on tilled ground from spring to autumn. Hardy: cabbages stand the winter frost.

TURNIP_SEED.name: Turnip Seed
TURNIP_SEED.description: Quick to come up. Sow on tilled ground in spring or autumn; hardy through the frosts.

CARROT_SEED.name: Carrot Seed
CARROT_SEED.description: Sow on tilled ground in spring or summer.

FLAX_SEED.name: Linseed
FLAX_SEED.description: Flax seed for the spring sowing. The crop is pulled for the spinners.

HEMP_SEED.name: Hemp Seed
HEMP_SEED.description: Sow on tilled ground in spring or summer; it grows tall and wants little water.

HERB_SEED.name: Herb Seed
HERB_SEED.description: Seed for a herb bed. Sow in spring or summer.

STRAWBERRY_SEED.name: Strawberry Runners
STRAWBERRY_SEED.description: Runners for a strawberry bed. Sow in spring or summer and keep them well watered.

GLASS.name: Glass
GLASS.description: Blown and cast glass for windows, bottles and lamps.

MEAD.name: Mead
MEAD.description: Honey wine, sweet and strong, an old drink of the halls.

PARCHMENT.name: Parchment
PARCHMENT.description: Scraped and stretched skin to write on: letters, charters and books.

FOOD.name: Army Rations
FOOD.description: Hardtack and salt pork seized from soldiers. Eaten on the road like any other food.

COAL.name: Coal
COAL.description: Mined from coal seams. Smiths and smelters burn it: forges near coal work faster, and a furnace makes ingots from less iron with it.

OIL.name: Rock Oil
OIL.description: Black oil from desert seeps. A prized trade good; chandlers refine it into lamp oil.

LAMP_OIL.name: Lamp Oil
LAMP_OIL.description: Refined oil for lamps and lanterns.

RUM.name: Rum
RUM.description: Pirate rum. A swig puts spring back in your step (+1 movement today).

HOLY_WATER.name: Holy Water
HOLY_WATER.description: Blessed water carried by pilgrims. Drink it to mend small wounds (+10 health).

RELICS.name: Holy Relics
RELICS.description: Bones and tokens of saints. A pious lord treasures them; a House that enshrines them gains standing.

SCRIPTURES.name: Scriptures
SCRIPTURES.description: Illuminated holy texts. A modest courtly gift.

POISON.name: Poison
POISON.description: Smuggled poison. Fences pay well and ask nothing.

FORGED_DOCUMENTS.name: Forged Documents
FORGED_DOCUMENTS.description: Passable letters of introduction. Carrying them helps a little at the negotiating table (+2%).

RARE_HERBS.name: Rare Herbs
RARE_HERBS.description: Exotic herbs. An apothecary brews them into an Elixir of Vigor.

ANCIENT_ARTIFACT.name: Ancient Artifact
ANCIENT_ARTIFACT.description: A relic of a lost age from a creature's hoard. Lords covet it; enshrined in your hall it brings your House prestige.

ENCHANTED_WEAPON.name: Enchanted Weapon
ENCHANTED_WEAPON.description: A rune-etched blade from a legendary hoard. Carried at the head of your army it adds 5% battle power.

DRAGON_SCALE.name: Dragon Scale
DRAGON_SCALE.description: A plate of scale harder than steel. Carried as a buckler it turns 10% of the harm you take; a blacksmith can work three into dragonscale armour.

DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.name: Dragonscale Armour
DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.description: Armour of dragon scale. Turns 25% of the harm you take, and kings would trade a province for it.

ROYAL_SEAL.name: Royal Seal
ROYAL_SEAL.description: A sovereign's signet. Carrying it lends you authority in negotiation (+5%); returned to a lord it earns real gratitude.

TREATY.name: Sealed Treaty
TREATY.description: Signed terms between courts. Useful leverage at the table (+3% negotiation), or a gift a lord will value.

GIFT_CHEST.name: Gift Chest
GIFT_CHEST.description: A chest of courtly presents meant for a lord. Present it at a royal audience.

FINE_WINE.name: Fine Wine
FINE_WINE.description: A vintage fit for a royal table. A small courtly gift.

CURSED_IDOL.name: Cursed Idol
CURSED_IDOL.description: A grinning idol carried up out of a delve. While you carry it the curse saps a little health and karma each day and dogs your luck below ground. Sell it or be rid of it some other way.

RESIN.name: Pine Resin
RESIN.description: Sticky resin tapped from pines: incense, ink and pitch.

TALLOW.name: Tallow
TALLOW.description: Rendered animal fat, for candles and soap.

PLANKS.name: Sawn Planks
PLANKS.description: Timber sawn to boards: the joiner's and cooper's stock.

STEEL.name: Steel
STEEL.description: Iron worked with charcoal into hard steel: the best blades, tools and plate.

SILVER_BAR.name: Silver Bar
SILVER_BAR.description: Refined silver, cast for the silversmith.

INK.name: Ink
INK.description: Soot and resin ground into a black ink.

JOINERY.name: Joinery
JOINERY.description: Stools, chests and tables: a joiner's honest work.

BARREL.name: Barrel
BARREL.description: An iron-hooped oak barrel, wanted by every brewer and fishmonger.

CHAINMAIL.name: Mail Hauberk
CHAINMAIL.description: A knee-length shirt of riveted iron rings over a padded coat. Turns a cut; a mace or a point still bruises through.

PLATE_ARMOR.name: Plate Harness
PLATE_ARMOR.description: Fitted steel plate from head to foot: a knight's harness. Heavy, and worth it.

HELMET.name: Iron Helm
HELMET.description: A conical iron helm with a nasal.

STEEL_SWORD.name: Steel Longsword
STEEL_SWORD.description: A long tempered steel blade, better balanced than any munition sword: the knight's sword.

SPEAR.name: Iron Spear
SPEAR.description: An ash shaft and an iron head: the commoner's weapon.

CROSSBOW.name: Crossbow
CROSSBOW.description: A stocked bow with an iron lath and a cranked string.

STEEL_TOOLS.name: Steel Tools
STEEL_TOOLS.description: Steel-edged chisels, saws and hammers: a craftsman works faster and finer with them.

SADDLE.name: Saddle
SADDLE.description: A leather riding saddle with iron fittings.

WOOL_CLOAK.name: Wool Cloak
WOOL_CLOAK.description: A heavy woollen cloak against the wind and rain.

FUR_COAT.name: Fur Coat
FUR_COAT.description: Pelts sewn over wool: proof against a northern winter.

FINE_GARMENTS.name: Fine Garments
FINE_GARMENTS.description: Dyed silk and linen cut for the court.

MEAT_PIE.name: Meat Pie
MEAT_PIE.description: Pastry and meat: a meal you can carry.

SAUSAGE.name: Sausage
SAUSAGE.description: Salted meat in a skin: keeps for weeks.

JAM.name: Fruit Preserve
JAM.description: Fruit boiled down with honey and sealed in a crock.

PICKLES.name: Pickled Vegetables
PICKLES.description: Vegetables put up in brine for the winter.

SOAP.name: Soap
SOAP.description: Tallow and wood-ash lye. Washing with it gets you and your clothes cleaner.

GOLD_JEWELLERY.name: Gold Jewellery
GOLD_JEWELLERY.description: Gold set with gems: jewellery for a lord.

POULTICE.name: Poultice
POULTICE.description: Herbs bound in linen against a wound.

TONIC.name: Herbal Tonic
TONIC.description: Herbs steeped in honeyed wine: heals and revives.

BOOK.name: Bound Book
BOOK.description: Parchment leaves, inked and bound in leather.

TIN.name: Tin
TIN.description: Tin from the stream-works and the far mines: a quarter part of it turns soft copper into hard bronze.

BRONZE_BAR.name: Bronze Bar
BRONZE_BAR.description: Copper and tin cast in bars: the bronzesmith's stuff for blades, axes and spearheads.

HAFT.name: Ash Haft
HAFT.description: A straight ash shaft for a spear, an axe, a mace or a polearm.

GRIP.name: Hilt & Grip
GRIP.description: A leather-bound grip with guard and pommel, ready to take a blade.

SHIELD_BOSS.name: Shield Boss
SHIELD_BOSS.description: A domed iron boss that covers a shield's grip.

WHETSTONE.name: Whetstone
WHETSTONE.description: A fine-grained stone for keeping an edge on a blade. It cracks in time.

RONDEL_DAGGER.name: Steel Rondel Dagger
RONDEL_DAGGER.description: A stiff steel spike between two discs: it finds the gaps in mail and plate.

BRONZE_SWORD.name: Bronze Leaf Sword
BRONZE_SWORD.description: A cast bronze leaf blade: old-fashioned, and it bends.

IRON_SWORD.name: Iron Arming Sword
IRON_SWORD.description: A one-handed iron sword for sword and shield.

STEEL_ARMING_SWORD.name: Steel Arming Sword
STEEL_ARMING_SWORD.description: A steel-edged one-handed sword, quick and keen.

BRONZE_AXE.name: Bronze Axe
BRONZE_AXE.description: A cast bronze axe head on an ash haft.

IRON_AXE.name: Bearded War Axe
IRON_AXE.description: A light bearded axe: it hooks shields and bites through mail rings.

DANE_AXE.name: Steel Dane Axe
DANE_AXE.description: A broad axe on a five-foot haft: two hands, terrible blows.

IRON_MACE.name: Iron Mace
IRON_MACE.description: A heavy iron mace: it crushes through mail.

FLANGED_MACE.name: Steel Flanged Mace
FLANGED_MACE.description: A flanged steel mace made for beating plate.

BRONZE_SPEAR.name: Bronze Spear
BRONZE_SPEAR.description: A bronze spearhead on an ash haft.

PIKE.name: Pike
PIKE.description: A long shaft with a small iron head: two hands, and a wall of them stops horse.

IRON_BILL.name: Bill
IRON_BILL.description: A hooked blade, spike and back-hook on a long haft: the yeoman's polearm.

HALBERD.name: Steel Halberd
HALBERD.description: Axe, spike and hook in one steel head on a long haft.

BUCKLER.name: Buckler
BUCKLER.description: A small iron fist-shield: quick to parry and riposte, little cover.

HEATER_SHIELD.name: Heater Shield
HEATER_SHIELD.description: A leather-faced, iron-rimmed shield in the knightly shape.

KITE_SHIELD.name: Kite Shield
KITE_SHIELD.description: A long shield from shoulder to shin.

PAVISE.name: Pavise
PAVISE.description: A tall standing shield to reload behind.

STEEL_HELM.name: Steel Bascinet
STEEL_HELM.description: A close steel helm with a padded lining.

GAMBESON.name: Gambeson
GAMBESON.description: A quilted coat of cloth and wool: the poor man's armour, and worn under mail.

BRIGANDINE.name: Brigandine
BRIGANDINE.description: Steel plates riveted inside a cloth coat.

LINEN.name: Weave Linen
LINEN.description: Spin flax and weave it into linen.

CAST_BRONZE.name: Cast Bronze
CAST_BRONZE.description: Melt copper (its own arsenic hardens it) and cast pots, bells and fittings.

BEER.name: Brew Beer
BEER.description: Brew ale from grain. Popular at taverns.

LIQUOR.name: Distill Liquor
LIQUOR.description: Distill strong spirits from grain. High value.

LEATHER_ARMOR.name: Tan Leather Armor
LEATHER_ARMOR.description: Cure hides into protective leather armor.

DRIED_MEAT.name: Cure Dried Meat
DRIED_MEAT.description: Cure raw meat into dried provisions.

POTTERY.name: Fire Pottery
POTTERY.description: Fire clay into pots and vessels.

TAN_LEATHER.name: Tan Leather
TAN_LEATHER.description: Cure hides into leather for the town's cobblers and saddlers.

SHIELD.name: Forge Shield
SHIELD.description: Hammer iron into a sturdy shield.

ARROWS.name: Fletch Arrows
ARROWS.description: Whittle and tip arrows for archers.

BOW.name: Craft Bow
BOW.description: Bend a yew stave into a longbow.

HEALING_SALVE.name: Brew Healing Salve
HEALING_SALVE.description: Infuse herbs into a medicinal salve.

POTION.name: Brew Potion
POTION.description: Brew mushrooms into a mysterious potion.

IRON_INGOT.name: Smelt Iron Ingots
IRON_INGOT.description: Smelt iron into ingots. Coal nearby fires the furnace hotter.

DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.name: Forge Dragonscale Armour
DRAGONSCALE_ARMOR.description: Rivet dragon scales into a suit of armour.

LAMP_OIL.name: Refine Lamp Oil
LAMP_OIL.description: Refine rock oil into clean-burning lamp oil.

ELIXIR.name: Brew Elixir of Vigor
ELIXIR.description: Brew rare herbs into a restorative elixir.

MERCHANT_APPRENTICE.title: Merchant Apprentice
MERCHANT_APPRENTICE.description: Prove yourself as a trader by accumulating wealth.

TRADE_EMPIRE.title: Trade Empire
TRADE_EMPIRE.description: Build a network of profitable properties.

MERCENARY_CAPTAIN.title: Mercenary Captain
MERCENARY_CAPTAIN.description: Complete mercenary contracts to build your reputation.

PROPHET.title: Prophet
PROPHET.description: Found your own religion and spread the faith.

TEMPLE_BUILDER.title: Temple Builder
TEMPLE_BUILDER.description: Construct religious buildings to spread your faith.

A_NEW_BEGINNING.title: A New Beginning
A_NEW_BEGINNING.description: Explore nearby lands, discover settlements, and grow your influence.

WANDERER.title: Wanderer
WANDERER.description: Explore the world and discover new lands.

MARKET_MANIPULATOR.title: Market Manipulator
MARKET_MANIPULATOR.description: Buy low and sell high — dominate the trade markets.

SILK_ROAD.title: The Silk Road
SILK_ROAD.description: Establish long-distance trade routes across the realm.

BANDIT_SLAYER.title: Bandit Slayer
BANDIT_SLAYER.description: Clear the roads of bandits and raiders.

HOLY_CRUSADER.title: Holy Crusader
HOLY_CRUSADER.description: Spread your faith through righteous combat.

MIRACLE_WORKER_QUEST.title: Miracle Worker
MIRACLE_WORKER_QUEST.description: Perform divine miracles to prove your devotion.

PILGRIMAGE.title: The Great Pilgrimage
PILGRIMAGE.description: Visit every holy site in the realm.

HERESY_HUNTER.title: Heresy Hunter
HERESY_HUNTER.description: Root out heretical movements threatening the faith.

TREASURE_HUNTER.title: Treasure Hunter
TREASURE_HUNTER.description: Find hidden treasures scattered across the realm.

MOUNTAIN_CLIMBER.title: Mountain Climber
MOUNTAIN_CLIMBER.description: Traverse the highest mountain peaks in the realm.

DIPLOMAT.title: Diplomat
DIPLOMAT.description: Establish diplomatic relations with multiple kingdoms.

KINGMAKER.title: Kingmaker
KINGMAKER.description: Become so influential you can sway the fate of kingdoms.

SPY_NETWORK.title: Spy Network
SPY_NETWORK.description: Build an intelligence network throughout the realm.

TAVERN_REGULAR.title: Tavern Regular
TAVERN_REGULAR.description: Become a well-known figure in the taverns of the realm.

SCHOLAR.title: Scholar
SCHOLAR.description: Research new technologies to advance your domain.

DRAGON_HUNTER.title: Dragon Hunter
DRAGON_HUNTER.description: Track and slay the legendary beasts terrorizing the land.

PEOPLES_CHAMPION.title: People's Champion
PEOPLES_CHAMPION.description: Help the common folk with their problems.

DIVINE_MANDATE.title: Divine Mandate
DIVINE_MANDATE.description: Become the supreme religious authority in the realm.

PHYSICIANS_HERBS.title: A Physician's Herbs
PHYSICIANS_HERBS.description: The town physician has run out of herbs for poultices and fever draughts. Gather them in the wild and bring them to her.

objectives.text: Bring 6 herbs to the physician of {target}

FURS_FOR_WINTER.title: Furs for the Winter
FURS_FOR_WINTER.description: The furrier's racks are bare and the cold months are coming. Hunt the wilds and bring back pelts.

objectives.text: Bring 4 pelts to the furrier of {target}

TOMB_OF_THE_OLD_KINGS.title: Tomb of the Old Kings
TOMB_OF_THE_OLD_KINGS.description: A scholar will pay for an account of a buried tomb, taken all the way down to the burial chamber.

fallback.text: Clear a Buried Tomb delve to the bottom

THE_DEEP_SEAM.title: The Deep Seam
THE_DEEP_SEAM.description: The miners' guild wants to know whether an abandoned mine can be worked again. Go to the bottom and come back.

fallback.text: Clear an Abandoned Mine delve to the bottom

THE_BLIND_DARK.title: The Blind Dark
THE_BLIND_DARK.description: Herders swear something lives at the bottom of the caves above the valley. Find out.

objectives.text: Find what lives at the bottom of {target}

fallback.text: Clear a Deep Cave delve to the bottom

THE_DROWNED_HALLS.title: The Drowned Halls
THE_DROWNED_HALLS.description: Sunken ruins hold the treasures of a city the sea took. Few who go down reach the last hall.

fallback.text: Clear a Sunken Ruins delve to the bottom

BREAD_FOR_THE_BESIEGED.title: Bread for the Besieged
BREAD_FOR_THE_BESIEGED.description: A town is shut in by a besieging host and its stores are running low. Get provisions through the lines.

objectives.text: Get supplies into a besieged holding, or fulfil a siege-relief contract

CONVOY_ESCORT.title: Escort the Convoys
CONVOY_ESCORT.description: Bandits and pirates prey on the trade roads. See your company's convoys safely to their posts and contract towns.

COMPANY_CONTRACTS.title: A Name for Reliability
COMPANY_CONTRACTS.description: The great houses trust a company that delivers. Fulfil supply contracts in full.

THE_RUMOURED_ISLE.title: The Rumoured Isle
THE_RUMOURED_ISLE.description: Sailors in the taverns talk of an island no chart shows. Hear the rumour (or buy a chart) and find the place.

objectives.text: Discover a land a rumour or a chart spoke of

NAME_THE_NEW_LAND.title: Name the New Land
NAME_THE_NEW_LAND.description: The royal cartographers will pay for a land no one has charted, and for the right to print its name.

A_SEASONED_CREW.title: A Seasoned Crew
A_SEASONED_CREW.description: A green crew becomes a good one only at sea. Make real voyages, port to port.

RUN_THE_BLOCKADE.title: Run the Blockade
RUN_THE_BLOCKADE.description: An enemy fleet has closed a realm's harbours and its towns pay anything for goods. Smuggle a cargo past the patrols and sell it on the black market.

objectives.text: Sell goods on the black market in a blockaded realm

SLAY_THE_SAGA_BEAST.title: Slay the Beast of the Saga
SLAY_THE_SAGA_BEAST.description: A creature out of the old songs walks the land and a realm has put a price on its head. Hunt it down.

SATISFACTION_DEMANDED.title: Satisfaction Demanded
SATISFACTION_DEMANDED.description: A rival adventurer has been boasting in every tavern that you are a coward. Answer with steel.

objectives.text: Win a duel against a rival adventurer

THE_MERCIFUL_HAND.title: The Merciful Hand
THE_MERCIFUL_HAND.description: The priests say a lord is measured by the mercy shown to those who kneel. Rule with mercy when petitioners come.

THE_IRON_LAW.title: The Iron Law
THE_IRON_LAW.description: Your stewards complain that the folk think your law is soft. Show them its weight from the bench.

SCALES_OF_JUSTICE.title: Scales of Justice
SCALES_OF_JUSTICE.description: A travelling jurist wants to see whether your court weighs a case fairly. Give a just ruling.

objectives.text: Rule on a petition with justice

WALLS_AND_WORKS.title: Walls and Works
WALLS_AND_WORKS.description: A holding that does not grow falls behind. Raise new works in your settlements.

RAIDERS_AT_THE_GATE.title: Raiders at the Gate
RAIDERS_AT_THE_GATE.description: Bandits have been probing the edges of your lands. Make sure the next raid breaks on your walls.

objectives.text: Repel a raid on one of your holdings

TAKE_THE_TOWN.title: Take the Town
TAKE_THE_TOWN.description: A walled town will not open its gates to anything but a siege. Invest it, starve or storm it, and take it.

NO_RELIEF_FOR_THEM.title: No Relief for Them
NO_RELIEF_FOR_THEM.description: The besieged are waiting for their king's army. Meet it in the field before it reaches the walls.

objectives.text: Beat a relief army marching on your siege

BY_ROYAL_DECREE.title: By Royal Decree
BY_ROYAL_DECREE.description: A new reign is judged by its first laws. Put an edict before your council and see it passed.

THE_KINGMAKERS_WAGER.title: The Kingmaker's Wager
THE_KINGMAKERS_WAGER.description: A throne stands empty and the claimants are gathering. Back the one who will win it.

objectives.text: Back the winning claimant in a succession crisis

HONOUR_AMONG_THIEVES.title: Honour Among Thieves
HONOUR_AMONG_THIEVES.description: The Guild's contact wants to see what you can do before trusting you with more.

objectives.text: Commit 3 crimes (jobs, black-market deals, fencing, theft)

A_FRIEND_INDEED.title: A Friend Indeed
A_FRIEND_INDEED.description: Those who travel with you follow for pay. Earn one companion's devotion.

courtingStages.label: Strangers
courtingStages.description: You don't know each other yet.

chat.label: Have a Chat
chat.description: Strike up a conversation. Low reward, always available.

compliment.label: Give a Compliment
compliment.description: Offer a sincere compliment. Charisma helps.

gift.label: Give a Gift
gift.description: Buy a thoughtful gift. Costs gold.

moonlight_walk.label: Moonlight Walk
moonlight_walk.description: Take a quiet walk together to deepen connection.

romantic_dinner.label: Romantic Dinner
romantic_dinner.description: Invite them to a lavish dinner. Requires a settlement.

private_vows.label: Exchange Private Vows
private_vows.description: Pledge devotion in private before the wedding.

propose.label: Propose Marriage
propose.description: Ask for their hand in marriage. Must be deeply in love.

quality_time.label: Spend Quality Time
quality_time.description: Invest in your marriage and keep affection strong.

befriend.label: Be Friendly
befriend.description: Make small talk and build rapport.

share_meal.label: Share a Meal
share_meal.description: Break bread together. Costs a little gold.

tell_stories.label: Tell Stories
tell_stories.description: Share tales and listen to theirs.

train_together.label: Train Together
train_together.description: Spar or drill with this person. Builds respect.

confide_secret.label: Confide a Secret
confide_secret.description: Trust them with a private truth. Great reward if it lands.

blood_oath.label: Swear Blood Oath
blood_oath.description: Bind your loyalty in solemn ritual. Powerful, but risky.

challenge.label: Challenge to Duel
challenge.description: Challenge them to a friendly (or not) duel.

giftItems.name: Gold Ring
giftItems.description: A gleaming ring of fine gold.

giftItems.name: Fine Blade
giftItems.description: A well-forged weapon. Martial types appreciate this.

giftItems.name: Rare Book
giftItems.description: A book of knowledge or poetry.

npcCourtEvents.text: {npc} gives you a warm smile and says something flattering.
{npc} surprises you with a small gift — a {item}.
{npc} seems jealous of someone you were talking to.
{npc} confides a personal story to you. You feel closer.
{npc} says something cutting about you in front of others.

marriageEvents.text: Your spouse {spouse} celebrates your anniversary with a special meal. 💕
{spouse} has fallen ill. You tend to them with care.
Your child {child} took their first steps today!

matters._comment: Matters of the heart and of friendship (systems/relationships/matters.js): the people the player knows bring them things — a loan, a confidence, a plea, a rival suitor, a question about a rumour, a jealous spouse, a grudge. One open matter per person, settled face to face (Meet People / the person's scene) before it expires. Tokens: {npc} {amount} {due} {reason} {suitor} {kin} {rumor} {subject} {other} {place}.

config._loyalty: loyaltyHonesty: a debtor's chance to repay rises by (loyalty - 50) x this. trustBonus: once you admit a crime to someone ('heard_crime: admit'), your later deny / lie rolls with them gain this (lost if they catch you lying). coldDays: an ignored grudge closes the door to courting for this long; an ignored rival suitor marries the one you courted. slanderDiscredit: share of a slander's credibility lost when a friend believes your denial.

loan.title: A Loan
reasons: The roof came in over the winter
My brother's debts came to my door
The guild fine was more than I had
A sick cow, then a dead one
ask: *twists their hands* I hate to ask. I need {amount} gold. {reason}. I'll pay you back, I swear it.
Can I ask you something, as a friend? {amount} gold. {reason}. You'd have it back with something on top.
loan.notice: {npc} has something to ask you, quietly. Find them in {place}.
loan.expire: {npc} stopped waiting for your answer about the loan.

debt.title: The Debt
ask: *can't meet your eyes* The {amount} gold. I don't have it. Not yet. I'm sorry.
About the money... it's gone, and I've nothing to show for it. I'm ashamed.
debt.notice: {npc} can't repay the {amount} gold you lent. They're in {place}.
debt.expire: You never pressed {npc} over the debt. They take it as forgiveness.

confidence.title: A Confidence
ask: *glances at the door* Can I trust you with something? About {subject}. That talk going round... it's {truth}. I know someone who'd know.
You'll keep this between us. The tale about {subject}? It's {truth}. My cousin serves at court.
sorrow: *quietly* My father's dying. I've told no one else. I don't know why I'm telling you.
I'm thinking of leaving {place}. For good. Nobody here knows yet.
confidence.notice: {npc} wants to tell you something, in private. They're in {place}.
confidence.expire: Whatever {npc} meant to tell you, they've kept it to themselves.

plea.title: A Plea
trouble: is in the reeve's gaol for a debt
has the fever and the physician wants paying first
was taken up by the press gang
owes the moneylender, and he's sent his men
ask: *eyes red* {kin} {reason}. {amount} gold would save them. I've nowhere else to turn.
plea.notice: {npc} is desperate and asking for you in {place}.
plea.expire: {npc} needed you, and you didn't come. They won't forget it.

rival_suitor.title: A Rival Suitor
ask: *a little flushed* {suitor} has been calling on me. With flowers. I haven't said no. Should I?
You should know: {suitor} has asked my father for me. I told him I'd think about it.
rival_suitor.notice: Someone else is courting {npc}. You'll find them in {place}.
rival_suitor.expire: {npc} is promised to {suitor}. You waited too long.

heard_crime.title: What They Heard
ask: *arms folded* They're saying things about you in {place}. "{rumor}" Is it true?
I heard something. "{rumor}" Tell me it's a lie.
heard_crime.notice: Talk about you has reached {npc} in {place}. They want to hear it from you.
heard_crime.expire: {npc} heard the rumours and never heard your side of it.

jealousy.title: Jealousy
ask: *cold* Who is {other}? Don't look at me like that. Who is {other}?
I've heard about you and {other}. The whole town has. Well?
askNoName: *cold* You've been distant. Is there someone else?
jealousy.notice: {npc}, your spouse, needs to speak with you. It doesn't sound good.
jealousy.expire: You avoided {npc}'s question. The silence between you grows.

grudge.title: A Grudge
ask: *sneers* Come to hear what I've been saying about you? Everyone else has.
Oh, it's you. I've been telling {place} all about you. Every word true.
grudge.notice: {npc} has been badmouthing you all over {place}.
grudge.expire: {npc}'s grudge settles into something cold and permanent.

solaris.name: The Solar Covenant
solaris.description: Worship of the Eternal Sun — the oldest surviving faith. Temples face east, and adherents mark holy days at dawn.

tidemother.name: Faith of the Tidemother
tidemother.description: Seafarers' faith centred on the Tidemother — goddess of currents, storms, and safe harbour.

earthroot.name: The Earthroot Communion
earthroot.description: Nature worship venerating the world-tree whose roots bind all living things. Shrines stand in forest glades.

ironfaith.name: The Iron Creed
ironfaith.description: Born among mountain clans, the Iron Creed teaches that the soul is forged through trial and labour.

starseers.name: Order of the Starseers
starseers.description: Mystic scholar-monks who chart the heavens and claim to read fate in the constellations.

stoneheart.name: The Stoneheart Pact
stoneheart.description: Mountain-dwellers who believe the gods sleep inside stone and that every carved hall is a prayer.

serpentway.name: The Serpent's Way
serpentway.description: Swamp mystics who worship the Great Serpent — symbol of death, rebirth, and the cycle of decay and renewal.

arcanum.name: The Arcane Orthodoxy
arcanum.description: Less a religion than a philosophical order — practitioners believe magic itself is divine and study is worship.

stormfather.name: Cult of the Stormfather
stormfather.description: Northern raiders worship the Stormfather — god of thunder, war, and the open sea. Sacrifices are made before raids.

dunewalkers.name: The Dunewalker Creed
dunewalkers.description: Desert faith teaching that the gods test mortals with heat and thirst. Water-sharing is the holiest act.

dreamweavers.name: The Dreamweaver Circle
dreamweavers.description: Practitioners enter dream-trances to commune with spirits. They believe waking life is the lesser reality.

ashwalkers.name: The Ashwalker Path
ashwalkers.description: Fire-worshippers who practised ritual immolation. Suppressed after the Great Pyre Rebellion of 230.

voidcallers.name: The Cult of the Void
voidcallers.description: An esoteric cult that worshipped the emptiness between stars. Banned after the Mindbreak Plague of 400.

bonesingers.name: The Bonesinger Rites
bonesingers.description: Ancestor-worship tradition where the dead were preserved and "sang" through wind-harps atop burial spires. Faded after prolonged plague.

flameheralds.name: Heralds of the Eternal Flame
flameheralds.description: A militant offshoot of the Solar Covenant. Launched three crusades before collapsing into internal schism.

bloodmoon.name: The Blood Moon Covenant
bloodmoon.description: Blood-sacrifice cult that performed rituals under the red moon. Eradicated by a combined crusade of the Solar Covenant and Iron Creed.

silentorder.name: The Silent Order
silentorder.description: Monks who took vows of eternal silence, believing all speech corrupted divine truth. Died out when no new followers could be recruited.

Peace.summary: +10% reputation gains; faithful realms warm to you 50% faster

Charity.desc: Give to the poor and needy
Charity.summary: +20% conversion and +0.5 karma a day, but -25% tithes

Justice.desc: Uphold law and punish the wicked
Justice.summary: Each devoted town steadies its realm (+1 stability, up to +3)

Humility.summary: -10% army upkeep and +0.3 karma a day

Sovereignty.desc: Divine right of the faithful to rule
Sovereignty.summary: +5% negotiation with lords; faithful realms warm to you twice as fast

Mysticism.desc: Seek the hidden mysteries of the cosmos

preaching._doc: Sermons for the player's faith (PlayerReligion.preach): one a day; each town tires of the preacher (saturation, recovering by the day); faith runs weak where the state church is lax; a rival state clergy may fine, denounce and finally ban the preacher from the realm.

offerings._doc: Faith income is real coin. The player's followers give out of the purses of the towns they live in, by the faithful there (presence share x people; the follower count past the towns' faithful gives nothing: PlayerReligion.collectFaithIncome); a hospice's pilgrims pay out of the towns around it (applyBuildingYields); a sermon's alms come from the town preached in; a realm's holy-site pilgrims (Religion.processTurn) and its temples' offerings (KingdomAI.updateInstitutions) come out of its own towns, by people. Each town gives its share, at most this share of the coin it holds that day, so a poor town gives less and none is emptied.

holySiteTypes.name: World-Tree Sapling
holySiteTypes.description: A sapling of the legendary world-tree

holySiteTypes.name: Grand Reliquary

holySiteTypes.name: Dragon Bone Shrine

holySiteTypes.description: Half-submerged ruins of an ancient temple to forgotten gods

PILGRIM_HOSPICE.name: Pilgrim Hospice

ships._shipcraft: What shipwrights must know to build (ship type `requires`: technology ids, data/technology.json). A shipyard builds what its realm's shipwrights know, plus anything the player has researched (they can teach them). Realms of an ordinary start know the era's whole craft; a realm born at the Dawn of Man (world/dawn.js) starts knowing nothing and learns `order` one technique at a time: the first `firstAfterYears` after its founding, then one every `learnEveryYears` (world/shipcraft.js). Independent towns of a dawn world know only what the player brings.

shipTypes.name: Sloop

shipTypes.name: Caravel

shipTypes.name: War Galley

shipTypes.name: Galleon

explorationEvents.name: Floating Cargo
explorationEvents.description: You discover drifting crates from a shipwreck.

explorationEvents.name: Uncharted Island
explorationEvents.description: You spot a small island not on any charts. Landing reveals hidden treasures.

explorationEvents.name: Whale Sighting
explorationEvents.description: A magnificent whale breaches near your ship. The crew takes it as a good omen.

explorationEvents.name: Sea Monster!
explorationEvents.description: A tentacled beast rises from the deep and attacks your ship!

explorationEvents.name: Stranded Sailors
explorationEvents.description: You find shipwrecked sailors clinging to debris. Rescue them for karma and information.

explorationEvents.name: Merchant Wreck
explorationEvents.description: The remains of a merchant vessel with salvageable goods.

explorationEvents.name: Calm Seas
explorationEvents.description: Beautiful weather and smooth sailing. Your crew's morale improves.

explorationEvents.name: Sudden Storm
explorationEvents.description: A fierce storm batters your ship. Hold fast!

explorationEvents.name: Pirate Ambush!
explorationEvents.description: Pirates emerge from behind a rocky outcrop!

explorationEvents.name: Dolphins
explorationEvents.description: A pod of dolphins escorts your ship. Sailors say it means good luck.

voyageEvents.title: Becalmed
voyageEvents.text: The wind dies. The sails hang slack and the sea turns to glass.

choices.label: Wait for the wind
choices.text: You lie becalmed for a day while the water casks run low.

choices.label: Man the sweeps
choices.text: The crew rows you through the doldrums, cursing every stroke.

pass.text: A breeze answers before the tune is done. The hands grin.

fail.text: No wind comes, and the old hands mutter that you have angered the sea.

choices.label: Set the idle hands fishing over the side
choices.text: Lines over every rail. The day is lost, but the mess is full.

voyageEvents.title: Sail Ho!
voyageEvents.text: A sail on the horizon, hull-down and closing on your course.

pass.text: A merchantman. Her master trades news of the sea lanes and a cask of fresh water.

fail.text: Pirates! They run out their guns as you come alongside.

win.text: You beat them off and take their purse.

lose.text: They board you, take what they like and leave you wallowing.

pass.text: You show her your stern and lose her by nightfall.

fail.text: She is faster. Pirates, and they mean to have you.

win.text: Cornered, your crew fights like devils and drives them off.

lose.text: They take a share of the hold and leave you limping.

choices.label: Run her down (piracy)
choices.text: You hoist no colours and give chase.

win.text: You plunder her hold and set her crew adrift in the boats.

lose.text: Her crew fights back hard, and you sheer off with a holed hull.

voyageEvents.title: A Derelict
voyageEvents.text: A derelict drifts across your bows: masts snapped, sails rotting, not a soul on deck.

pass.text: Her strongroom is intact. You carry off her strongbox and a few bales.

fail.text: Something foul lingered in her hold. The flux breaks out among your men.

choices.label: Strip her timbers
choices.text: Your carpenter strips good oak and spars to patch your own hull.

choices.label: Give her a wide berth
choices.text: The crew crosses themselves as she drifts astern.

voyageEvents.title: Coils in the Swell
voyageEvents.text: The lookout swears he saw great coils rise and sink off the bow. The crew talks of nothing else.

choices.label: Hunt the beast
choices.text: You beat to quarters and go looking for it.

win.text: A sea serpent, and you have slain it. Its teeth will hang in every tavern you drink in.

lose.text: It was real. It stove in your planking and took a man before it sounded.

choices.label: Steer wide of those waters
choices.text: You lose a day going around, and the crew breathes easier.

pass.text: You call it a log and a bellyful of rum, and the crew laughs with you.

fail.text: Nobody laughs. The night watch refuses to go aloft.

voyageEvents.title: Man Overboard!
voyageEvents.text: A sailor goes over the side in a squall. You can see his head in the wake.

pass.text: You haul him aboard half-drowned. The crew will not forget it.

fail.text: You search until dark, but the sea has him.

choices.label: Go over the side after him yourself

pass.text: You hit the water, get an arm round him, and the hands haul you both up on a line. They will follow you anywhere now.

fail.text: The cold takes your breath. They drag you back aboard alone, coughing seawater; the sea has him.

choices.label: Hold your course
choices.text: You will not risk the ship for one man. The crew watches him fall astern.

voyageEvents.title: St Elmo's Fire
voyageEvents.text: Blue fire crawls along the yards and crackles at the masthead in the dark.

choices.label: Proclaim it a blessing
choices.text: You tell them the saint walks with the ship. They believe you.

choices.label: Lead the crew in prayer
choices.text: The whole ship's company kneels on the wet deck until the fire fades.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: The hands whisper about drowned men's lanterns.

voyageEvents.title: A Convoy Asks for Escort
voyageEvents.text: A convoy of fat merchantmen signals you: pirates work these waters, and they will pay for an escort.

choices.label: Escort them
choices.text: You shepherd the convoy along a day's detour.

pass.text: The pirates never show. The merchants pay all the same.

fail.text: Two pirate sloops fall on the convoy at dawn.

win.text: You drive them off. The grateful merchants pay handsomely.

lose.text: The convoy scatters and you take a mauling covering it.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: You wish them luck and hold your course.

choices.label: Demand protection money
choices.text: They pay, and they will tell every harbourmaster what you did.

voyageEvents.title: A Castaway
voyageEvents.text: A castaway clings to a spar, waving weakly at your sails.

choices.label: Take him aboard
choices.text: Fed and dried, he signs on as a hand.

choices.label: Sail past
choices.text: You have no food to spare. The crew does not meet your eye.

voyageEvents.title: Smugglers' Lugger
voyageEvents.text: A lugger running without lights comes alongside. Cheap wine, she says, and no questions.

choices.label: Buy her wine (120g)
choices.text: Six casks swing into your hold. Somebody's excise man is the poorer.

choices.label: Take her name for the harbourmaster
choices.text: You note her name and course for the next harbourmaster.

choices.label: Send her on her way
choices.text: She melts back into the dark.

voyageEvents.title: A Great Shoal
voyageEvents.text: The sea boils silver: a shoal of herring as far as the eye can see.

choices.label: Cast the nets
choices.text: Fresh fish for every mess and more salted down for the voyage.

choices.label: Press on
choices.text: You do not stop.

voyageEvents.title: Fog Bank
voyageEvents.text: A fog bank swallows the ship. From the helm you cannot see the bowsprit.

pass.text: Leadsman calling every minute, you come out the far side unscathed.
