fail.text: A grinding shudder: you have scraped a reef.

choices.label: Take the lead-line at the bow yourself

pass.text: You call the soundings yourself, fathom by fathom, and bring her out into clear air. The hands look at you differently.

fail.text: You call 'no bottom' a breath too late: she touches, shudders, and slides off.

choices.label: Heave to until it lifts
choices.text: You lie to for a day, bells ringing in the murk.

voyageEvents.title: Grumbling Below Decks
voyageEvents.text: The hands are muttering: short commons, hard usage, and a captain who doesn't care.

choices.label: Promise a bonus (3g a hand)
choices.text: Coin talks. The muttering stops.

choices.label: Break out extra rations
choices.text: A double ration and a tot all round.

pass.text: The lash restores order, for now.

fail.text: The crew turns sullen. Two hands slip away in the jolly boat that night.

choices.label: Go forward and hear them out yourself (charisma)

pass.text: You sit with them on the forecastle and hear every complaint. The worst of it blows over.

fail.text: They hear you out in silence, and go back to muttering when you go aft.

choices.label: Let them grumble
choices.text: It festers.

voyageEvents.title: A Message in a Bottle
voyageEvents.text: A sealed bottle bobs alongside, its cork waxed and stamped.

choices.label: Fish it out and read it

pass.text: A drowned merchant's last words, and the mark of a cache ashore. You find it on the way.

fail.text: A love letter, sadly lettered. The crew reads it aloud at supper, much moved.

choices.label: Leave it to the sea
choices.text: Some messages are not for you.

voyageEvents.title: Whales Off the Bow
voyageEvents.text: A pod of whales rolls alongside, blowing, close enough to smell their breath.

choices.label: Let the hands watch them go by
choices.text: The whole crew lines the rail. Nobody says much, and everybody is smiling.

choices.label: Lower a boat and go after one

pass.text: A long, bloody day, but you tow a whale alongside and try her out: meat and oil for the voyage.

fail.text: The whale sounds, then comes up under the boat. You get the men back, and not much else.

crew._doc: Sailors are hired at ports and paid daily. A ship below its crewRequired sails slower, fights worse and nets fewer fish; below minCrewShare it cannot leave port. Morale rests at restingMorale; storms, defeats and missed wages lower it, victories raise it, and sailors desert when it falls below desertionMorale.

portPrices._doc: Port prices as multiples of the good's land base price (data/playerEconomy.json GOODS, moved by the season), so sea goods share the land economy's scale. Exporters sell cheap and pay exportResale of their own price; local markets sit around base with a spread; importers pay a premium and sell none. A port whose own town market stocks the good never imports it.

provisions._doc: Ships away from port feed their crew from the hold: one unit of any listed food feeds sailorsPerRation sailors for a day. A ship's chandler at a port sells the provision item at chandlerMarkup over the town's food price (never below minPrice). A crew with nothing to eat loses hungerMoraleLoss morale a day; after scurvyAfterHungryDays hungry days scurvy breaks out aboard, and a broken crew deserts.

voyage._doc: Voyages to a port take real days: each day the ship sails getSailingSpeed hexes along a sea route (half in a storm), and the normal day passes. eventChance is the daily chance of an at-sea event (voyageEvents); logLength caps the voyage log.

farm.description: A dedicated space for agricultural experiments and crop research.

workshop.description: An advanced facility for engineering, metallurgy, and military research.

trading_post.description: A school of commerce, economics, and trade strategy.

harbor.description: A dedicated facility for naval engineering and seamanship research.

library.description: A great hall of study for cultural and educational advancement.

apothecary.description: A facility for researching herbal remedies, surgery, and disease prevention.

CROP_ROTATION.name: Crop Rotation
CROP_ROTATION.description: Rotating crops across fields restores soil nutrients and improves yields.
CROP_ROTATION.flavorText: The land gives more when you give it time to breathe.

IRRIGATION.name: Irrigation Systems
IRRIGATION.description: Channel water to fields for consistent irrigation.

SELECTIVE_BREEDING.name: Selective Breeding
SELECTIVE_BREEDING.description: Breed stronger livestock for better wool and meat.
SELECTIVE_BREEDING.flavorText: Nature perfected through patience and observation.

FERTILIZATION.name: Advanced Fertilization
FERTILIZATION.description: Use composting and manure techniques to dramatically boost farm output.
FERTILIZATION.flavorText: From waste, abundance. The circle of the field is complete.

GRANARY_CONSTRUCTION.name: Granary Construction
GRANARY_CONSTRUCTION.description: Build granaries to store surplus grain and prevent spoilage.
GRANARY_CONSTRUCTION.flavorText: Seven years of plenty shall sustain seven years of famine.

IMPROVED_TOOLS.name: Improved Tools
IMPROVED_TOOLS.description: Better-forged tools increase mining and logging efficiency.
IMPROVED_TOOLS.flavorText: A sharp axe makes light work.

ADVANCED_SMELTING.name: Advanced Smelting
ADVANCED_SMELTING.flavorText: In the heart of the forge, impurities burn away.

WATER_MILL.name: Water Mill
WATER_MILL.description: Harness water power to automate milling and sawing.
WATER_MILL.flavorText: The river works tirelessly so we don't have to.

STONECUTTING.name: Stonecutting
STONECUTTING.description: Cut and shape stone for stronger construction.
STONECUTTING.flavorText: From rough rock, we carve the foundations of empire.

STEEL_FORGING.name: Steel Forging
STEEL_FORGING.description: Forge weapons and armor of superior steel.
STEEL_FORGING.flavorText: Steel that sings when drawn — a craftsman's pride.

BASIC_TRAINING.name: Basic Training
BASIC_TRAINING.description: Organized militia training for better combat performance.
BASIC_TRAINING.flavorText: Even farmers fight better when they know which end of the sword to hold.

ARCHERY_MASTERY.name: Archery Mastery
ARCHERY_MASTERY.description: Advanced bow techniques for deadlier ranged attacks.
ARCHERY_MASTERY.flavorText: Their arrows blot out the sun.

CAVALRY_TACTICS.name: Cavalry Tactics
CAVALRY_TACTICS.description: Mounted combat formations and flanking maneuvers.
CAVALRY_TACTICS.flavorText: A thundering charge to break any shield wall.

SIEGE_ENGINEERING.name: Siege Engineering
SIEGE_ENGINEERING.description: Build siege engines to assault fortified positions.
SIEGE_ENGINEERING.flavorText: No wall can stand against the relentless pounding.

FORTIFICATION.name: Fortification
FORTIFICATION.description: Build defensive walls and watchtowers for your settlements.
FORTIFICATION.flavorText: These walls shall be our unyielding shield.

ROAD_BUILDING.name: Road Building
ROAD_BUILDING.description: Surveyors and road gangs: anyone can clear a dirt path, but proper roads, stone paving and bridges start here.
ROAD_BUILDING.flavorText: All great journeys begin with a well-trodden path.

PAVED_ROADS.name: Paved Roads
PAVED_ROADS.description: Stone-paved roads for even faster travel.
PAVED_ROADS.flavorText: Rome endured because its roads did.

BRIDGE_CONSTRUCTION.name: Bridge Construction
BRIDGE_CONSTRUCTION.description: Build bridges to cross rivers and reduce swamp penalties.
BRIDGE_CONSTRUCTION.flavorText: Where rivers once stopped us, bridges carry us onward.

CARTOGRAPHY.name: Cartography
CARTOGRAPHY.description: Map the land to reveal more territory and plan better routes.
CARTOGRAPHY.flavorText: With knowledge of the land comes mastery over it.

AQUEDUCTS.name: Aqueducts
AQUEDUCTS.description: Monumental water channels that boost settlement growth.
AQUEDUCTS.flavorText: Water flows uphill when engineers will it so.

BASIC_ACCOUNTING.name: Basic Accounting
BASIC_ACCOUNTING.description: Better bookkeeping means lower trade losses.
BASIC_ACCOUNTING.flavorText: A lord who knows his ledger commands more than gold.

TRADE_NETWORKS.name: Trade Networks
TRADE_NETWORKS.description: Establish trade routes for higher caravan profits.
TRADE_NETWORKS.flavorText: Connections forged in gold last longer than those in iron.

CURRENCY_MINTING.name: Currency Minting
CURRENCY_MINTING.description: Mint your own coins for more favorable trade terms.
CURRENCY_MINTING.flavorText: A coin with your likeness commands respect in any market.

MERCHANT_GUILD.name: Merchant Guild
MERCHANT_GUILD.description: Found a merchant guild for powerful economic bonuses.
MERCHANT_GUILD.flavorText: United merchants shape the fate of kingdoms.

BANKING_SYSTEMS.name: Banking Systems
BANKING_SYSTEMS.description: Advanced financial institutions and investment returns.
BANKING_SYSTEMS.flavorText: Let money beget money, and prosperity shall follow.

SHIPBUILDING.name: Shipbuilding
SHIPBUILDING.description: Construct seaworthy vessels for trade and exploration. Fleet limit +3 ships.
SHIPBUILDING.flavorText: The first plank laid is a promise to the sea.

NAVIGATION.name: Navigation
NAVIGATION.description: Star charts and compass enable long-distance sea voyages. Ships sail 30% faster; +25% exploration finds.
NAVIGATION.flavorText: By star and compass, the unknown becomes a road.

DEEP_SEA_FISHING.name: Deep Sea Fishing
DEEP_SEA_FISHING.description: Venture into deep waters for bountiful catches. +40% fish from wharf boats and fishing fleets.
DEEP_SEA_FISHING.flavorText: The deep waters teem with silver bounty.

NAVAL_WARFARE.name: Naval Warfare
NAVAL_WARFARE.description: Train marines and outfit warships for sea battles.
NAVAL_WARFARE.flavorText: Command the seas, and the land shall kneel.

LIGHTHOUSE.name: Lighthouse
LIGHTHOUSE.description: Build coastal lighthouses to protect shipping and boost port trade.
LIGHTHOUSE.flavorText: A single flame on the shore saves a thousand souls at sea.

HERBALISM.name: Herbalism
HERBALISM.description: Identify and cultivate medicinal plants for basic remedies. +15% plague resistance.
HERBALISM.flavorText: The forest is the oldest apothecary.

SURGERY.name: Surgery
SURGERY.description: Skilled surgeons save wounded soldiers: -20% battle deaths, and 30% of the fallen are carried off wounded instead (half strength for 5 days).
SURGERY.flavorText: A steady hand and a sharp blade — the surgeon's arts.

PLAGUE_PREVENTION.name: Plague Prevention
PLAGUE_PREVENTION.description: Quarantine protocols and sanitation reduce disease spread. +40% plague resistance.
PLAGUE_PREVENTION.flavorText: Cleanliness wards off death more surely than any sword.

HOSPITAL.name: Hospital
HOSPITAL.description: Establish hospitals for comprehensive healthcare in settlements.
HOSPITAL.flavorText: Where the sick are tended, civilisation endures.

WRITING.name: Writing
WRITING.description: Develop a writing system for record-keeping and knowledge preservation. +10% research; halves the upkeep overhead of running many properties.
WRITING.flavorText: With marks on clay, we conquered time itself.

PHILOSOPHY.name: Philosophy
PHILOSOPHY.description: Schools of thought that enrich culture and governance.
PHILOSOPHY.flavorText: The unexamined realm is not worth ruling.

DIPLOMACY_MASTERY.name: Diplomacy Mastery
DIPLOMACY_MASTERY.description: Advanced diplomatic techniques for treaties and alliances. +30% effective diplomacy; tribute and peace treaties cost 20% less.
DIPLOMACY_MASTERY.flavorText: Words, well placed, can accomplish what armies cannot.

UNIVERSITY.name: University
UNIVERSITY.description: Found a great university to accelerate all research.
UNIVERSITY.flavorText: Knowledge multiplies when minds gather under one roof.

PRINTING_PRESS.name: Printing Press
PRINTING_PRESS.description: Mass-produce books and spread literacy across the realm.
PRINTING_PRESS.flavorText: A single press can topple empires — or build them.

ESPIONAGE.name: Espionage
ESPIONAGE.description: Train spies and establish intelligence networks.
ESPIONAGE.flavorText: The truest weapon is the one your enemy never sees.

HEAVY_CAVALRY.name: Heavy Cavalry
HEAVY_CAVALRY.description: Armored knights on warhorses — the ultimate shock force.

PLATE_ARMOR.name: Plate Armor
PLATE_ARMOR.description: Full plate armor provides extraordinary protection: enemies strike 15% weaker and 15% fewer of your soldiers die.
PLATE_ARMOR.flavorText: Encased in steel, a single knight becomes a fortress.

CROSSBOW.name: Crossbow
CROSSBOW.description: Mechanical bows that penetrate heavy armor: ranged units hit 25% harder (scaled by their share of your army).
CROSSBOW.flavorText: Even a peasant with a crossbow can fell a knight.

WINDMILL.name: Windmill
WINDMILL.description: Harness wind power for grinding grain and pumping water.
WINDMILL.flavorText: What the wind gives freely, the wise put to work.

GLASSMAKING.name: Glassmaking
GLASSMAKING.description: Produce glass for windows, lenses, and trade goods.
GLASSMAKING.flavorText: From sand, something wondrous — clear as water, hard as stone.

DEEP_MINING.name: Deep Mining
DEEP_MINING.description: Mine deeper veins for rare ores and gems.
DEEP_MINING.flavorText: The deeper we dig, the richer the earth becomes.

IRRIGATED_FARM.name: Irrigated Farm
IRRIGATED_FARM.description: Irrigated farmland produces abundant grain even in arid regions. Upkeep: 8g/day

GRANARY.name: Granary
GRANARY.description: Stores the harvest safely: your farms within 1 hex produce +20% and lose only half as much to droughts and floods. Upkeep: 3g/day

FOUNDRY.name: Foundry
FOUNDRY.description: Advanced metalworking facility. Produces refined metals. Upkeep: 20g/day

WATER_MILL.name: Water Mill
WATER_MILL.description: Water-powered mill that grinds flour or saws firewood. +50% output on a river. Upkeep: 8g/day

QUARRY.name: Quarry
QUARRY.description: Extracts building stone from the earth. Upkeep: 12g/day

WATCHTOWER.name: Watchtower
WATCHTOWER.description: Keeps watch over everything within 4 hexes, wherever you are. Upkeep: 5g/day

MERCHANT_GUILD.name: Merchant Guild
MERCHANT_GUILD.description: A guild hall that adds +10% to all your trade profits (up to 3 halls). Upkeep: 15g/day

SHIPYARD.name: Shipyard
SHIPYARD.description: Repairs your ships docked beside it by 5% a day, free. Upkeep: 12g/day

FISHING_FLEET.name: Fishing Fleet
FISHING_FLEET.description: A fleet of fishing boats harvesting the deep sea. Upkeep: 8g/day

LIGHTHOUSE.name: Lighthouse
LIGHTHOUSE.description: Guides ships in safely: +15% on cargo you sell at a port beside it. Upkeep: 5g/day

HOSPITAL.name: Hospital
HOSPITAL.description: Treats the sick and wounded: you heal 15 health a day while within 2 hexes. Upkeep: 10g/day

UNIVERSITY.name: University
UNIVERSITY.description: A center of higher learning: research takes 25% less time (up to 2 universities). Upkeep: 18g/day

WINDMILL.name: Windmill
WINDMILL.description: A tall wind-powered mill that grinds grain into flour faster than a basic Mill. Upkeep: 5g/day

LONGBOWMAN.name: Longbowman
LONGBOWMAN.description: Elite ranged unit with devastating volleys: up to +6% power against melee-heavy foes

CAVALRY.name: Light Cavalry
CAVALRY.description: Fast mounted units, excellent for flanking and pursuit

SIEGE_ENGINE.name: Siege Engine
SIEGE_ENGINE.description: Devastating siege weapons: +40% army power when raiding or besieging a settlement (max +100%)

WARSHIP.name: Warship
WARSHIP.description: Armed vessel for naval combat and coastal raids

HEAVY_CAVALRY.name: Heavy Cavalry
HEAVY_CAVALRY.description: Heavily armored mounted knights — devastating shock troops

CROSSBOWMAN.name: Crossbowman
CROSSBOWMAN.description: Armored ranged unit with armor-piercing bolts

STEEL_WEAPONS.name: Forge Steel Weapons
STEEL_WEAPONS.description: Forge superior steel weapons worth more.

STEEL_ARMOR.name: Forge Steel Armor
STEEL_ARMOR.description: Forge protective steel armor and equipment.

PLATE_ARMOR_SET.name: Forge Plate Armor
PLATE_ARMOR_SET.description: Craft full suits of plate armor for elite warriors.

GLASS_GOODS.name: Produce Glass Goods
GLASS_GOODS.description: Craft valuable glass items for trade and construction.

tax_collector.name: Tax Collector
tax_collector.description: You are charged with visiting settlements and collecting taxes on behalf of the crown. A thankless but lucrative office.

duties.description: Visit at least 3 kingdom settlements and collect taxes each month.

jailer.name: Jailer
jailer.description: You are the keeper of the kingdom's dungeons. Hunt fugitives, capture criminals, and deliver them to the nearest jail.

duties.description: Capture at least 1 fugitive and bring them to justice each month.

marshal.name: Marshal
marshal.description: Commander of the kingdom's military patrols. Defend the realm, clear bandits from the roads, and escort caravans.

duties.description: Complete at least 4 patrols through kingdom territory each month.

spymaster.name: Spymaster
spymaster.description: Master of whispers and shadows. Gather intelligence on rival kingdoms, uncover plots, and manage the kingdom's informant network.

duties.description: Gather at least 2 pieces of foreign intelligence each month.

court_chaplain.name: Court Chaplain
court_chaplain.description: Spiritual advisor to the court. Tend to the kingdom's faith, bless the people, and maintain holy sites.

duties.description: Visit and bless at least 2 kingdom settlements each month.

trade_envoy.name: Trade Envoy
trade_envoy.description: Official representative of the kingdom's trade interests. Negotiate deals, establish trade routes, and bring prosperity.

duties.description: Complete at least 2 trade missions to foreign kingdoms each month.

royal_cartographer.name: Royal Cartographer
royal_cartographer.description: Official mapmaker of the realm. Explore uncharted territory, survey borders, and expand the kingdom's knowledge of the world.

duties.description: Explore and survey at least 20 new tiles each month.

chancellor.name: Chancellor
chancellor.description: Chief advisor to the ruler and overseer of the kingdom's affairs. The highest non-royal office, with authority over all other officials.

duties.description: Hold court at the capital and maintain kingdom stability each month.

taxCollection._doc: How a Tax Collector collects (systems/titles.js). fee/levy/skim multiply the rolled fee (the collector's take) and the crown's levy (4x the fee); happiness, karma, renown, rep (x the office's reputationGain) apply per collection; resentment is a grudge kept on the settlement (crownLevy) that fades one point per resentmentDecayDays and cuts later yields by resentmentYield per point; squeezing a resentful town risks a riot. A skimmer faces the month's audit. The crown's share (the levy, less any skim, halved by a riot) is drawn from the town's purse (economy.gold) after the collector's fee and credited to the kingdom's treasury on the crownLines tax lines (world/crownBooks.js). unrest goes to the player's holding there, or (x unheldUnrestHappiness) onto the mood of a town he does not hold; a riot shuts the crown's tax-house for riotRevoltDays (settlement.taxRevolt, read by systems/fiscal.js).

blessing._doc: A Court Chaplain's blessing on a settlement: mood up by happiness, and for `days` days anyone there catches disease at sicknessMult of the usual chance (systems/ailments.js).

DROUGHT.name: Severe Drought
DROUGHT.description: A prolonged drought scorches the land, devastating crops and drying rivers.
DROUGHT.text: A terrible drought grips {region}. Crops wither and wells run dry.

PLAGUE.name: Plague Outbreak
PLAGUE.description: A devastating plague sweeps through settlements, killing thousands.
PLAGUE.text: Plague has broken out in {settlement}! The dead are piling up in the streets.

FLOOD.name: Great Flood
FLOOD.description: Rivers burst their banks, flooding farmland and washing away roads.
FLOOD.text: Devastating floods ravage the lowlands near {settlement}.

EARTHQUAKE.name: Earthquake
EARTHQUAKE.description: The earth shakes violently, toppling buildings and opening fissures.
EARTHQUAKE.text: A mighty earthquake strikes near {settlement}! Buildings crumble and the earth splits.

BOUNTIFUL_HARVEST.name: Bountiful Harvest
BOUNTIFUL_HARVEST.description: Ideal weather conditions produce a bumper harvest across the realm.
BOUNTIFUL_HARVEST.text: The harvest in {region} is the best in living memory! Granaries overflow.

GOLD_RUSH.name: Gold Rush
GOLD_RUSH.description: Rich gold deposits are discovered, drawing prospectors from across the realm.
GOLD_RUSH.text: Gold has been discovered near {settlement}! Prospectors flood into the region.

TRADE_BOOM.name: Trade Boom
TRADE_BOOM.description: A flourishing period of trade enriches merchants and kingdoms alike.
TRADE_BOOM.text: Trade flourishes across {region}. Merchants report record profits.

MARKET_CRASH.name: Market Crash
MARKET_CRASH.description: A sudden collapse in trade confidence sends markets into freefall.
MARKET_CRASH.text: Markets crash across {region}! Merchants are ruined and prices plummet.

PIRATE_SURGE.name: Pirate Surge
PIRATE_SURGE.description: Pirates grow bold and numerous, threatening coastal trade.
PIRATE_SURGE.text: Pirates terrorize the shipping lanes near {settlement}. Sea trade grinds to a halt.

BANDIT_UPRISING.name: Bandit Uprising
BANDIT_UPRISING.description: Organized bandit gangs terrorize the countryside.
BANDIT_UPRISING.text: Bandits have formed an organized gang near {settlement}. The roads are unsafe.

KINGDOM_WAR.name: Kingdom War
KINGDOM_WAR.description: Two kingdoms go to war, dragging their neighbors into the conflict.
KINGDOM_WAR.text: {kingdom1} declares war on {kingdom2}! Armies march to battle.

REBELLION.name: Peasant Rebellion
REBELLION.description: Oppressed peasants rise up against their lords.
REBELLION.text: The peasants of {settlement} have risen in rebellion against {kingdom}!

SUCCESSION_CRISIS.name: Succession Crisis
SUCCESSION_CRISIS.description: The death of a ruler without a clear heir throws a kingdom into turmoil.
SUCCESSION_CRISIS.text: The ruler of {kingdom} has died without a clear heir. Rival claimants vie for the throne.

DIPLOMATIC_MARRIAGE.name: Royal Wedding
DIPLOMATIC_MARRIAGE.description: A royal marriage unites two houses and eases tensions between kingdoms.
DIPLOMATIC_MARRIAGE.text: A grand wedding celebration! {kingdom1} and {kingdom2} forge an alliance through marriage.

RELIGIOUS_SCHISM.name: Religious Schism
RELIGIOUS_SCHISM.description: A major split within a faith divides believers and sows discord.
RELIGIOUS_SCHISM.text: A schism erupts within the {faith}! Believers are forced to choose sides.

HOLY_CRUSADE.name: Holy Crusade
HOLY_CRUSADE.description: Religious leaders call for a holy war to reclaim sacred territory.
HOLY_CRUSADE.text: A crusade is declared! The faithful rally to reclaim the holy lands.

COMET_SIGHTING.name: Comet Sighting
COMET_SIGHTING.description: A blazing comet streaks across the sky. Some see it as a blessing, others a curse.
COMET_SIGHTING.text: A comet appears in the night sky! Priests debate its meaning while the commoners tremble.

ECLIPSE.name: Solar Eclipse
ECLIPSE.description: The sun goes dark in the middle of the day, spreading fear and awe — and driving the frightened to the temples.
ECLIPSE.text: The sun is swallowed by darkness! An eclipse throws the realm into momentary panic.

MONSTER_SIGHTING.name: Monster Sighting
MONSTER_SIGHTING.description: A fearsome creature is sighted in the wilds, threatening travelers and settlements.
MONSTER_SIGHTING.text: A terrible beast has been sighted near {settlement}! Brave warriors are needed.

FESTIVAL.name: Grand Festival
FESTIVAL.description: A grand celebration brings joy and commerce to the realm.
FESTIVAL.text: {kingdom} celebrates a grand festival! Music, food, and merriment fill the streets.

REFUGEE_WAVE.name: Refugee Wave
REFUGEE_WAVE.description: War or disaster drives refugees to seek shelter in neighboring kingdoms.
REFUGEE_WAVE.text: Refugees pour into {settlement}, fleeing turmoil. They bring labor but strain resources.

VOLCANIC_ERUPTION.name: Volcanic Eruption
VOLCANIC_ERUPTION.description: A volcano erupts, raining ash and fire upon the surrounding lands.
VOLCANIC_ERUPTION.text: A volcano erupts with cataclysmic fury! Ash blots out the sun across {region}.

BLIZZARD.name: Great Blizzard
BLIZZARD.description: An unseasonably fierce blizzard blankets the land in deep snow.
BLIZZARD.text: A terrible blizzard sweeps across {region}. Roads are impassable and livestock freeze.

FAMINE.name: Hungry Months
FAMINE.description: Last year's stores run out before the new crop is in. Bread is dear and tempers short. Most likely in the lean weeks of late winter and early spring.
FAMINE.text: The granaries of {region} are bare. Hunger stalks the lean months.

slander.label: Slander
slander.description: {victim} tells anyone who will listen that {perpetrator} is a coward and a cheat ({location})

merchant_slander.label: Merchant Slander
merchant_slander.description: {victim} warn the market that {perpetrator}'s company pays late and sells short weight ({location})

contract_broken.label: Broken Contract
contract_broken.description: {perpetrator} promised {victim} goods for {location} and never delivered

famine_dole.label: Famine Dole
famine_dole.description: {perpetrator} fed the hungry of {location} from their own treasury

feast_given.label: A Feast
feast_given.description: {perpetrator} kept a feast at {location} that the guests are still talking about

pilgrimage_made.label: Pilgrimage
pilgrimage_made.description: {perpetrator} walked the pilgrim's road and knelt at {location}

feast_brawl.label: Brawl at a Feast
feast_brawl.description: there was a brawl at {perpetrator}'s table in {location}, and the host was in the thick of it

beast_slain.label: Beast Slain
beast_slain.description: {perpetrator} faced down {victim} in the wilds near {location}

wilds_rescue.label: Rescue in the Wilds
wilds_rescue.description: {perpetrator} saved {victim} out in the wilds near {location}

wilds_find.label: A Find in the Wilds
wilds_find.description: {perpetrator} came back from the wilds near {location} with {victim}

affair.label: Affair
affair.description: {perpetrator} has been seen keeping close company with {victim} of {location}, and {perpetrator} a married soul

mail_opened.label: Broken Seals
mail_opened.description: {perpetrator} has been reading other people's letters: the seal of {victim} was found lifted in {location}

whisperer.label: Whisperer Exposed
whisperer.description: {perpetrator} was the one spreading those lies about {victim}, it's been traced back to {location}

blackmailer.label: Blackmail
blackmailer.description: {perpetrator} tried to blackmail {victim}, and the crown's men know it ({location})

tellings._comment: Rumours grow in the telling. Each time a rumour reaches a new town, the teller either passes on the version they heard (inherit) or changes it (chance). A telling multiplies the rumour's severity in that town (consequences, guard hostility) and replaces its text there. {base} is the plain description; {perpetrator} {victim} {location} {rival} fill as usual. 'stolen' deeds are credited to someone else; 'clears' tellings no longer name the player.

crime.label: Grown in the telling
crime.text: {base}. And two more who tried to stop it, the way it's told here.

crime.label: Monstrous
crime.text: They say {perpetrator} did unspeakable things to {victim} in {location}. Some swear there was a black rite in it.

crime.label: Softened
crime.text: Word is {perpetrator} and {victim} fell to blows in {location}. Who started it depends on who's telling.

crime.label: Blamed on a stranger
crime.text: Something ugly happened to {victim} in {location}. A stranger in a grey cloak, most say. Nobody here names {perpetrator}.

crime.label: Garbled
crime.text: {perpetrator}, or someone with a name like it, did for {victim} somewhere past {location}. Or was it the other way round?

deed.label: Become legend
deed.text: {base}. Single-handed, if you believe the telling here, and laughing the while.

deed.label: Credited to another
deed.text: {base}... except here they swear it was {rival}, not {perpetrator}.

deed.label: Soured
deed.text: {base}, they say, though some whisper it was done for gain, not goodness.

talk.label: Grown in the telling
talk.text: {perpetrator} and {victim} of {location}! Caught in the hayloft, they say, and not for the first time.

talk.label: Doubted
talk.text: Some say {perpetrator} is sweet on {victim} of {location}. Others say that's the ale talking.

refuted.label: Sung down
refuted.text: There's a song going round that {perpetrator} was falsely accused over {victim}. The bard tells it well.

deedRenown._comment: A deed's word is worth deedWeight = local severity / refSeverity x the telling's regard (legend 1.2, soured 0.3, stolen 0), clamped to [minWeight, maxWeight]. Each town it reaches raises the player's reputation with that town's realm by reputationPerTown x weight (up to reputationCap); a friend there who hears it warms by matters.config.deedPraise x weight. A type with localRenown false (a sack) wins no realm's love.

scandals._comment: Court scandals (systems/whispers.js): tales about the great (rulers, rival adventurers) that hatch at a capital or a town, spread town to town, gather heat and weigh on the realm's stability (kingdom.scandal.stab, read by world/kingdomState.js). Some are true, some are lies; nobody knows which until it is proven, debunked or forgotten. The player hears them in taverns and can fan them, quash them, dig for the truth, blackmail the subject, sell the proof to an enemy crown, or plant a tale of their own. Lines: {subject} {place} {kingdom} {enemy}. fallout.proven / fallout.debunked: what a ruler's tale does to the realm on top of the stability shock (stability, unity, piety, treasuryPct, enemyRelations, advisorLoyalty — Whispers.applyFallout).

bastard.label: A Hidden Bastard
lines: They say {subject} has a bastard hidden away in {place}, and the child has the royal eyes.
A wet-nurse in {place} swears she suckled a child of {subject}'s. Paid in crown silver, she says.
bastard.proven: A child of {subject}'s, born on the wrong side of the blanket, was found in {place}. The court of {kingdom} is in uproar.
bastard.debunked: The so-called bastard of {subject} turned out to be a miller's boy with a lying mother. {subject} is vindicated.

poison.label: A Poisoning
lines: They say {subject}'s uncle didn't die of a fever. Something in the wine, from a cup {subject} poured.
A cook from the palace fled to {place}. She won't say what she put in the soup, or who told her to.
poison.proven: The palace cook confessed before the priests: {subject} ordered the poison. {kingdom} reels.
poison.debunked: The cook who 'fled' turned up drunk in a ditch and recanted everything. The tale of {subject}'s poison dies.

debts.label: The Crown's Debts
lines: They say {subject} has pawned the crown jewels to the moneylenders. Paste on the royal head, gold in a vault in {place}.
Soldiers in {kingdom} haven't seen silver in weeks. {subject} is broke, and everyone knows it but the heralds.
debts.proven: The moneylenders of {place} went public with the pawn tickets. {subject} is a debtor king, and {kingdom} knows it.
debts.debunked: {subject} paid the garrison in full, in good coin, in the square at {place}. So much for the debts.

heresy.label: A Secret Heresy
lines: They say {subject} keeps an old idol in a locked room and prays to it at night.
A chapel boy in {place} saw {subject} spit on the altar. Nobody believed him. Then he vanished.
heresy.proven: The idol was found, exactly where they said. The priests of {kingdom} turn their faces from {subject}.
heresy.debunked: {subject} walked barefoot to the shrine at {place} and was blessed before the crowd. The heresy talk withers.

pact.label: A Secret Pact
lines: They say {subject} writes secret letters to {enemy}. Our sons die so the crown can haggle over the peace.
A courier was stopped near {place} with {enemy}'s seal in his boot. They say the letter was for {subject}.
pact.proven: The letters were real. {subject} has been bargaining with {enemy} behind {kingdom}'s back.
pact.debunked: The 'letters to {enemy}' were forged by a clerk with a grudge. He hanged in {place} this morning.

coward.label: Cowardice
lines: They say {subject} ran from a fight near {place}, left their own people in the mud.
Ask anyone in {place}: {subject} hid in a wine cellar while better folk did the fighting.
coward.proven: Three survivors from {place} told it the same way: {subject} ran. The name won't wash clean.
coward.debunked: {subject} showed the scars from {place} in the square. Nobody calls them a coward now.

affair.label: An Affair
lines: They say {subject} slips out at night to a house in {place}, and it isn't to pray.
A maid in {place} found {subject}'s ring in a bed where it had no business being.
affair.proven: {subject} was caught leaving the house in {place} at dawn. The whole of {kingdom} is laughing.
affair.debunked: The house in {place} turned out to belong to {subject}'s old nurse. The affair talk sours into pity.

madness.label: Madness
lines: They say {subject} talks to the portraits now, and waits for them to answer.
A guard from the palace drinks in {place}. He says {subject} had the hounds tried for treason.
madness.proven: {subject} addressed the court of {kingdom} as if it were a flock of geese. The councillors exchange looks.
madness.debunked: {subject} held a sharp, cold council at {place} and dismissed the guard who'd talked. Mad as a fox, maybe.

cheat.label: A Cheat
lines: They say {subject} rigged the lists at {place}. Bribed the marshal, loosened a rival's girth.
{subject}'s loaded dice cleaned out half the soldiers in {place}, they say.
cheat.proven: The marshal of {place} confessed: {subject} paid him. The name is mud in every tavern.
cheat.debunked: The 'loaded dice' were checked by the priests of {place}: honest bone. {subject} is cleared.

graverobber.label: Grave-Robbing
lines: They say {subject} sells the bones out of the old tombs to the witches in {place}.
That gold {subject} spends so freely? Grave-goods. Someone's grandmother's rings, they say, from {place}.
graverobber.proven: A fence in {place} named {subject} as the source of the grave-goods. The priests want answers.
graverobber.debunked: The grave-goods were traced to a gang in {place}, not to {subject}. An apology is owed.

streetCrime._comment: Violence on a town's street map (systems/streetCrime.js, ui/innerMapReactions.js): who sees it, how they react on the spot, what they remember, and what they say afterwards. Vandalism is smashing the town's things (a well, a stall, a lamp, the furniture in someone's house): {victim} is then the thing smashed ('the well'). Placeholders in lines: {victim} the victim's name, {kin} how the speaker names the victim ('my brother Brom', 'Brom'), {player} the player's name, {town} where it happened, {deed} 'killed' / 'beat'.

sight._comment: Chebyshev tiles from the victim. Indoors everyone in the building sees it. Guards within guardHearRadius who did not see it come running all the same; anyone else within hearRadius turns to look, and the timid hurry away.

disposition._comment: Change to a witness's opinion of the player (0-100, 50 neutral). Kin and friends are also hit by NpcDisposition.onNpcHarmed; these are on top.

refuse._comment: A witness below talkBelow will not chat (amends or leave only). Traders who saw it refuse to deal below tradeBelow.

hearsay._comment: Townsfolk who did not see it hear of it through the town's talk: at the scene share = base + perDay * days since (capped at 1); in towns the rumour has reached, elsewhereShare. mentionAgain: chance they bring it up again once already told.

heat._comment: Share of the crime's underworld heat when no one saw it (a body is still found).

arrest._comment: The watch: days in the cell on top of the heat-based sentence, a fine for a beating (scaled by town size, never less than the bounty owed here), the odds of running for it, and how long the guards remember an unanswered crime in their town.

followIn: Out you come — or I come in!
I saw you go in! Stay where you are!

anger: That's not yours to break! Guards!
Guards! A killing in the street!
That's not yours to break! Guards!
Touch {kin} again and I'll kill you!
I'll have your blood for this!
That's not yours to break! Guards!
Wrecking the town, are we? Stop!
Halt! In the name of the crown!

heard: Stay back, it's not our business.

fear: *keeps their distance* You're the one who smashed {victim}. I don't want any trouble.
*eyes you warily* I saw you take {victim} to pieces. What next, my door?
anger: I saw you smash {victim}, you vandal. Who's to mend it, eh?
You've a nerve, after what you did to {victim}.
old: You're the one who smashed {victim}. We haven't forgotten.
Mind your hands. {victim} is still not mended.

fear: *backs away* I saw what you did to {victim}. Please... I don't want any trouble.
*won't meet your eyes* You're the one who set upon {victim}. Just... leave me be.
anger: I saw you beat {victim} in the street like a dog. What sort of creature are you?
You've a nerve, talking to me after what you did to {victim}.
old: I've not forgotten what you did to {victim}.
You're the one who beat {victim}. People here remember.

fear: *trembling* I saw you kill {victim}. Please, I won't say anything, just don't hurt me.
*goes pale* Stay back! I saw what you did to {victim}!
anger: Murderer. I watched {victim} die at your hands, and you dare speak to me?
{victim}'s blood isn't even dry and here you are, bold as brass. Get away from me.
old: I still see {victim} lying there when I close my eyes. You did that.
You're the one who killed {victim}. I'll never forget your face.

fear: *flinches* Not again, please! I'm still black and blue from the last time.
*shields their face* Stay away from me! Haven't you hurt me enough?
anger: You've got some gall. My ribs still ache from your beating.
Come to finish the job? I'll not go down so easy this time.
old: I remember you. You beat me in the street, and for nothing.
The bruises have faded. What you did hasn't.

fear: *keeps their distance* You're the one who smashed {victim}. I don't want any trouble.
*eyes you warily* I saw you take {victim} to pieces. What next, my door?
anger: I saw you smash {victim}, you vandal. Who's to mend it, eh?
You've a nerve, after what you did to {victim}.
old: You're the one who smashed {victim}. We haven't forgotten.
Mind your hands. {victim} is still not mended.

fear: *steps between you and the door* You hurt {kin}. Please, just go.
{kin} still can't sleep for what you did. Leave us alone.
anger: You beat {kin} half to death. Give me one reason not to return the favour.
Lay a finger on {kin} again and it'll be the last thing you do.
old: I haven't forgotten what you did to {kin}.
Our family remembers you. You beat {kin}.

fear: *sobbing* You killed {kin}. Why? Why would you do that?
*voice breaking* {kin} is dead because of you. Go away. Please, just go away.
anger: *glares with red eyes* You killed {kin}. I'll see you hang, if it's the last thing I do.
You murdered {kin} in the street. Get out of my sight before I do something.
old: {kin}'s grave is still fresh in my heart. You put it there.
There's not a day I don't curse your name for {kin}.

fear: *keeps their distance* You're the one who smashed {victim}. I don't want any trouble.
*eyes you warily* I saw you take {victim} to pieces. What next, my door?
anger: I saw you smash {victim}, you vandal. Who's to mend it, eh?
You've a nerve, after what you did to {victim}.
old: You're the one who smashed {victim}. We haven't forgotten.
Mind your hands. {victim} is still not mended.

fear: {victim} is my friend. I saw what you did. Please, just leave.
anger: {victim} is my friend, and you beat them in the street. I'll not forget it.
old: You're the one who hurt {victim}. Don't expect a kind word from me.

fear: *hushed* {victim} was my friend. And you... you just killed them.
anger: {victim} was my friend. You murdered them, and I'll make sure everyone knows it.
old: I lost a friend in {victim} because of you. Don't think I've forgotten.

anger: You're the one who smashed {victim}. You'll pay for the damage, one way or another.
Wrecking the town's things in plain sight? You're coming with me.
old: I've had my eye on you since you smashed {victim}. Keep your hands to yourself.

anger: You're the one who beat {victim} in the street. You'll answer for that.
Assaulting the townsfolk in plain sight? You're coming with me.
old: I've had my eye on you since you beat {victim}. Step carefully.

anger: {victim}'s killer, walking up to the watch? In the crown's name, you're under arrest.
I saw you cut down {victim}. Hands where I can see them.
old: We've not forgotten {victim}. Neither has the crown.

here: Did you hear? Some stranger smashed {victim} in broad daylight. About your build, now I think of it.
*looks you over* Somebody wrecked {victim}. You wouldn't know anything about that?
elsewhere: There's talk of a lout in {town} who went about smashing things. Was that you?
I heard of trouble in {town}: someone breaking up the town's things.

here: Did you hear? Someone set upon {victim} in the street. A stranger, they say... about your build, now I look at you.
*eyes you warily* Folk say {victim} took a beating from some outsider. You wouldn't know anything about that?
elsewhere: I heard tell of a brawler in {town} who beat some poor soul senseless. Was that you?
There's talk of trouble in {town}. Someone matching your look, so they say.

here: *lowers voice* They say {victim} was killed in the street, and the killer still walks about. You... you look like the one they describe.
*edges away* Word is {victim} was murdered. Folk are saying it was a stranger. Someone like you.
elsewhere: There's a story out of {town}: a stranger killed {victim} in the street. They say the killer looked a lot like you.
*studies your face* You've been to {town}? There was a killing there. I hope it wasn't you they meant.

refuseTrade.vandalism: {name} won't trade with someone who goes about smashing the town's things.
refuseTrade.assault: {name} won't trade with someone who beats people in the street.
refuseTrade.murder: {name} saw you kill {victim} and will have nothing to do with you.

lines.refuseTalk: They want nothing to do with you.

text.vandalism: {guard} steps into your path, hand on his sword. "You smashed {victim}, in front of the whole street. Pay for the damage, or see the inside of a cell."
text.assault: {guard} plants himself in your path, hand on his sword. "You beat {victim} in the street, in front of half the town. You can pay the fine, or you can see the inside of a cell."
text.murder: {guard} blocks your way, blade half drawn. "{victim} lies dead and the whole street saw who did it. You're coming with me."

outcomes.submit: You give yourself up. The watch takes you to the cells: {days} days.
outcomes.fine: You count {fine} gold into the guard's hand. He writes it in his book and lets you go, with a warning.
outcomes.escaped: You dodge past {guard} and lose him in the crowd. The watch will be looking for you.
outcomes.caught: You break and run, but {guard} is faster. They drag you to the cells: {days} days.
outcomes.resist: You square up to {guard}. Resisting the watch will not help your name.

found._comment: Coming upon a body. radius: how far off a body is noticed (indoors: the whole room). gatherShare of the unafraid walk over to look; the rest stop and stare. Standing within overRadius of a body when it is found, or carrying one, makes the finders witnesses to the killing. barks: kin/friend (grief, {kin} = my wife / my son…, {victim} = name), guard, bystander.fear/anger, caught.{guard,kin,fear,anger}, carried.{guard,fear,anger}.

guard: Murder in my streets... someone saw something.
Stand back! Stand back from the body!
Fetch the captain — there's been a killing.
You! Step away from that body!
Don't move! What have you done?
You there — hands where I can see them!
kin: YOU! What did you do to {kin}?!

guard: You're carrying a corpse! Stop right there!
fear: Gods — is that a body over their shoulder?!

brave.name: Brave
brave.description: Charges first and fights to the last. Soldiers follow you gladly.
greetings: *straightens up* They say you never take a step back in battle.
The bards already sing of your courage, friend.

craven.name: Craven
craven.description: Your army has broken and run too often. Men whisper that you flee first.
greetings: *smirks* Off to run from another fight?

cruel.name: Cruel
cruel.description: You hurt the weak and enjoy it. Fear opens doors; affection closes them.
greetings: *keeps a careful distance* I've heard what you did to those people.

merciful.name: Merciful
merciful.description: You spare the beaten and feed the hungry. The common folk remember kindness.
greetings: *smiles warmly* You're the one who helped the poor folk, aren't you?

greedy.name: Greedy
greedy.description: Every coin is yours to take. Merchants haggle hard with you, and everyone counts their purse.
greetings: *clutches purse* What do you want this time?

generous.name: Generous
generous.description: Open-handed with coin and drink. People are glad to see you coming.
greetings: Ah, the open-handed one! Drinks are on you again, I hope?

pious.name: Pious
pious.description: Prayer, pilgrimage and miracles have marked you as devout. The clergy count you among their own.
greetings: *bows head* Blessings upon you, faithful one.

zealous.name: Zealous
zealous.description: You burn heresy and preach without rest. The devout adore you; everyone else is wary.
greetings: *glances nervously* No heretics here, I swear it.

cunning.name: Cunning
cunning.description: Spies, informants and schemes. You know things others don't.
greetings: *lowers voice* I hear you always know more than you let on.

honest.name: Honest
honest.description: You keep your word: quests finished, contracts honoured, alliances kept.
greetings: Your word is good, they say. That's rare these days.

deceitful.name: Deceitful
deceitful.description: Broken oaths and slipped bonds. Nobody quite trusts what you say.
greetings: *narrows eyes* I'll count my change twice, thank you.

merchant_prince.name: Merchant Prince
merchant_prince.description: Your trade fortune is the talk of every market. Guilds deal with you as an equal.
greetings: A pleasure! Every merchant from here to the coast knows your name.

sea_wolf.name: Sea Wolf
sea_wolf.description: Pirates hunted and sea battles won. Sailors fear and admire you.
greetings: *eyes your weathered hands* You've the salt of the sea on you, captain.

scholar.name: Scholar
scholar.description: Research, lore and ancient ruins. Learned folk seek your opinion.
greetings: Ah, the scholar! Is it true you read every tome you find?

gambler.name: Gambler
gambler.description: Dice at every tavern. Fortune favours you a little — and debt follows you a lot.
greetings: *rattles dice* Fancy a round, friend? I hear you never refuse.

drunkard.name: Drunkard
drunkard.description: More nights in the tavern than out of it. Good company, poor counsel.
greetings: *grins* Back for another round, are we?

beloved.name: Beloved of the People
beloved.description: Festivals, fair taxes and open hands. The commons would follow you anywhere.
greetings: *beams* It's an honour! My mother still talks about your festival.

dread_lord.name: Dread Lord
dread_lord.description: Conquest, raids and threats. People do what you say — and love you not at all.
greetings: *trembles* W-whatever you need, my lord. Please.
*won't meet your eye* I've done nothing wrong, I swear it.

wanderer.name: Wanderer
wanderer.description: You've seen more of the world than most kings. Strangers warm to a well-travelled face.
greetings: A traveller! Where have your roads taken you lately?

kinslayer.name: Kinslayer
kinslayer.description: You raised your sword against the realm you married into. Such a stain never washes out.
greetings: *spits* Kinslayer. The gods see what you did.

champion.name: Champion of Tournaments
champion.description: Lists and archery butts: you win them. Nobles want you at their feasts.
greetings: *gasps* The champion of the lists! May I shake your hand?

scarred.name: Scarred
scarred.description: An old wound left its mark across your face. Hard men respect it; most folk look away.
greetings: *stares at your scar, then quickly away* G-good day to you.
*nods at the scar* Saw some fighting, eh?

lame.name: Lame
lame.description: A badly healed wound left you with a limp: one less hex on the road each day, and people pity you a little.
greetings: *watches you limp in* Sit, sit — rest that leg.

petitions._comment: Petitions & Court — dilemmas petitioners bring to the player's holdings. See src/systems/petitions.js for the schema and the effect-key registry. Tokens in text: {name} {name2} {settlement} {kingdom} {people} {rivalPeople} {faith} {house} {rival} {prior} {priorChoice}.

land_dispute.title: The Moved Boundary Stone
land_dispute.text: Two farmers of {settlement}, {name} and {name2}, each swear the other moved the boundary stone between their fields by night. The harvest of a whole strip hangs on your word.

ignore.result: With no ruling, the quarrel turned to fists at the market cross.

choices.label: Send a surveyor to find the true line
choices.result: Your surveyor traces the old charter line. Both men grumble, but both accept it.

choices.label: Split the strip down the middle
choices.result: Neither man is satisfied — which the village takes as a fair sign.

choices.label: Declare the strip crown land
choices.result: The strip is yours now. Both farmers curse you, for once in agreement.

guild_monopoly.title: The Clothiers' Charter
guild_monopoly.text: {name}, master of the clothiers' guild of {settlement}, lays a heavy purse before you. The guild asks for sole right to sell cloth in the town — no peddlers, no foreign bolts.

ignore.result: The guild takes your silence as contempt.

choices.label: Grant the monopoly and take the purse
choices.result: The guild's purse is heavy. The price of cloth will soon be heavier.

choices.label: Grant a five-year charter for a fee
choices.result: A charter with an end date — the guild grumbles at the terms and pays.

choices.label: Refuse: the market stays open
choices.result: The peddlers cheer. The guild masters do not.

merchant_venturers.title: The Merchant Venturers
merchant_venturers.text: {name}, spokesman of the merchant venturers of {settlement}, asks that your House charter a trading company under its own seal — posts, factors and contracts in your name — rather than leave the trade to foreign houses.

ignore.result: The venturers took their ledgers to a rival house.

choices.label: Seal a charter for your own company
choices.result: The charter is sealed. Your House may found a trading company (Trading Company, in any town).

choices.label: Sell the venturers a charter of their own
choices.result: The venturers pay handsomely and trade under their own seal.

choices.label: Trade is no business of a lord
choices.result: The venturers bow stiffly and leave.

famine_plea.title: Empty Granaries
famine_plea.text: A delegation from {settlement}, led by the reeve {name}, kneels in the snow. The stores will not last the season; children are already going hungry.

ignore.result: No help came. Some starved; more left.

choices.label: Buy grain from the treasury
choices.result: Carts of grain roll into {settlement}. They will remember who fed them.

choices.label: Requisition the merchants' stores
choices.result: Your soldiers open the merchants' cellars. The poor eat; the merchants count their losses.

choices.label: Send the hungry to the temples' charity
choices.result: The priests feed whom they can. It is not enough, but it is something.

choices.label: Refuse — the treasury is not a granary
choices.result: The delegation leaves in silence. The winter does the rest.

drought_plea.title: The Wells Run Dry
drought_plea.text: The summer has been merciless around {settlement}. {name} asks that you pay diggers for a deep well before the cattle die.

ignore.result: The cattle died in the dry fields.

choices.label: Pay for the deep well
choices.result: Sweet water at forty feet. {settlement} drinks to your health.

choices.label: Order prayers for rain

success.result: Rain falls three days later. The priests say it was you; you let them.

failure.result: The sky stays brass. The prayers are not answered.

choices.result: Bells ring and censers swing across {settlement}.

choices.label: Make the town share the old well by lot
choices.result: A fair rota, grimly kept.

heretic_preacher.title: The Hedge Preacher
heretic_preacher.text: A wild-eyed preacher, {name}, draws crowds in the square of {settlement}, denouncing {faith} as a lie of the rich. The priests demand you silence him.

ignore.result: Unchecked, the preacher's crowds grew — and so did the priests' anger.

choices.label: Expel him from the town
choices.result: {name} is marched to the boundary stones. His followers watch in silence.

choices.label: Imprison him for sedition
choices.result: The cell door shuts. The square is quiet — for now.

choices.label: Let him preach — words are not crimes
choices.result: {name} goes on preaching, freely and loudly.

choices.label: Debate him before the crowd

success.result: You take his arguments apart one by one. The crowd laughs him out of town.

failure.result: He is quicker than you. The crowd laughs — at you.

choices.result: You climb the steps of the market cross.

noble_sons_crime.title: A Noble Son's Crime
noble_sons_crime.text: {name2}, the son of a landed family, killed a tanner of {settlement} in a drunken quarrel. Witnesses abound. His father begs mercy and hints at gratitude; the tanner's widow demands the rope.

ignore.result: You let it rot. The commons say the gallows are only for the poor.

choices.label: Hang him — the law is the same for all
choices.result: {name2} hangs at dawn. The commons cheer; the great families mark the day.
choices.chronicle: {house} hanged a noble's son for murder in {settlement}.

choices.label: Exact a blood-price for the widow
choices.result: The father pays the widow handsomely. No one is happy, which is how justice often feels.

choices.label: Accept the father's 'gratitude'
choices.result: The purse is heavy and the boy walks free.

choices.label: Pardon him for his family's service
choices.result: {name2} walks free with a lecture. The widow's curses follow you up the stairs.

refugees_at_gates.title: Refugees at the Gates
refugees_at_gates.text: Hundreds of refugees fleeing war have gathered outside {settlement}. Their spokeswoman, {name}, asks for shelter. The townsfolk eye them warily.

ignore.result: The refugees camped at the walls until hunger and fever broke them up.

choices.label: Open the gates
choices.result: The refugees stream in, thin and grateful.

choices.label: Admit those who will serve in the militia
choices.result: The able-bodied take up spears; the rest move on.

choices.label: Turn them away
choices.result: The gates stay shut. The column trudges on down the road.

migrants_seek_land.title: Settlers Seek Land
migrants_seek_land.text: A band of landless families led by {name} asks leave to clear the woods beside {settlement} and settle there under your protection.

ignore.result: The families moved on to a kinder lord.

choices.label: Grant them the woodland, tax-free for a year
choices.result: Axes ring in the woods by {settlement}.

choices.label: Grant it, for rent
choices.result: They agree to your terms, without enthusiasm.

choices.label: The woods are for your hunting
choices.result: The families leave. The deer remain.

peoples_conflict.title: Quarrel of the Quarters
peoples_conflict.text: In {settlement}, the {people} and the {rivalPeople} have come to blows over the market well. Elders of both peoples stand before you, each demanding the other be punished.

ignore.result: The quarters settled it themselves, with cudgels.

choices.label: Side with the {people}
choices.result: The {people} rejoice. The {rivalPeople} will not forget.

choices.label: Side with the {rivalPeople}
choices.result: The {rivalPeople} rejoice. The {people} will not forget.

choices.label: Dig a second well for all
choices.result: Two wells, and a fragile peace.

choices.label: Flog the brawlers of both quarters
choices.result: Order returns at the end of a whip.

peoples_festival_ban.title: A Foreign Rite
peoples_festival_ban.text: The {people} of {settlement} wish to hold their ancestral rite in the streets. Townsfolk call it strange and unlucky, and {name} has gathered signatures to ban it.

ignore.result: The rite went ahead amid jeers and thrown stones.

choices.label: Allow the rite, under the watch's protection
choices.result: Drums and masks fill the streets. Some townsfolk even join in.

choices.label: Ban it within the walls
choices.result: The {people} hold their rite in a field outside, grieving.

choices.label: Attend the rite yourself
choices.result: Your presence silences the jeering. The {people} will speak of it for years.
choices.chronicle: {house} honoured the rites of the {people} at {settlement}.

bandit_surrender.title: The Bandit's Surrender
bandit_surrender.text: {name}, a bandit captain who has plagued the roads near {settlement}, comes under a white flag. He offers to lay down arms — in exchange for a pardon for himself and his men.

ignore.result: Unanswered, the bandits went back to the roads.

choices.label: Pardon him and take his men into your guard
choices.result: {name} kneels and swears to serve. Your sergeants look doubtful.
choices.chronicle: {house} pardoned the bandit {name} and took him into service.

choices.label: Seize and hang him
choices.result: A white flag is no shield for a murderer. {name} hangs at the crossroads.

choices.label: Take his hoard and let him go
choices.result: The bandit's chest is heavy. He rides off lighter, and smiling.

temple_request.title: A Temple for {settlement}
temple_request.text: Father {name} of {faith} asks you to fund a proper temple in {settlement}. The faithful worship in a barn, he says, and the gods notice such things.

ignore.result: The priest preached a sermon on ungrateful lords.

choices.label: Fund a stone temple
choices.result: Masons arrive within the week. The faithful weep at the first stone.

choices.label: Fund a modest shrine
choices.result: A small shrine rises by the well.

choices.label: Demand the priests tithe to you instead
choices.result: Father {name} pays, pale with fury.

choices.label: Refuse politely
choices.result: The priest bows stiffly and leaves.

moneylender_debt.title: The Moneylender's Bond
moneylender_debt.text: {name2}, a moneylender of {settlement}, holds the bond of {name}, a cooper who cannot pay. By the letter of the contract the cooper's house and tools are forfeit.

ignore.result: The moneylender took the cooper's house. The town took note.

choices.label: Enforce the contract
choices.result: A bond is a bond. The cooper's family moves in with his sister.

choices.label: Cancel the debt by decree
choices.result: The moneylender tears the bond with shaking hands.

choices.label: Pay half from your purse and reschedule the rest
choices.result: Both men leave with something. The town admires the compromise.

choices.label: Cap interest across the town
choices.result: Your decree is read in the square. The lenders draw up new contracts.

widow_inheritance.title: The Widow's Forge
widow_inheritance.text: The smith of {settlement} has died. His widow, {name}, means to keep the forge. His brother, {name2}, says custom gives it to him.

ignore.result: The brother took the forge by force; the widow took to the road.

choices.label: The forge is the widow's
choices.result: {name} relights the forge the same night.

choices.label: Custom gives it to the brother
choices.result: Custom is satisfied. The widow is not.

choices.label: Sell the forge and split the price (less your fee)
choices.result: A new smith buys the forge. The family splits the coin and the grudge.

soldiers_tavern_brawl.title: Soldiers Wreck a Tavern
soldiers_tavern_brawl.text: Men of the garrison smashed {name}'s tavern in {settlement} after a dispute over a dice game. The tavernkeeper wants compensation; the sergeant says his men were cheated.

ignore.result: The tavern stays shuttered and the soldiers swagger.

choices.label: Dock the soldiers' pay
choices.result: The men pay, and mutter.

choices.label: Pay from the treasury
choices.result: The tavern reopens. The soldiers learn nothing.

choices.label: Flog the ringleaders
choices.result: Discipline is restored, publicly.

witch_accusation.title: The Herbwoman Accused
witch_accusation.text: A child in {settlement} has sickened, and the mob blames {name}, an old herbwoman who lives by the mill. They drag her before you crying witchcraft.

ignore.result: Left to itself, the mob decided. It was ugly.

choices.label: Take her under your protection
choices.result: The mob disperses, sullen. {name} bows deeply to you.

choices.label: Banish her from the town
choices.result: {name} hobbles away down the north road.

choices.label: Hold a proper trial

success.result: The physician shows the child ate bad mushrooms. The town is shamed and quiet.

failure.result: The trial finds nothing either way. Nobody is satisfied.

choices.result: You summon witnesses and a physician.

miners_strike.title: The Miners Lay Down Picks
miners_strike.text: The miners and quarrymen of {settlement} refuse to work. {name} speaks for them: the pay is a pittance and the tunnels kill a man a month.

ignore.result: The strike dragged on; the town went without stone and ore.

choices.label: Raise their wages from your treasury
choices.result: The picks ring again.

choices.label: Promise a share of next season's profit
choices.result: The miners return to work on your word.

choices.label: Break the strike with the garrison
choices.result: Spears drive the miners back into the dark.

deserter_caught.title: A Deserter Caught
deserter_caught.text: {name}, a young levy, ran from the war and was caught hiding in his mother's barn near {settlement}. The captains want an example made.

ignore.result: The captains carried out the sentence themselves, and despised you for not giving it.

choices.label: Hang him as an example
choices.result: The levies watch {name} hang. None desert that month.

choices.label: Send him back to the front lines
choices.result: {name} returns to the line under guard.

choices.label: Spare him — he is a boy
choices.result: His mother kisses your boots. The captains mutter about softness.

war_levy_plea.title: Spare Us the Levy
war_levy_plea.text: With the harvest standing, the people of {settlement} beg exemption from the war levy. {name} says if the men march, the grain will rot.

ignore.result: The levy was taken by default. Half the harvest rotted.

choices.label: Exempt them
choices.result: The men stay to reap. The captains count their thin ranks.

choices.label: The levy stands
choices.result: The men march. The women and old folk reap what they can.

choices.label: Hire mercenaries in their place
choices.result: Hired swords march in place of farmers.

foreign_merchant_rights.title: A Foreign Merchant Prince
foreign_merchant_rights.text: {name}, a merchant prince from distant lands, asks for a warehouse and the right to trade freely in {settlement}, offering a gift of rare spices and silver.

ignore.result: The merchant prince took his caravans elsewhere.

choices.label: Grant him free trade
choices.result: Spices and silks fill the market — and local merchants fume.

choices.label: Grant it, with a heavy toll
choices.result: He accepts, calculating.

choices.label: Protect the local guilds
choices.result: The local guilds toast your name.

monastery_exemption.title: The Abbey's Exemption
monastery_exemption.text: The abbot of a {faith} abbey near {settlement} asks that its lands be freed from tax, that the brothers may feed the poor.

ignore.result: The abbot complains to his superiors of your indifference.

choices.label: Grant the exemption
choices.result: The abbey's bells ring in your honour.

choices.label: Tax them like anyone else
choices.result: The abbot pays, and prays for your soul with feeling.

choices.label: Exempt them in exchange for a school
choices.result: The brothers will teach the town's children their letters.

orphans.title: The Orphans of {settlement}
orphans.text: Fever has left a dozen children orphaned in {settlement}. {name}, a washerwoman, has been feeding them from her own pot, and begs for help.

ignore.result: The children scattered to the streets.

choices.label: Found an orphanage
choices.result: A house with a hearth and a matron. The children have a home.

choices.label: Give them to the temple's care
choices.result: The priests take them in.

choices.label: Bind them as apprentices
choices.result: The guilds get cheap hands; the children get a trade, eventually.

poacher.title: The Poacher
poacher.text: Your foresters have caught {name} with a deer on his shoulders. His family is starving, he says, and he had no other way.

ignore.result: The foresters let him go, and the woods filled with snares.

choices.label: Hang him by forest law
choices.result: Forest law is old and hard. {name} hangs.

choices.label: Fine him and keep the deer
choices.result: He pays what he has.

choices.label: Hire him as a gamekeeper
choices.result: Who better to catch poachers than a poacher?

festival_request.title: A Midsummer Feast
festival_request.text: The folk of {settlement} ask you to sponsor the midsummer feast — oxen, ale, musicians — as the old lords did.

ignore.result: The feast was a meagre affair, and they knew whom to blame.

choices.label: Sponsor a lavish feast
choices.result: The ale flows for three days. Songs are made about your table.

choices.label: Sponsor a modest feast
choices.result: Bread, beer and a fiddler. It suffices.

choices.label: Times are hard; no feast this year
choices.result: The square stays quiet on midsummer night.

disputed_match.title: A Match Across a Feud
disputed_match.text: {name}, the daughter of a family sworn to {house}, wishes to marry a son of {rival}. Her father asks whether the House forbids it.

ignore.result: The lovers eloped. Both houses took offence.

choices.label: Bless the match
choices.result: A wedding softens old grudges — a little.
choices.chronicle: {house} blessed a marriage with {rival}, cooling an old feud.

choices.label: Forbid it
choices.result: The girl weeps; her father thanks you.

choices.label: Bless it, and demand a dowry from {rival}
choices.result: {rival} pays, with very bad grace.

cousin_debts.title: The Cousin's Debts
cousin_debts.text: {name}, a cousin of {house}, has run up ruinous gambling debts in the name of the House. His creditors are at your door.

ignore.result: The creditors spread word that {house} does not pay its debts.

choices.label: Pay the debts — the House's name is at stake
choices.result: The creditors are paid. {name} is lectured within an inch of his life.

choices.label: Disown him publicly
choices.result: {name} is struck from the House's rolls.

choices.label: Make him work the debt off in your service
choices.result: {name} becomes the House's least willing clerk.

rival_herald_insult.title: A Herald's Insult
rival_herald_insult.text: A herald of {rival} has read out a mocking verse about {house} in the great hall of {kingdom}. Your household waits to see how you answer.

ignore.result: Silence was taken for weakness.

choices.label: Demand a public apology
choices.result: {rival} apologizes through gritted teeth.

choices.label: Laugh it off
choices.result: Your good humour wins some admirers — and some sneers.

choices.label: Answer with a sharper verse

success.result: Your reply is repeated in every tavern. {rival} is the joke now.

failure.result: Your verse limps. The court winces.

choices.result: You call for pen and ink.

veterans_pension.title: The Old Soldiers
veterans_pension.text: Grey veterans of old campaigns, led by {name}, ask for pensions. They bled for the realm, they say, and now beg in the streets of {settlement}.

ignore.result: The veterans told every recruit how the realm repays its soldiers.

choices.label: Grant pensions
choices.result: The old soldiers salute you with shaking hands.

choices.label: Grant them plots of land instead
choices.result: Swords to ploughshares, literally.

choices.label: Refuse — they were paid in their day
choices.result: The veterans spit on the steps as they leave.

plague_quarantine.title: Fever in the Lower Town
plague_quarantine.text: {name}, a physician of {settlement}, warns that a fever is spreading in the lower town. She asks you to seal it off before it reaches the rest.

ignore.result: No action was taken. The fever spread.

choices.label: Seal the lower town
choices.result: Chains go up across the lanes. Behind them, people wail.

choices.label: Pay physicians to treat the sick
choices.result: Physicians in beaked masks go door to door.

choices.label: Leave it to prayer
choices.result: The priests lead processions through the lower town.

smuggler_bribe.title: The Smugglers' Offer
smuggler_bribe.text: A smooth-tongued fellow named {name} offers you a share of the smuggling trade through {settlement} — if your toll-men look the other way.

ignore.result: The smugglers took your silence as consent, and paid you nothing.

choices.label: Take your cut
choices.result: A purse appears on your table every new moon.

choices.label: Arrest him and raid the warehouses
choices.result: Contraband piles up in the square. {name} sits in a cell.

choices.label: Make them pay a legal toll
choices.result: Smugglers become importers, at a price.

pilgrim_shelter.title: Pilgrims Seek Shelter
pilgrim_shelter.text: A column of {faith} pilgrims led by {name} asks for food and shelter in {settlement} on their way to a holy site.

ignore.result: The pilgrims slept in the ditches and spoke of your town's coldness.

choices.label: Shelter and feed them
choices.result: The pilgrims bless your hall as they go.

choices.label: Charge them for lodging
choices.result: Pilgrims pay; pilgrims remember.

choices.label: Walk a day's road with them
choices.result: Your company on the road inspires several to take up your faith.

council_seat.title: A Seat on the Council
council_seat.text: {name}, a wealthy burgher of {kingdom}, asks you to name him to the council. He promises the guilds' support — and a handsome gift.

ignore.result: The burgher found a more obliging patron.

choices.label: Appoint him
choices.result: The nobles are appalled to sit beside a draper.

choices.label: Council seats are not for sale
choices.result: The burgher leaves with his purse.

choices.label: Offer the seat to a commoner instead
choices.result: A blacksmith sits on the council. The realm talks of nothing else.
choices.chronicle: {house} gave a council seat in {kingdom} to a commoner.

border_lord_tribute.title: The Border Lord's Grievance
border_lord_tribute.text: {name}, a lord on the marches of {kingdom}, complains that royal taxes leave him nothing to pay his garrison. He hints that the realm's enemies pay better.

ignore.result: The border lord grew sullen, and his gates less watchful.

choices.label: Remit his taxes for a year
choices.result: The marches hold firm.

choices.label: Remind him what treason costs

failure.result: He opens his gates to raiders out of spite.

choices.result: You send a letter sealed in black wax.

choices.label: Send royal troops to his castle
choices.result: Royal banners fly over the marches.

colony_autonomy.title: The Colonists' Charter
colony_autonomy.text: The elders of {settlement}, led by {name}, ask for a charter of rights: their own council, their own courts, and lower taxes.

ignore.result: The elders read your silence as contempt.

choices.label: Grant the charter
choices.result: {settlement} celebrates its charter.

choices.label: Grant them a council, but keep the courts
choices.result: Half a loaf, accepted gravely.

choices.label: Refuse — a colony is ruled, not consulted
choices.result: The elders leave in silence.

bandit_loyal.title: The Pardoned Bandit Returns
bandit_loyal.text: {prior}, the bandit you pardoned, has served your guard with ferocious loyalty. Today he brings in the heads of the gang he once rode with, and asks for a captain's rank.

ignore.result: {prior} took the silence hard, but stayed.

choices.label: Make him a captain
choices.result: Captain {prior} salutes you. The roads are safer than they have been in years.
choices.chronicle: {prior}, once a bandit pardoned by {house}, became a captain of its guard.

choices.label: Reward him with gold, but no rank
choices.result: {prior} pockets the gold with a shrug.

bandit_betrays.title: The Bandit's Betrayal
bandit_betrays.text: {prior}, the bandit you pardoned, has fled back to the hills — with the guard's horses and the strongbox of {settlement}.

ignore.result: {prior} is a legend in the taverns now — at your expense.

choices.label: Lead the hunt yourself
choices.result: You run {prior} to ground in a shepherd's hut. This time there is no pardon.

choices.label: Post a bounty
choices.result: Bounty hunters bring back his head within the month.

choices.label: Let him go — the lesson is learned
choices.result: The strongbox is gone. So is your faith in reformed men.

bandit_raids_again.title: The Bandit Rides Again
bandit_raids_again.text: {prior}, the bandit you let go with his life for his hoard, has rebuilt his band. Farms near {settlement} are burning.

ignore.result: The raids went on unchecked.

choices.label: Ride out against him
choices.result: His band scatters before your riders.

choices.label: Pay him to go elsewhere
choices.result: He takes the gold — and someone else's farms burn.

noble_son_again.title: He Has Killed Again
noble_son_again.text: {prior}, the noble son you spared, has killed again — a serving girl this time. The town is at the edge of riot, and everyone remembers your last ruling.

ignore.result: A mob burned the young lord's family home. Order broke down for days.

choices.label: Hang him now
choices.result: Too late for the girl. Not too late for justice, the people say — barely.
choices.chronicle: {house} hanged {prior}, twice a killer, too late to save his second victim.

choices.label: Exile him beyond the realm
choices.result: {prior} is put on a ship. The town is not appeased.

choices.label: Protect him again
choices.result: Your guards ring his family's house. Stones fly at your banners.

heretic_flock.title: The Preacher's Flock
heretic_flock.text: {prior}, the hedge preacher you let speak, now has a flock of hundreds in {settlement}. They ask for a chapel of their own; the priests of {faith} call it open heresy.

ignore.result: The flock built its chapel anyway, and the priests blame you.

choices.label: Let them build
choices.result: A plain timber chapel rises. Its bell sounds different from the temple's.

choices.label: Disperse the flock
choices.result: Soldiers break up the meetings. {prior} vanishes into the hills.

choices.label: Invite {prior} into the established temple

success.result: {prior} accepts a pulpit. The schism heals.

choices.result: You broker a meeting between preacher and priests.

refugees_settled.title: The Refugees Give Thanks
refugees_settled.text: The refugees you sheltered in {settlement} have cleared fields and raised houses. {prior} comes with their first harvest as a gift.

ignore.result: The gift went unacknowledged.

choices.label: Accept their gift
choices.result: Their harvest fills your table.

choices.label: Return it — let them keep their first harvest
choices.result: They will tell their grandchildren of this.
choices.chronicle: The refugees of {settlement} became loyal subjects of {house}.

refugees_unrest.title: Old Townsfolk and New
refugees_unrest.text: The refugees you admitted to {settlement} are clashing with the old townsfolk over work and wages. {prior} says her people are being driven from the market.

ignore.result: The clashes festered into a riot.

choices.label: Guarantee the newcomers' rights
choices.result: The law protects the newcomers. The old townsfolk resent it.

choices.label: Pay for public works to employ them
choices.result: New walls, new jobs, fewer fights.

choices.label: Send the troublemakers away
choices.result: Shelter, it turns out, had conditions.

herbwoman_healer.title: The Herbwoman's Cure
herbwoman_healer.text: {prior}, the herbwoman you protected, has broken a fever that the priests could not. The mothers of {settlement} want her honoured — and the priests want her silenced.

ignore.result: {prior} went back to her hut by the mill.

choices.label: Name her town physician
choices.result: {prior} has a salary now, and a house near the square.
choices.chronicle: {house} named the once-accused herbwoman {prior} physician of {settlement}.

choices.label: Honour her quietly
choices.result: A purse and a word of thanks.

miners_promise.title: The Miners Call in Your Promise
miners_promise.text: {prior} and the miners of {settlement} have worked the season on your word. Now they want the share you promised.

ignore.result: A broken promise. The mines fell silent again.

choices.label: Pay the promised share
choices.result: Your word is good. The miners will work for you again.

choices.label: Renege — profits were poor
choices.result: The miners curse your name in the dark.

gamekeeper_report.title: The Gamekeeper's Catch
gamekeeper_report.text: {prior}, the poacher you made gamekeeper, has broken a ring of poachers selling your deer in three towns. He brings the ringleader to you.

ignore.result: The ringleader bribed his way out.

choices.label: Reward {prior}
choices.result: The poacher-turned-keeper beams with pride.

choices.label: Fine the ring heavily
choices.result: The ring pays for every deer, twice over.

plague_contained.title: The Fever Breaks
plague_contained.text: {prior} reports that the fever in {settlement} has broken. The lower town is mourning, but the rest of the town was spared.

ignore.result: The physicians went unthanked.

choices.label: Reward the physicians
choices.result: {prior} is cheered through the streets.

choices.label: Hold a service of thanksgiving
choices.result: The temple is packed to the doors.

plague_spreads.title: The Fever Spreads
plague_spreads.text: Despite everything, the fever has burst out of the lower town of {settlement}. {prior} begs for drastic measures.

ignore.result: The fever ran its course. The graveyards filled.

choices.label: Burn the infected quarter
choices.result: Smoke hangs over {settlement} for days. The fever dies with the houses.

choices.label: Bring physicians from every town
choices.result: The fever is beaten back, at great cost.

choices.label: Let those who can flee
choices.result: Half the town empties onto the roads.

smuggling_exposed.title: Your Arrangement Exposed
smuggling_exposed.text: A customs clerk has found your name in {prior}'s smuggling ledgers. He has not yet gone to the magistrates.

ignore.result: The clerk went to the magistrates. The ledgers were read aloud.

choices.label: Pay the clerk to burn the ledgers
choices.result: The ledgers burn. The clerk buys a fine house.

choices.label: Confess and pay restitution
