bourse._comment: Underwriters, bills of exchange and the Bourse (src/systems/underwriting.js, src/systems/bills.js, src/systems/bourse.js). Balance notes in docs/economy-balance.md; the rules in GAMEPLAY_MANUAL.md → 'Underwriters, Bills & the Bourse'.

underwriting._cover: Open cover: one standing policy per kind, bought at an underwriter's office. Each day it bills a premium on what it covers that day (ships at sea, caravans on the road, stock in store, works, farms): the expected loss from the same inputs the loss sites use, times `loading`, times the claims surcharge. It attaches `attachDays` after it is opened and pays each covered loss less the deductible, up to `maxClaim` a loss.

marine.name: Hull & cargo
marine._risk: Per day at sea. Storms: the season's chance of foul weather at sea × the hull damage (in repair cost) and cargo washed overboard they bring. Hostile squadrons near the ship: their chance of stopping it × the chance it loses × hull damage and cargo seized. Events at sea (on a voyage): ships.json's eventChance a day × the share of events that batter the hull (eventHullShare, eventHullPct) or put cargo over the side (eventCargoShare × eventCargoLoss). stormChance is the season's expected storm danger at sea (measured: storms and blizzards, weighted by their seaDanger). A worn hull (below ships.json settings.leakBelow, 50%) leaks: storms wash more cargo out of it.

caravan.name: Goods on the road
caravan._risk: Per caravan per day: base, plus perRaider for each raider within raiderRadius of it and perLair for each outlaw lair within lairRadius; halved on a road-linked journey (wardens). Covers your caravans and your company's convoys.

stock.name: Stock in store
stock._risk: Each store-room's and post's own weekly theft chance (MerchantPrince.theftChance, MerchantHouses.robberyChance) × the share thieves carry off × the stock's value, billed by the day.

works.name: Works & property
works._risk: Per works per day: base × its value; a siege wears siegeWear a day (the repair bill); a crown in crisis may seize it (crisisChance a week × the salvage value). Seizure by a realm at war with you is a war risk no underwriter covers; neither is a town turning on you.

crop.name: Crops in the field
crop._risk: Per farm per day: the day's expected crop × the season's expected shortfall to weather (`seasonShortfall`) plus any blight or drought on the land now. A field with a worse record of its own (an average of its days, experienceWeight) is priced on that instead. Pays the shortfall of each day's crop against what the farm would bring in fair weather.
crop._harvest: The year's harvest (world/harvests.js): through the growing season (harvests.json → growing) each day bills the expected shortfall of the farm's region over the season's length × the farm's yearly crop — the forecast's shortfall as far as it is sure (conf), harvestPrior (a usual year's expected shortfall) where it is not. When the harvest is reckoned, the region's shortfall in the farm's crop × its yearly crop is claimed, pro rata to the days of the season the cover carried.

guild._doc: Underwriters' guilds at the great ports: their own capital pool. A guild whose capital falls below failBelow of what it started with fails: its covers lapse and its claims are paid at `recovery`. A new guild opens `refoundDays` later.

book._doc: Each underwriter also writes covers for other merchants. Every week its book earns premium (premium × book) and pays claims: lossRatio of the premium in quiet times, more for each war, blockade, pirate fleet and great storm in its waters (warLoss, blockadeLoss, pirateLoss), with noise. A banking house's desk books it all on the house's reserves (systems/finance.js); a guild on its own capital.

fraud._doc: A false claim: forged protests of loss bought through the Thieves' Guild (rank minRank or above). The forger takes forgerFee of the claim at once. Every false claim is investigated: caught with `caught` chance, less perRank for each guild rank, more perClaim for each claim of yours in the last claimsMemoryDays and bigShare for a claim near the cap. Caught: no pay, the cover is cancelled, a fine of fineMult × the claim (from your purse; what you cannot pay becomes heat), heat in the realm, the office will not insure you for banDays.

bills._doc: Bills of exchange: pay gold into one banking house and draw a bill payable at another house (or the same house's seat in another realm). fee = base + perHex × the distance between the two seats, min minFee; payable from usance days (the distance at usanceHexes a day); presented after validDays it is protested (protestFee). A thief who takes a bill can have it cashed by a forger after cashDays unless you stop it at a branch of the paying house first (stopFee). A bill on a failed house falls on the house that drew it; if that one failed too, the receivers pay `recovery`.

bourse._doc: The Bourse: an exchange in each of the `exchanges` greatest capitals. Shares in the rival merchant houses (100 each), the banking houses (1000), the player's company once floated (100) and the chartered companies (ventures and royal monopolies, 1000). Each share's fair value is its earnings over the yield the market asks of its kind (see _yields); a bank's is weighed by its vaults (reserveWeight); its price is fair × sentiment (a mean-reverting walk) × the market's mood × any mania, and the player's own trading moves it (impact, decaying by the day). Dividends are paid weekly from real profit.
bourse._yields: The yield the market asks of each kind: a share is worth its book × (1 + slope × (return on capital ÷ yield − 1)), the return a running average weighted roeWeight a week, within [minMult, maxMult] of book: 1× book at the yield asked, more above it, damped by the kind's slope (the market is wary of paying up front for growth). `priors` is the return each kind is expected to make before it has shown any: a merchant house's mining leases (systems/concessions.js) make its trade worth far more than its books.

ventures.name: The Company of the Far Isles
ventures._doc: An overseas venture under a crown's charter: it lives by new lands (Discovery: sites found and known to its crown, colonies claimed) and dies by the sea (pirates, war, a fleet lost).

ventures.name: The Royal {good} Farm of {kingdom}
ventures._doc: A crown's monopoly let to a company: its rents follow the realm's trade and prices (world/economyIndex.js); a crown deep in debt squeezes it, a crown that defaults may revoke it.

panics._doc: Market-wide falls in mood: a banking house failing, a crown defaulting or a war on an exchange's realm.

manias.name: The Isles Mania
manias.start: Fortunes are made overnight in {name} at the Bourse of {place}: every clerk and widow buys.
manias.burst: The {name} bubble has burst at the Bourse of {place}. {listing} falls by half in a morning; the banks call in their loans.

manias.name: The {good} Craze
manias.start: All {place} talks of {listing}: its shares change hands three times a day.
manias.burst: {listing} crashes at the Bourse of {place}: the craze is over and the speculators ruined.

manias.name: The Merchant Fever
manias.start: A fever for {listing} grips the Bourse of {place}; its shares are bid far above its books.
manias.burst: The fever breaks: {listing} tumbles at the Bourse of {place}.

transport._doc: Roads, canals & logistics (world/transport.js: the road segments, their quality and the haulage terms of the trade links; systems/publicWorks.js: upkeep, works, tolls). The world's roads (tile.hasRoad) are split into segments, each the road between two neighbouring settlements. A segment has a tier (track, road, paved highway), a condition 0..100, a river crossing (bridge, ford or ferry) and may be closed (a snowbound pass, a ford in flood). Nothing here draws RNG: initial conditions, washouts and closures are hashes of the world seed, the segment and the week.
transport._tiers: move: multiplier on the terrain move cost of a road hex (the player; the generated road's 0.5 is 'road'). speed: caravan speed factor. friction: the trade link's haulage factor against the old flat roadFactor 0.6 (1 = no road): a road in good repair now hauls cheaper than the old flat road (0.5), a track dearer. decay: condition lost a week; repair: condition the realm's upkeep restores a week; upkeep: gold per hex per week. crossing: the river crossing a new segment of this tier gets.
transport._tierOf: The tier a generated segment starts at: highway between two cities or capitals of one realm, track between two villages, road otherwise.
transport._haulage: The pace of a link's trade (world/transport.js applyLink -> SettlementMarket.flows). rate = (speed / refSpeed)^flowBySpeed: the share of the surplus and of the price gap a market turn moves (speed: the road's caravan speed, 0.75 over open country, 1 on a road, 1.3 on a highway, 0.8 rutted; refSpeed 0.75 = open country moves as before). keep = (speed / refSpeed)^-keepBySpeed: the stock the exporter's merchants hold back (x markets.json trade.keepDays) — reliable carts on a good road mean less held against the next delivery. Clamped to [minRate, maxRate] and [minKeep, maxKeep]. Sea links keep 1. Measured in docs/economy-balance.md (Roads: dispersion).
transport._bands: Condition bands: at or above `worn` a road works as its tier; between `ruined` and `worn` it is rutted (move x ruttedMove, friction x ruttedFriction, speed x ruttedSpeed); below `ruined` it is no better than open country.
transport._weather: Weekly wear: winter frost and spring thaw add to the decay; a realm at war wears its roads (requisitions, no road gangs); each war host or relief host standing on a road hex grinds it down (armyDamage a day). Spring mud: tracks and rutted roads cost +1 to move and their friction x mudFriction; open country links x openMud. Winter: open-country links, tracks and rutted roads x winterFriction (roads in good repair, highways and canals spared).
transport._passes: A segment over mountain, highland, snow or tundra hexes (at least minHexes) is a pass. In winter it closes when snow falls on its highest hex on the weekly check, and for all of deep winter (dayInSeason >= deepFrom) when it crosses mountain or snow. A closed pass stops the trade links over it; the player wades through at +closedMove.
transport._rivers: Crossings: a bridge carries the road (no penalty); a ford costs the player fordMove and adds fordFriction to the link, and closes in a spring flood (floodChance a week); a ferry (a washed-out bridge within ferryRange of a town) costs ferryMove, a ferryFare and ferryFriction. Bridges wash out in a storm or a spring flood: washChance a week (x washRutted when the road is rutted).
transport._terrain: Links that are not on a road: haulage friction x (base + perMove x the mean move cost of the hexes on the straight line), clamped to [min, max] (plains = 1).
transport._perish: Perishable goods spoil on the way: extra friction perDay x the haul's days, and loss x days of what moves never arrives (at most maxLoss). Haul days: distance / (landSpeed x the road's speed factor), or seaSpeed by sea, canalSpeed by canal.
transport._upkeep: Each realm pays its roads' upkeep weekly (tier upkeep x hexes, x the Royal Road-Building edict's cost) when its treasury is above floor, it missed no payment and its debt ratio is under maxDebt; at war it pays warShare of it. A paid segment is repaired, an unpaid one only decays. Roads outside any realm are kept by their towns at freeRepair a week.
transport._works: Public works (systems/publicWorks.js). goods per hex (road works) or per work; days per hex or per work; hands: land hands hired in the site town while it builds (world/townLabour.js), paid the town's land wage x wageMult a day. Goods are bought from the site town's market (and its link partners) at the going price, at most drawShare of a stock a day: a short market slows the work and its prices climb. toll: the toll rate on the value carried over it (NPC trade; caravans pay it at the gate), playerToll the fee the player pays crossing it. cond: the condition it leaves. Canals join two towns of one region within maxDist (one a port, or a river between them) and cut the link's friction to friction x; harbours cut sea links' friction x friction at either end.
transport._build: wageMult: the hands' daily pay (x the town's land wage). drawShare: most of a market's stock a work buys in a day. budgetPad: what the player puts up front beyond the estimate (the rest is refunded on completion). crownShare: the crown's cut of a foreign investor's tolls. maxPerRealm / maxPlayer: works under way at once.
transport._realms: NPC crowns weigh their roads on their weekly turn: rebuild washed-out bridges and repair ruined roads when the treasury is above repairAt; upgrade their busiest road a tier above upgradeAt (x personality; at most one every upgradeEvery days, and only a road carrying upgradeTraffic gold a day, a track counting double); build harbour works above harbourAt and dig a canal above canalAt (each at most once per harbourEvery / canalEvery days per realm; canals only between towns no good road joins, and at most canalPerTowns of the world's towns). No new works at war (repairs only), in debt (debtRatio above maxDebt) or with welfare under minWelfare. personality: multiplier on the thresholds (lower = keener).
transport._news: History kept for the heralds and the chatter (world.transport.history), at most cap records; chatterRange: hexes within which townsfolk talk of a road.
transport._counsel: The Steward points out a washed-out bridge or ford on a road carrying at least minTrade gold a market turn within radius hexes, with the estimated toll payback.
transport._render: Map colours of a road's condition (the trade map and the world map's road overlay at minZoom and above).

mints._doc: Specie, Mints & the Price Level (world/moneySupply.js, systems/mints.js). Every realm has coin in circulation (world.money.realms[id].coin), seeded at coinPerHead x its people. Each week (every `every` days) coin moves: the realms' NPC trade settles part of its balance in specie, tribute and crown loans move it, debased coin is driven out (Gresham), panics send it abroad, a little wears away, and the mints strike new coin from the gold and silver ore they buy in the realm's markets and from the player. The realm's price level follows its coin per head (x velocity: hoarding in war and panic) against the world's, smoothed and clamped, and multiplies every price in its markets together with the coin's purity (world/coinage.js). Set enabled false to switch the whole system off (every reader returns neutral). Balance: docs/economy-balance.md 'Specie, Mints & the Price Level'.
mints._level: Quantity term: the realm's price level target = (coin x velocity / people, against the world's) ^ elasticity, clamped to [min, max]; the level moves `smoothing` of the way there each week. Kept narrow on purpose: a whole-basket gap between two realms is a gap every trader can work.
mints._velocity: Hoarding: a realm at war hoards `war` of its coin, one with a run on its bank or a fresh crown default `panic` more; velocity moves `adjust` of the way to its target each week (never below `floor`).
mints._trade: Specie flows from trade: the NPC traders' goods crossing a border (their value at the exporter's price, left on each trade link by world/settlementMarket.js) are settled `specie` in coin, the rest in bills and kind. hume: the price-specie flow: a realm with less coin per head than a trading partner is cheaper, sells it more, and wins back hume x the gap in log coin per head (unclamped) x the smaller of the two realms' coin a week from it, so a drained realm recovers, a realm whose mines pour out coin spends it abroad, and a persistent deficit settles a few points under the norm. maxShare: most of a realm's coin that leaves it in one week by trade.
mints._transfers: Share of a payment between crowns that moves coin in circulation: tribute and capitulation indemnities (raised from the people, spent by the victor), crown loans from a banking house in another realm (and their repayment). maxShare caps one transfer at that share of the payer's coin.
mints._gresham: Bad money drives out good: a realm whose coin is debased loses rate x (1 - purity) of its coin a week to its sounder trading partners (merchants hoard and export the old full-weight pieces).
mints._flight: Coin flight: a realm with a run on one of its banks, or a crown default in the last `defaultDays`, loses `rate` of its coin a week to the soundest realm it trades with.
mints._wear: Coin lost a week: worn, clipped, buried, carried off to far lands. The mints must keep striking to hold the level.
mints._drift: The invisible balance: pilgrims, mercenaries' pay, smugglers and travellers carry coin from realms with much of it to realms with little, whether they trade or not. Each week a realm's coin moves by ratio ^ -drift (its coin per head against the world's), the total kept, so a realm with no trading partners is not stranded at the clamp.
mints._income: The crown's tax yield follows the coin about (KingdomAI.incomeMultiplier x level ^ elasticity, clamped): a realm drained of coin collects less, one awash in it more. The crowns' daily income is otherwise a ledger of their realms' commerce; see docs/economy-balance.md for why it is only partly backed.
mints._mint: The mints. Each week every realm's mint buys gold and silver ore from its markets where the stock stands above `keep` x the market's target (at most weeklyFine of fine value, x the mint policy's draw), plus what the player sold it. fine: coin a unit of bullion holds at full purity (gold ore, 40g base, holds 36; silver ore, 18g, holds 16; a gold bar, 150g, 140): the mint is a deep buyer at about base price, better than the stalls when the metal is plentiful, worse when it is scarce. Coin struck = fine / purity (a debased mint strikes more coin from the same bullion); the crown keeps the seigniorage, the rest goes into circulation. The player is paid fine x (1 - seigniorage) x the realm's price multiplier, never more than `askCap` of the open market's ask for that good here (no buy-here-sell-to-the-mint loop), up to playerWeeklyFine a week per mint. remint: share of the foreign coin that came in during the week (trade, tribute, loans, Gresham, flight) brought to the mint to be restruck as the realm's own, for the same seigniorage: most of a mint's profit in a realm without mines.
mints._debase: Debasement through the mint (systems/finance.js debase): the crown recoins the circulating coin at the lower standard and keeps the difference; the swollen coin raises prices on top of the purity term, and Gresham's law starts draining the good coin abroad. coinShare: share of the recoined surplus that enters circulation.
mints._recoinage: A recoinage edict calls in the old coin and strikes it anew at full purity. Holders get back purity + crownShare x (1 - purity) of each piece (the coin in circulation shrinks: prices fall); the crown pays crownShare x (1 - purity) x the coin from its treasury, and the realm's stability moves `stability` (relief at honest coin less the grumbling at the exchange). A crown out of trouble (debt ratio under maxDebtRatio, treasury above treasuryCover x the cost) proclaims one by itself; the player as ruler may at any time. Not again within cooldown days.
mints._exchange: Money changers: carrying gold into a realm whose coin is of another purity costs perPurity x the purity gap of the gold carried (at most max), when the purse holds at least minGold and was not assayed in the last cooldownDays (a traveller criss-crossing a border pays once, not at every crossing). Recorded as 'exchange' in the ledger. The rate shown between two coins is their silver content (purity) ratio.
mints._concession: Leasing a mint: the player pays fee = feeShare x the mint's average weekly seigniorage (last seignHistory weeks) x share x the term's weeks up front into the treasury, and takes `share` of the seigniorage each week for termDays. Not to be had while at war with the realm, from a mint that struck nothing, or while another lease runs.
mints._counterfeit: Passing false coin (Thieves' Guild members of rank minRank and above, in a settlement of a realm): stake [minStake, maxStake] of good coin in silvered copper, passed for gain x the stake on success. Caught with chance base + heatPer x heat - rankCut x rank, x (looser + (1 - looser) x the coin's purity): a debased coin is easier to fake. Caught: the stake is lost, a fine of fineShare x the stake, heat +caughtHeat, and arrest with arrestChance. Passed: heat +passHeat, and the false coin swells the realm's coin. Once every cooldown days.
mints._news: The heralds and the townsfolk: a coin shortage (level at or below shortAt and falling) or a flood of coin (level at or above floodAt and rising) is news once per realm every gapWeeks; recoinages always. Counsel: warn the ruler when their realm's level is outside [shortAt, floodAt] or its coin is debased; tell the player when bullion in their packs would fetch at least bullionGain over the market at a mint within mintRadius hexes.

fiscal._doc: The Crown's Purse (src/systems/fiscal.js, src/world/crownBooks.js). Each realm keeps real books: taxes come out of its towns' purses (economy.gold, where their production and trade income is credited) and wages and upkeep go back into them, so taxation moves gold, never makes it. Revenue lines: land tax (the peasants' earnings x the harvest, plus part of the town's production gold), poll or hearth tax (taxable heads: peasants, artisans, merchants; clergy and nobles exempt), excise (the artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade income), customs (systems/tradePolicy.js and the crown's tolls), the demesne (the crown's own estates: a share of production gold) and monopolies, seigniorage (world/moneySupply.js), tax farms sold, the extraordinary levy, offices and crown land sold. Expense lines: army wages (field pay at war), court and administration, roads and works (world/transport.js, systems/publicWorks.js), debt service (systems/finance.js), the famine dole and granaries, the ruler's purse (systems/throne.js). Everything else that moved the treasury lands under 'other'. Set enabled false to fall back to the old income (the growth of the towns' gold). Balance: docs/economy-balance.md 'The Crown's Purse'.
fiscal._levels: Tax levels: each multiplies the base rates. NPC crowns pick one level for all three taxes; a ruler sets each tax apart in the Treasury panel.

light.label: Light
light.blurb: The people prosper and stay; the chests fill slowly.

heavy.label: Heavy
heavy.blurb: The chests fill; the realm grumbles and the poor drift away.

crushing.label: Crushing
crushing.blurb: Every last penny: unrest, flight, tax revolts.

fiscal._rates: Base rates at the standard level: land (share of the peasants' earnings and of landProd x the town's production gold), poll (gold per taxable head a day), excise (share of the artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade income).
fiscal._sales: rates.sales: the land tax's share of the coin a town took for the goods it sold to other towns (economy.fySales, world/settlementMarket.js flows and the caravans), x the land tax's level; rates.hoard: a day's share of the coin a town holds past hoardReserve a head (the assessors find what the town sits on), x the land tax's level. 2026-11, when the towns' coin became real: the countryside sells the capitals their food, and the crown's tax on those sales is what brings the coin back to the capital (in the soldiers' and clerks' pay).
fiscal._collectEvery: The collectors come round each town once every collectEvery days (staggered by town) and take every day's dues since.
fiscal._fallback: Earnings per head a day for a town whose labour record is not set up yet.
fiscal._demesne: The crown's own estates: `share` of the towns' production gold (the capital's counts `capital` times). Selling crown land in a crisis gives up `crisis.land.share` of what is left for `crisis.land.days` of its yield; it never falls below `min`.
fiscal._army: Wages: pay a day per soldier (x warPay while at war, x the realm's upkeep bonuses and military-spending events), bounty per new recruit. Pay levels for a ruler (NPC crowns pay full, half when broke): mult on the wages, cap on the army the realm keeps, stability. Unpaid soldiers desert after desert.afterDays: the army the realm can keep falls capPerDay a day (never below capMin) until they are paid.

army._spendWeights: Where the army's wages are spent (systems/fiscal.js _spendBack): the towns the collectors visited, by their people x this weight for their kind (the capital's garrison and the towns' quarter more men than the villages). 2026-11: added when the towns' coin became real; by people alone the villages took the soldiers' pay and the capitals, which buy the villages' food, ran dry.

half.label: Half pay
half.blurb: Cheap, and the men drift home.

generous.label: Generous
generous.blurb: Loyal regiments, and more men take the shilling.

fiscal._court: Court and administration a day: base + perTown x towns + perHead x people, x the court level. A frugal court breeds corruption (corruption a day), a lavish one is loved.

frugal.label: Frugal
frugal.blurb: Fewer clerks, and those who stay take their own cut.

fiscal._corruption: 0-1. Unpaid officials raise it unpaidGain a day; it decays `decay` a day while they are paid. It leaks `leak` x corruption of the taxes before they reach the treasury, and adds to the people's burden. Selling offices adds officesSale.
fiscal._burden: The burden the people feel, on the labour model's scale (base 0.15 = the customary dues; world/townLabour.js welfare falls by (burden - 0.15) x taxWeight per stratum): base x the realm's tax index (land, poll and excise levels weighted), + farmPerSqueeze x (a farmer's squeeze - 1), + corruption x `corruption`.
fiscal._stability: Stability target term 'Taxes & pay': -(tax index - 1) x perLevel, -arrearsPerDay a day the soldiers and officials go unpaid (at most arrearsCap), -corruption x `corruption`, plus the pay and court levels' own.
fiscal._npc: NPC crowns review their taxes every `every` days (staggered): from the standard level, + bias by personality, + 1 at war, + 1 below reserveLow days of spending in the chests (+2 below lowDays), - 1 above reserveHigh (-2 above highDays), + 1 with soldiers unpaid, - 1 when stability is under unrestAt or a tax revolt broke out in the last revoltDays; they move one step a review. Below halfPayDays of spending with soldiers unpaid they go to half pay.
fiscal._coin: Taxes are paid in coin out of circulation and wages paid back into it (world/moneySupply.js 'fisc' flow): each week the realm's coin moves by -share x (collected - spent), at most maxShare of its coin.
fiscal._farms: Tax farming. A crown short of money (below needDays of spending, deficitWeeks weeks in deficit, at war below warDays, or with its soldiers unpaid) auctions, at most once every `cooldown` days, the taxes of one town (not its capital; at most maxShare of its towns) for term days: the lot's estimate is the town's recent crown taxes x term; a banking house bids discount (a hash in the range) of it, the player may outbid by `outbid`; the lot closes after `close` days. The farmer collects the town's taxes x squeeze (less collectCost) in place of the crown. Player squeeze levels: mult, reputation lost in the realm a day, the town's happiness a day. A house squeezes `bankSqueeze`.

gentle.label: Gentle
gentle.blurb: Collect what is owed and no more.

harsh.label: Harsh
harsh.blurb: Bailiffs and distraint. Hated, and rich.

fiscal._revolts: Tax revolts, weekly per town (a hash roll, no RNG): pressure = (burden - burdenAt) x perBurden + (welfareAt - the peasants' welfare) x perWelfare + farmed (if farmed), each at least 0; chance = min(max, pressure x chance). A revolt withholds the town's taxes for `days`, costs it `happiness`, the realm `stability`, and drives a tax farmer's men out.
fiscal._crisis: Ways out of a fiscal crisis besides borrowing, the levy, debasement and default (systems/finance.js chooses): selling offices raises `offices.days` of revenue (corruption + corruption.officesSale); selling crown land raises `land.days` of the yield of `land.share` of the demesne.
fiscal._explain: What the Treasury panel (src/ui/actionMenu/treasury.js, via src/ui/actionMenu/taxGuide.js) tells the player each tax, level and budget line is. {pct:path} prints a number of this file as a percent, {num:path} as it stands, {c100:path} times 100 (a sum per hundred), {x:path} as a multiplier: the prose follows the tuning. Per-level effects (revenue x, burden and stability) are computed from levels/burden/stability, not written here. Keep each line to what the code reads.

explain.intro: Every coin the crown takes comes out of its towns' purses (the coin their people hold), and its wages go back into them. Collectors call on each town every {num:collectEvery} days and take every day's dues since; a town whose purse is empty pays only what it has, and a town in revolt pays nothing for {num:revolts.days} days.
explain.collection: Every tax is then × the realm's collection (the steward, stability, blockades, events) and less {pct:corruption.leak} × corruption kept by the officials.

land.name: Land tax
land.who: The countryside and the town's trade: the peasants who work the land, and the town as a whole for what it makes and sells away.
land.on: The peasants' earnings (swelled or cut by the harvest), the town's production, the coin it took for goods sold to other towns, and the coin it sits on.
land.how: {pct:rates.land} of the peasants' earnings × the harvest (×0.5 to ×1.5), + {pct:rates.land} of {pct:rates.landProd} of the town's production gold, + {pct:rates.sales} of the coin from goods sold to other towns, + {pct:rates.hoard} a day of the coin it holds past {num:rates.hoardReserve}g a head. All × the land tax's level.
land.weight: It is {pct:burden.weights.land} of the realm's tax index: a step on the land tax moves the burden and stability twice as far as a step on the hearth tax or the excise.

poll.name: Hearth tax
poll.who: Every working head: peasants and artisans count once, merchants {x:pollWeights.merchants}; clergy and nobles are exempt.
poll.on: Heads, not earnings: a poor town pays as much per person as a rich one.
poll.how: {c100:rates.poll}g a day for every 100 taxable heads, × the hearth tax's level.
poll.weight: It is {pct:burden.weights.poll} of the realm's tax index.

excise.name: Excise
excise.on: The artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade income.
excise.how: {pct:rates.excise} of the artisans' earnings + {pct:rates.excise} of the town's trade income, × the excise's level.
excise.weight: It is {pct:burden.weights.excise} of the realm's tax index.

explain.levels: Each level multiplies that tax's take: 🍃 Light {x:levels.light.mult}, ⚖️ Standard {x:levels.standard.mult}, 💰 Heavy {x:levels.heavy.mult}, ⛓️ Crushing {x:levels.crushing.mult}. NPC crowns set all three to one level; a ruler sets each apart.
raise: Revenue: that tax's take × the level (paid only from what the towns' purses hold).
The people's burden rises (base {pct:burden.base} × the tax index). Every class's welfare falls by (burden − 15%) × its weight, so people drift along the trade roads to towns that treat them better.

Tax revolts: above a burden of {pct:revolts.burdenAt} (or where the peasants are hard-pressed), each town risks a revolt each week (at most {pct:revolts.max}): no taxes for {num:revolts.days} days, −{num:revolts.happiness} happiness there, −{num:revolts.stability} stability.
Stability: the realm's target falls {num:stability.perLevel} for each whole step the tax index stands above Standard (and rises as much below it).
Coin: taxes take coin out of circulation and wages put it back; each week the realm's coin moves by {pct:coin.share} of the difference.
explain.lower: Lowering does the reverse: less gold, a lighter burden (people stay and settlers come), fewer revolts, a steadier realm. Light taxes can leave the army unpaid: soldiers unpaid more than {num:army.desert.afterDays} days desert.
explain.army: Army wages: {num:army.pay}g a day per soldier (×{num:army.warPay} at war, × the realm's upkeep bonuses), + {num:army.bounty}g for each new recruit, × the pay level. Paid before the court. Soldiers spend it where they are quartered.
explain.court: Court & administration: {num:court.base}g + {num:court.perTown}g a town + {num:court.perHead}g a head, a day, × the court level. The clerks spend it in the capital.

terms.burden: The people's burden: what the taxes weigh on them ({pct:burden.base} is the customary due). Raised by the tax levels, a tax farmer's squeeze and corruption.
terms.stability: The 'Taxes & pay' part of the realm's stability: the tax levels, unpaid days (up to −{num:stability.arrearsCap}), corruption (−{num:stability.corruption} at 100%), and the army-pay and court levels.
terms.corruption: The share of officials on the take: {pct:corruption.leak} of it leaks out of the taxes. It grows while the clerks go unpaid, under a frugal court and when offices are sold, and fades while they are paid.
terms.demesne: The crown's own estates: their share of the land's production gold (the capital's counts {x:demesne.capital}). Selling crown land shrinks it for good.
terms.reserve: Days in hand: how many days of spending the chests would cover.

lines.land: The land tax: on the peasants' earnings (by the harvest), the town's production and its sales to other towns.
lines.poll: The hearth tax: so much a working head (merchants more, clergy and nobles exempt).
lines.excise: The excise: on the artisans' earnings and the merchants' trade.
lines.customs: Tariffs on goods crossing the border, and the crown's road, bridge and canal tolls.
lines.demesne: The crown's own estates (a share of the land's gold) and its monopolies (licences, the post).
lines.seigniorage: The mint's profit on striking and re-striking the realm's coin.
lines.farms: Lump sums paid by tax farmers who bought the right to collect a town's taxes.
lines.levy: An extraordinary levy: an extra share on every tax while it runs (a crown deep in debt), and forced gifts from its subjects.
lines.sales: One-off sales: offices, crown land, licences and petitions, and surplus arms sold off.
lines.army: Soldiers' daily pay and recruits' bounties, the fleet's upkeep, field costs, and wages the crown pays its commissioned officers (you, when you serve).
lines.arms: Weapons, shields, helms, harness and arrows the crown buys from its towns' markets to arm its soldiers.
lines.court: The household, officers and clerks (by the realm's size), and the upkeep of royal edicts.
lines.works: Building and keeping up roads, bridges, canals and other public works.
lines.debt: Interest and repayments on the crown's loans from the banking houses.
lines.dole: Famine relief: grain bought for the hungry and to stock the granaries.
lines.purse: The ruler's own cut of the crown's revenue (the royal levy: your gold, if you rule).
lines.loans: Gold borrowed from the banking houses (not income: it must be paid back).
lines.debase: Gold made by debasing the coin (prices rise after).
lines.other: Everything else that moved the treasury (events, tribute, temples, licences): the books always balance.

fiscal._smoothing: Daily smoothing of the books' average revenue and spending (the Finance tick's income and the reserve).

estates._doc: Land, Estates & the Putting-Out System (world/estates.js model, systems/landMarket.js land market, systems/puttingOut.js cottage industry). The farmland about every settlement (the grain, flax and vines of world/harvests.js and its market profile) is split into the peasants' own freeholds and commons (1 - estateShare) and a few estates (manors, granges, halls) held by the crown, noble houses, the church, the town's burghers or the merchant houses. An estate is a share of the town's farmland, not extra land: its crops are the town's own, already in its market, so an estate changes the market only by what its holder changes (drainage and marl raise its soil, enclosure turns its fields to sheep, the cottagers' winter work draws hands from the fields out of season). Tenants pay rent once a month: coin (a fixed sum on the estate's usual crop, the tenants bear a bad year) or a share of the crop (rent follows the harvest and its price). Land is valued at its expected net rent over the realm's land rate (systems/finance.js bond rates), and changes hands: indebted nobles and crowns in crisis sell, the merchant houses, burghers and church buy, war cedes and conquest confiscates, dowries and bequests pass estates on. Balance: docs/economy-balance.md 'Land, Estates & the Putting-Out System'.
estates._derive: Estates per settlement by size (count); estateShare of the farmland is held in estates (the rest is freehold and commons, which no one sells); householdSize people to a household. Shares between a town's estates are a hash of the seed and the town (weights 0.6-1.4). Holders: the first estate of a capital is the crown's demesne; the rest by hash with weights by size (independent towns: the crown's weight goes to the burghers). nobles: noble houses per realm (names: hash of the realm and the house's number).
estates._crops: What an estate grows, valued at base price x sqrt(the town's scarcity) (clamped scarcity): the town's farm goods from its market profile (grain, flax, wine; the harvest in force already counted). Enclosed land runs sheep: wool = woolYield x the crops' base value / wool's base price a day, with sheepHands of the tenants kept on as shepherds.
estates._rent: Share of the gross crop the tenants pay by rent level; enclosed land pays `enclosed` (a grazier's lease). capacity: most of a month's crop tenants can hand over (a coin rent above it falls into arrears). steward: the bailiff's and steward's cut. avgAlpha: how fast the usual crop a coin rent is fixed on follows the actual one (a month's step). Loyalty (0-100) drifts `loyaltyStep` of the way to its target each month: the level's target, +kindBonus for a share of the crop, -arrearsHit in a month of arrears, +putOutBonus where the cottagers earn piece wages, an enclosure costs enclosureHit. Collection: 70% of what is due at loyalty 0, all of it from loyalty 75; below strikeBelow a hash roll strikeChance withholds the month's rent. High rents drive households away: flight x (1 + (40 - loyalty)/40) of them a month, to the nearest town; mood: below sullenBelow the town loses sullenMood happiness a month, above contentAbove gains contentMood (the player's estates only; NPC landlords keep customary rents). Below riotBelow a hash roll riotChance raises a rent riot (riotMood).
estates._press: Pressing tenants for their arrears (the player's estates): the bailiff collects up to `share` of what is owed (no more than a month's capacity of the crop, nor than the town's coin), once every `everyDays`; it costs `loyalty`. If loyalty falls below riotBelow, a hash roll (riotChance x the shortfall below riotBelow / riotBelow + 0.1, at most riotMax) raises a rent riot: nothing is collected, the town's mood falls, and riotForgive of the arrears are written off. In a good month (no arrears that month) tenants pay back arrearsShare of their spare capacity (the crop above what was due) by collection; the bailiff then writes off arrearsForgive of what is left.
estates._value: Land price = expected yearly net rent (at the estate's own rent, mode and loyalty) / the land rate. Land rate = base + bondShare x (the realm's bond rate - bondRef) (systems/finance.js), +war while the realm fights, +unrest while its stability is under 35, within [min, max]; free towns pay `free`. Buyer's duty: the crown takes `duty` of a purchase. Offers for an estate not on the market: the holder asks value x premium (indebted holders x distressAsk); the church never sells (mortmain), a crown only to a buyer of at least crownRep reputation. A quick sale to the richest buyer about fetches quickSale x value; no buyer with the purse for it: it goes on the market at listAsk x value.
estates._npc: The holders' purses (notional: their rents are not drawn from anywhere, but every estate that changes hands between them, the player and the crowns moves real gold from the buyer's purse to the seller's, or a crown's treasury). Each month a holder spends spend[kind] of its rents (nobles x 1 +/- extravagance by a hash, + warLevy of them while their realm is at war); a shortfall is debt, carrying debtRate a month. Nobles live a little beyond their rents (spend 1.08). A holder whose debt passes distressAt x the value of its land puts its cheapest estate on the market at distressPrice x value. A crown deep in debt (its debt past crownSellAt x what it can carry, or its treasury empty at war) sells one with crownChance a month at crownPrice. Houses and burghers earn houseIncome / townIncome a day from trade besides their rents. Listings wait `wait` days for a buyer (the player first), then the richest purse of a house, burghers of the town, noble of the realm or (churchBuys of the time) the church takes it; unsold after `relist` days the price drops relistCut, withdrawn under withdrawAt x value. Yearly at sowing: bequest (a noble with two or more estates leaves one to the church), dowry (per realm: a noble estate passes to another noble house), and nobles and houses enclose where wool is dear (woolAbove) and grain cheap (grainBelow), npcEnclose a year.
estates._war: Peace terms: a realm that loses a war cedes cedeChance of the time its best crown estate to the victor's crown. Conquest: when a town changes realm, the old realm's crown and noble estates there pass to the new crown; the player's are confiscated when their reputation with the new realm is under confiscateBelow or they are at war with it.
estates._works: Improvements the player pays for (cost per tenant household, at least `min`; the hands' wages, wageShare of it, go to the town): drain (once: soil +soil), marl (soil +soil, wearing off `wear` a year; again once less than `again` is left), enclose (sheep: the households but sheepHands leave for the nearest town of its size or larger, an enclosure riot with chance (60 - loyalty)/60 within [riotMin, riotMax]), relet (undo an enclosure). Soil is capped at soilMax.
estates._dowry: Settling an estate on a realm's nobility as a dowry: reputation +value/perRep (at most maxRep) and House Prestige +value/perPrestige (at most maxPrestige). Holding land: +prestige a month per estate (at most prestigeMax), the House's standing as landed gentry.
estates._puttingOut: The putting-out system (systems/puttingOut.js). Merchants (the NPC houses and the player) put out raw wool and flax to the cottagers about a town, who spin and weave at home for a piece rate: cheaper than a guild workshop (guildRate of the cloth's base price a unit), slower, and of varying quality. Rural households: the town's peasants / householdSize x rural[type]; slack[season]: the share who take work (winter idle, harvest busy); each spins and weaves perHousehold units of fibre a day. The player's batches share npcShare's remainder of the capacity. Goods: input -> output at ratio x quality (quality: a hash in [qMin, qMax] + rates[].quality). Rates: piece wage = share x the cloth's base price a unit (paid up front, to the town's households), speed (more take the work), quality. Out of winter the work draws hands from the fields: away[season] of the households' work is field time lost (the town's crops x 1 - drawn share x landSensitivity). Guilds: in a town whose weavers' guild holds a royal charter, collection risks the guild's officers (chartered.chance: they seize `seize` of the cloth and fine `fine` of its worth, the feud grows by feud); an unchartered guild only fines (open.*). Journeymen and up of the guild are let be. NPC putting-out: weekly per town (none where the guild is chartered): where the cloth fetches more than the fibre and the piece rate (minMargin of the cloth's worth), npcShare of the capacity works the fibre above npcKeep x its target, delivered a week later. Uncollected cloth waits holdDays.
estates._map: Where the estates show on the world map (world/estates.js fieldHexes, ui/renderer/features.js renderRuralSites): an estate is a share of its town's farmland, not a hex of its own, so each is drawn on a free hex of `terrain` within `reach` of its town (nearest first, then a hash; never a settlement, a point of interest or a hinterland site). sprites: the variants for a working estate, enclosed: for one turned mostly (>= enclosedAt) to sheep; the format is data/hinterland.json `sprites`.
estates._counsel: The Steward's Counsel: estates on the market within saleRadius hexes at no more than bargainAt x their value that the player can afford; the player's tenants restless under restlessBelow loyalty.

infant: a cold that settled in the chest
old: old age
a long sleep in the night
a failing heart
the weight of years
winter: the lung-rot of a hard winter

findText.lair: Take the caravan's strongbox back from the outlaws of {target}
findText.foe: Run down {target} and recover the caravan's strongbox

missing_caravan.returnText: Bring the strongbox back to {giver} in {town}
missing_caravan.handIn: *pries open the lid* It's all here. You've saved my season — here, as promised.

alt.label: Keep the strongbox ({gold} gold inside)
alt.text: You kept {giver}'s strongbox and its {gold} gold.
alt.grievance: I heard you found my strongbox — and kept it. Thief.

spice_supplier.deliverText: Carry the letter of terms to {person}, {role} of {target}
spice_supplier.recipientLine: *breaks the seal and reads* Terms from {giver}, is it? Tell them I'll deal — here is my answer.
spice_supplier.handIn: *reads the reply and grins* We have a bargain! You're a born go-between.

findText.lair: Clear out the outlaw lair of {target}
findText.foe: Break {target}, who camp in the woods nearby

bandit_camp.handIn: *lets out a long breath* Done? Truly? The captain will hear of this — and so will the town.

lost_report.fetchText: Ask {person} of {target}, who picked up a dropped report at the tavern
lost_report.returnText: Bring the patrol report back to {giver} in {town}
lost_report.holderLine: *fishes in a pocket* This? Found it under a bench. Thought it looked official — take it, I want no trouble.
lost_report.handIn: *snatches it and tucks it away* The captain need never know. I owe you, friend.

alt.label: Hand the report to the captain instead (40 gold reward)
alt.text: You turned {giver}'s lost report in to the captain.
alt.grievance: You gave that report to the captain. I was docked a month's pay.

findText.foe: Hunt down {target}, who have been killing the livestock

livestock_killer.returnText: Tell {giver} in {town} the beasts are dead
livestock_killer.handIn: *wipes eyes* No more dead lambs in the morning. Bless you, bless you.

missing_son.handIn: *throws arms around {person}* You brought them home! I'll never be able to repay you.

alt.label: Let {person} go
alt.text: {person} begged you not to take them back, and you let them go.
alt.grievance: You found my child and let them walk away? You should have brought them home.

stolen_relic.handIn: *kneels and kisses the relic* It is home. The faithful will sing your name tonight.

alt.label: Sell the relic to a collector ({gold} gold)
alt.text: You sold the shrine's relic for {gold} gold.
alt.grievance: The relic was sold — and by you. The gods see everything.

findText.site: Lay the dead to rest in {target}

restless_dead.returnText: Tell {giver} in {town} the graves are quiet
restless_dead.handIn: *makes the holy sign* The graves are quiet. Our people may visit their dead again.

rare_ore.handIn: *turns the ore in the firelight* Now THAT is metal. I'll make you something worthy of it.

findText.foe: Track down {target}, who stole the knight's sword

stolen_sword.returnText: Bring the sword back to {giver} in {town}
stolen_sword.handIn: *runs a thumb down the edge* Not a nick on it. My name is saved — and you have a friend at this forge.

alt.label: Keep the sword for yourself
alt.grievance: You've the knight's sword on your hip, I hear. My sword. My name.

findText.lair: Take the locket back from the outlaws of {target}
findText.foe: Run down {target} and take the locket back

lost_locket.returnText: Bring the locket back to {giver} in {town}
lost_locket.handIn: *clutches the locket to their chest* Oh... it's really her locket. Thank you. Thank you.

alt.label: Sell the locket to a fence ({gold} gold)
alt.text: You sold {giver}'s grandmother's locket for {gold} gold.
alt.grievance: They say you sold my grandmother's locket to a fence. How could you?

hermit_medicine.returnText: Tell {giver} in {town} the medicine was delivered
hermit_medicine.recipientLine: *takes the pouch with shaking hands* Medicine... from {giver}? The fever has had me a week. Thank them for me.
hermit_medicine.handIn: *sighs with relief* Delivered, and in time? You're a good soul.

rival_documents.holderLine: *eyes you coolly* Papers? I keep nothing that concerns you.
rival_documents.handIn: *glances through the pages and smiles thinly* Discreet and effective. My family will remember this.

alt.label: Return the documents to their owner instead (100 gold)
alt.text: You sold {giver}'s scheme back to its target.
alt.grievance: You played me false and took my rival's coin. I shan't forget it.

deliver_challenge.recipientLine: *reads, and flushes red* A challenge? Tell {giver} I accept — and I name the day.
deliver_challenge.handIn: *reads the answer with relish* So the cur accepts. My house's honour will be seen to.

ancient_ruins.handIn: *listens wide-eyed* Just as I dreamed! Here — my share of the finding is yours.

bounty_target.handIn: *counts out the coin* Half the bounty, fair and square. Good hunting.

npcKnowledge._doc: What each kind of townsperson knows of the realm and the town (systems/npcKnowledge.js). `topics` in the order they speak of them; the first `sure` they know for certain, the rest is hearsay (a band may be off by one, said with a hedge). `places` = how much they know of the land about the town.
hedges: , if the talk at the well is true

sure: I'll tell you how things stand.
hearsay: Well, I only know what I hear.
guarded: I don't say much to strangers.
Not much I care to tell you.

army: barely an army worth the name
the greatest host of any realm

favour._repay: A favour's coin is a loan (mem.owed): repaid within repayDays it warms them by repaidWarmth (late: lateWarmth); asked after past due, they cool by overdueCold once.

wideKnowledge._comment: What townsfolk know of the land about (NpcKnowledge.aboutTown): outlaw lairs within lairRadius, an old place within siteRadius; with expertise places >= wideAt (a guard or traveller, liked enough) they know lairs within wideLairRadius and two old places within wideSiteRadius.

rebuff._doc: Who will not answer the player. Below refuseBelow disposition (or holding a grudge) they always turn the player away; below grudgingBelow, grudgingChance% of the time. Each rebuffed question costs pester disposition. lines by mood (grudge: {victim}); topics add lines for hostile/cold moods per question: news, town, realm, folk, family, people, work.

grudge: After what you did to {victim}? Ask me nothing. Ever.
*spits* You want news? Here's news — {victim} is gone, and it's on you.
I'll tell you nothing. Not for {victim}'s sake, not for coin. Get out.
hostile: Shove off.
Go and bother somebody else.
*turns their back on you*
Get out of my sight before I call the watch.
Ask me again and see what happens.
I'd sooner talk to a dog.
Clear off. You're not welcome here.
cold: I've nothing to say to you.
Find someone else to pester.
*folds arms* Not to you, I don't.
Why would I tell you anything?
Can't you see I'm busy? Go on, off with you.
That's none of your business.
wary: Don't know, don't care. Ask someone else.
*eyes you* I keep my own counsel with strangers like you.

news: News? Not for the likes of you.
Whatever I've heard, you'll not hear it from me.
town: Find your own way round. I'm no guide for you.
You'll learn this place soon enough — or better, leave it.
realm: Politics is for people I trust. That's not you.
folk: What happens to folk here is no business of yours.
family: Leave my family out of it.
You stay away from my kin, you hear?
people: I don't gossip with the likes of you.
What I think of my neighbours stays between me and them.
work: Help? From you? I'd rather go without.

road._doc: Out on the open road (no town on the hex) — systems/npcKnowledge.js aboutRoad and roadGreeting. Everything said is read from the world: the roadhouse (its name, keeper, rooms, how well it's kept), whose land it is and what kind, where the road runs (traced along the road to the towns it reaches, with the way and the days), outlaws and old places near, and the season. keeper: the one who keeps the house speaks of it as theirs; traveler: where they've come from and where they're bound (the two towns the road joins); anyone else of what they see. {house} {keeper} {town} {from} {to} {dir} {days} {realm} {land} {ruler} {lair} {leader} {site} {rooms} — filled in. days: how a walk is put, by hexes ([max hexes, words]).

keeper: Come in off the road. You'll want a bed, or a bowl, or both.
Shut the door behind you, the wind gets in. Welcome to {house}.
Another one off the road. Sit, sit — there's stew on.
Mind the step. Not many come by this late in the {season}.
traveler: Another soul on the road. Where are you bound?
Well met. Good to see a face that isn't a tree.
Sit if you like. I don't bite.
any: Road-weary, are you? Aren't we all.
*looks you over* You're not from round here. Nobody is, out here.

house: This is {house}. Mine — or the bank's, some winters.
{house}, this is. I've kept it {years} years now.
You're in {house}. {rooms} rooms, a roof that mostly keeps the rain out, and the only fire for miles.

good: The beds are clean and the ale's honest. Folk ride out of their way to stop here.
fair: Nothing fancy, but nobody's died in their sleep. Not lately.
poor: I'll not lie to you — it's seen better days. So have I.

why: Folk walking from {from} to {to} need somewhere to stop. That's all a roadhouse is.
Halfway between {from} and {to}, give or take. That's what keeps the doors open.

journey: I've come up from {from}, bound for {to}. {daysTo} yet, if my feet hold.
On my way to {to}. Left {from} {daysFrom} back.
I'm walking to {to}. Came by way of {from} — wouldn't recommend it.
nowhere: I'm not sure where I'm bound. Away, mostly.

house: {house} — {keeper} keeps it. Decent enough place to break a journey.

realm: This is {realm} land. {ruler}'s, for what that's worth out here.
We're in {realm} — though the crown's men seldom ride this far.
none: No crown holds this stretch. Nobody taxes you out here — and nobody comes when you scream.

terrain.forest: Forest both sides of the road; you can't see ten paces in.
terrain.hills: Hill country. Every mile's uphill, both ways.
terrain.mountains: High country — the passes close when the snow comes.
terrain.plains: Open country. You see weather coming a day off.
terrain.grassland: Open grassland, mile on mile of it.
terrain.swamp: Marsh all round. Stay on the road or the bog has you.
terrain.desert: Dry country. Carry water, whatever they tell you.
terrain.tundra: Cold country. The ground's iron half the year.
terrain.jungle: Jungle pressing in. The road gets narrower every season.
terrain.beach: Close by the sea — you can smell it.

both: The road runs {dirA} to {townA}, {daysA}, and {dirB} to {townB}, {daysB}.
Go {dirA} and it's {townA}, {daysA}. Go {dirB} and it's {townB}, {daysB}. Nothing much between.
one: Follow the road {dirA} and you'll come to {townA}, {daysA}.
off: There's no proper road here. {townA}'s the nearest place, {daysA} {dirA}.

raids: Watch yourself. Riders out of {lair} work this road{leaderBit}. Travel by daylight.
Outlaws out of {lair}, {dir} of here{leaderBit}. They've hit carts on this road.
quiet: They say there's an outlaw camp at {lair}, {dir} of here. Quiet lately. That worries me more.
none: The road's quiet enough. Wolves, now and then.

site: There's {site} {dir}, off the road. People go looking. Not all of them come back past here.

Spring: Spring rains turn the road to soup. Mind the ruts.
Summer: Summer's the busy time — carts and drovers every day.
Autumn: Autumn now. Folk hurry to get where they're going before the snow.
Winter: Winter. Hardly a soul on the road — you're brave or desperate.

days: the best part of a week

townLife._doc: How townsfolk spend their day on the town map (world/innerMap/townLife.js). Folk spawn and go about only within the town (its streets, edgeMargin tiles clear of the map's edge). watch: the fewest guards a place keeps (townsfolk guards count toward it; the rest are the lord's watchmen); nightWatchShare of them keep the night (and sleep the morning). periods: the hour each part of the day begins. schedule[role][period]: weights of what they do — home, work, errand, market, tavern, church, plaza, well, stroll, chat, play ('default' for roles not listed; guards keep posts and patrols instead). stay: seconds spent at each ([min, max]; a real minute is an hour). tendOutside: the chance a role works out front of its door instead of indoors. chat.lines: said by two neighbours stopping to talk, by part of the day, by role, or 'any' ({name} = the other).

foraging._doc: The town herbalists (some villagers by trade, systems/practiceSkills.js craftTrades) at work on the map (world/innerMap/townHerbalists.js): at work, share of the time one walks out to a bush that gives one of gives (its wild give: ferns, heather and lavender herbs; the berry bushes and brambles berries; the wild rose flowers), one of the nearer few within reach tiles of home and out past townClear tiles from the town, and cuts from it with a sickle for pickSeconds; the bush stands, picked bare (pickedDay), and gives nothing more for regrowDays. At most maxPerDay bushes a day on one map. Berries go into the town's food store (as a harvest does); herbs and flowers into its goods (goodsPer each), taken to the first of stores[good] the town has. labels: what they are seen doing.

mining._doc: The town miners (a few villagers by trade, systems/practiceSkills.js craftTrades, and in the hills and mountains its mountainTrades) at work on the map (world/innerMap/townMiners.js): at work, share of the time a miner walks out to a rock (one of the nearer few within reach tiles of home, out past townClear tiles from the town) and breaks it up with a pick, blow by blow every interval seconds, each blow taking blow % of its health less the rock's resistance %. When it gives the rock is gone. At most maxPerDay rocks a day on one map. The miner carries up to carryMax stone to the first of stores the town has, worth goodsPerStone town goods each.

woodcutting._doc: The town woodcutters (a share of villagers and farmers by trade, systems/practiceSkills.js craftTrades) at work on the map (world/innerMap/townWoodcutters.js): at work, share of the time a cutter walks out to a tree (one of the nearer few within reach tiles of home, out past townClear tiles from the town) and fells it, blow by blow every interval seconds, each blow taking blow % of its health less the tree's fell.hardness %; it comes down as the player's do (its own stump, toppling away from the cutter, kept with the map's fellings so it grows back). At most maxPerDay trees a day on one map. The cutter carries up to carryMax logs to the first of stores the town has, worth goodsPerWood town goods a log. Old stumps they grub out too: a stump left grubAfterDays (or one the map was drawn with) may be dug out instead (grubShare of the time a cutter goes out, while there is one; at most maxGrubPerDay a day on one map), for its firewood (goodsPerFirewood each), and the ground stays clear for good.

any: My back's been at me all week.
Have you seen the price of salt?
merchant: I've a fine bolt of cloth in, {name}.
priest: Will we see you at prayers?
blacksmith_npc: Had a horse throw a shoe this morning.
traveler: Is there a decent inn here?
Where I've come from, they'd never believe it.

knockout._doc: Beaten to 0 health in a street fight is beaten senseless, not dead (systems/knockout.js). npc: how long a knocked-out townsperson lies senseless (seconds, [min, max]; a real minute is an hour) and the share of health they wake with. player: hours lost when the player is knocked out, the health share they wake with, and the share of their purse taken when robbed. finish: the chance whoever downed the player finishes them — base, a violent (aggressive) sort, one who dislikes them (disposition under 25, added), one holding a grudge (the player hurt their kin or friend), one whose kin the player killed; the watch never kills (it arrests the wanted). rob: the chance, by role, they go through the player's purse instead of just leaving. Who started it matters: fetchWatch — the player threw the first blow, so (in a town with a watch) the one who downed them runs for the guards, with this chance, and the player wakes in the cells (unless a grudge finishes them first). npcStarted — they set on the player: finish (by temperament: base/aggressive/grudge) or, where the realm allows it, capture into their own prison camp (capture: the chance; days: [min, max] of labour; freedomCost: gold per day left), else rob or leave. Whether a realm lets private citizens keep prison camps is its law (data/laws.json → privatePrisons; its ruler may change it). householder: someone at home who hates the player (a grudge, or disposition under hateBelow; aggressive temperament under angryBelow) may set on them when they walk in (chance, once a visit). lines: what they say ({victim} = the one the grudge is for, {camp} = the camp's name).

arrest: That's enough. You're coming with me.
warn: Let that be a lesson. Stay out of trouble.
fetch: Stay there — I'm fetching the watch.
You'll answer to the watch for this.
capture: You'll make a fine pair of hands for {camp}.
Chain this one. To {camp} with them.
householder: I know what you did. You'll not leave here standing.
Get out — no. You're not getting out.

jail._doc: The jail map (world/innerMap/jail.js, ui/innerMapJail.js): the names of the other prisoners and the gaoler, and what they say. The cellmates themselves are named by player/prison.js (data/underworld.json → prison). transport: the march when sentenced where there is no jail (villages) — to the nearest town of jailTypes (the same crown first), hexesPerDay; each day on the road raiders may fall on the escort (raid: base chance, more per hostile band within radius hexes, capped at max), or a guard offers to loose you for coin (bribe), a wheel breaks (delay: a day lost), a kindness or a cruelty (health). Raid choices: slip (stealth, agility — an escape), fight (combat, strength — the captain takes reward share off the sentence), stay (the guards win guardsWin of the time; else the raiders take you into servitude takenShare of the rest, or rob you and leave you free). lines: {town}, {from}, {left}, {cost}, {days}, {took}, {added}, {cut}. zones: places the player may not go (tile._zone; ui/innerMapZones.js). jail_cells — the cells and the corridor behind the gaol's front room, closed to visitors: the warden (the gaoler) warns the first time, and at the second step in (or graceSeconds lingering after the warning) shouts and attacks.
prisonerLines: I didn't do it. None of us did.
Rats again last night. Big as cats.
Three winters I've been in here.
The gaoler's soft on coin, if you've any.
gaolerLines: Bread at dusk. If you're lucky.

quiet: The escort marches on. Your wrists are raw under the irons.
A long day on the road. The guards talk of a girl in {town}.
Rain all day. The chains are cold and the guards are colder.
You pass a gibbet at a crossroads. The guards laugh.
Farmers stop work to watch the prisoner go by.
{left} day(s) more to {town}, says the sergeant.
raid: Arrows from the treeline! Raiders fall on the escort.
A band of raiders blocks the road, blades out. The guards close round the cart.
Shouts in the dusk — riders coming hard. Raiders!
bribe: The youngest guard sidles up at the fire. "{cost} gold, and your chains come loose tonight."
A guard eyes your purse. "For {cost} gold I sleep sound and you walk."
delay: A cart wheel splits in a rut. A day lost mending it.
A flooded ford. The escort waits a day for the water to fall.
kindness: A farmwife presses bread and a cup of milk into your hands.
An old priest on the road says a prayer for you and shares his water.
cruelty: A guard takes his temper out on you with the butt of his spear.
They make you walk behind the horses, in the dust, all day.
arrive: You are marched through the gates of {town} in chains, to its gaol.
The walls of {town} at last — and its gaol.

outcomes.slipped: In the fight you slip your chains and run for the trees. No one follows — yet.
outcomes.slipCaught: A guard rides you down: +{added} days, and a beating for your trouble.
outcomes.fought: You snatch up a fallen blade and fight beside the guards. When it is over the captain takes {cut} days off your sentence.
outcomes.foughtHurt: You throw yourself into the fight and are cut for it. The guards drive the raiders off without you.
outcomes.guardsWin: You keep your head down. The guards drive the raiders off.
outcomes.taken: The escort breaks and scatters. The raiders take you for themselves — {days} days in their chains.
outcomes.abandoned: The escort breaks and flees. The raiders take {took} gold and leave you chained in the road. By dark you have worked the irons loose — free.
outcomes.bribePaid: You press {cost} gold into his hand. Before dawn your chains are loose and the guard is snoring.

seats._doc: Lords' seats on the town map (world/innerMap/seats.js): manors and the castle of a capital. seatTypes: the buildings that are seats. doorGuards[type]: how many stand at its door day and night (titles: what they're called). A manor's doors are barred when nobody is at home (no one inside: the lord and household go about the town by day); a castle always keeps its garrison. While its guards stand, they turn the player away by night (nightFrom/nightTo hours) or with a warrant out in the realm, and let them in otherwise; knock the guards down and the door is yours (still barred if nobody is home). Whoever holds the seat (it is theirs, or their colony, or their crown's town) always walks in. lines: what the guards say ({lord} = the lord's name or 'the lord', {seat} = the building's name). zones: places in the castle the player may not go (tile._zone; ui/innerMapZones.js) — castle_private, the lord's chambers and the treasury: a castle guard warns, then attacks. staff: who keeps the castle inside (role → [count, npc type]); names for them.

away: {lord} is not at home. No one goes in while the house is empty.
The house is shut up. Come back when {lord} is in.
Nobody's home, and nobody's going in. Move along.
barred: The doors of {seat} are barred, and no one answers your knock.
night: At this hour? {lord} receives no one. Come back in the morning.
The house is abed. Off with you till daylight.
Gates are shut for the night. Try again at dawn.
warrant: I know your face. There's a warrant out on you — clear off before I call the watch.
Not you. Not with the crown wanting words with you.
admit: State your business. ...Very well, go in. Mind your manners.
{lord} is in. Go on, and wipe your boots.
In you go. Keep your hands where we can see them.
unguarded: No one stands at the door. You slip inside.
welcome: Your house, my lord. All is well.

warn: Those are the lord's own rooms. Out!
Halt! No one goes there without leave.
Back to the hall, you. Now.
castle_private.warnNote: Go back to the great hall.
castle_private.attackNote: You were told to keep to the hall.

lots._doc: Building lots and vacant buildings on the town map (world/lotBook.js, world/townPlanner.js, world/innerMap/lots.js, systems/lots.js). The planner sets lots aside along the streets before the houses fill in: count[type] of them (many in a village, few in a city: a city is built up), each width x depth tiles. Anyone may buy one — the player or an AI House or townsman — and build inside its bounds; the player builds only on a lot they hold (or out in the wilds). pricePerTile[type] × the lot's area is its price. vacant[type]: houses left standing empty in town, for rent (rentPerDay[type] gold a day, paid at each day's end; miss a day and you're put out) or for sale (salePrice[type]). ai: the chance each day, per town, that someone buys a free lot (buyChance), takes a vacant house (rentChance) or leaves one (leaveChance); buildDays from purchase to the building standing; builds: what they put up (building types with designs); buyers: townsfolk names when no House buys.
lots._houseBuild: A house the player raises on their own lot to let (systems/lots.js buildHouseOnLot): cost[type] gold, standing after days[type].
lots._letting: The player's own houses (bought, or raised on a lot) let to townsfolk: each day a house on offer finds a tenant at tenantChance; a tenant pays rentPerDay[type] x rentMult each day, misses it at missChance (behindMult x that once already behind), paying back up to one day's arrears with each day paid; after leaveAfterMissed days unpaid they slip away. A warning when a tenant first misses and every warnEvery days behind; a summary of rents taken and paid every summaryDays. sellBack: what a lot (and a house on it) or a town house fetches when sold, of what it cost.

laws._doc: The laws of each realm (systems/laws.js; the Laws panel ui/actionMenu/laws.js). Each law has options; a realm's law is set on kingdom.laws (saved with the realm). Until a ruler sets one, a realm keeps its old custom: share[option] of realms hold each (a hash of the realm, the same all game). Only the ruler of a realm may change its law: each change costs changeCost.treasury from the crown's treasury and changeCost.stability of the realm's stability (folk dislike upheaval), plus the option's own stability (adopting a hard law costs more), and a law may be changed again only after cooldownDays. Every law is read by the game: privatePrisons by systems/knockout.js (a private citizen may drag the beaten off to their prison camp only where it's allowed); foreignLand by systems/lots.js (where only subjects may hold land, a stranger can't buy a lot or a house, nor rent one); punishment by systems/streetCrime.js and systems/underworld.js (arrests: fines and days in the cells) (the watch's fines and days in the cells, × fine and × jail) and by systems/knockout.js (× deter: the chance that whoever downs you finishes you or goes through your purse, and that one who hates you sets on you at home); vice by systems/gangs.js (what the gangs' gambling dens take, the crackdown they draw, and the licence the crown takes).
