strike.label: Strike
strike.hint: A heavy cut. Beats a thrust aside; a guard turns it into a riposte.

thrust.label: Thrust
thrust.hint: A quick point. Punishes a feint; a strike beats it aside.

feint.label: Feint
feint.hint: Draws the guard and slips past it, winding them; a thrust punishes it.

guard.label: Guard
guard.hint: Catch your breath. Turns a strike into a riposte; a feint draws it out.

duels._armour: Weapons, shields and armour in data/arms.json are read from there (systems/arms.js): duel damage, handling, reach, penetration, block and protection by damage type. These tables keep the rest: a smith's hammer and bare fists; dragonscale and the amulet.

lines.strike>thrust: {a} brings a heavy cut down and beats {b}'s thrust aside.
lines.thrust>feint: {b} feints; {a}'s point darts straight in through the empty motion.
lines.feint>guard: {a} draws {b}'s guard high and slips under it.
lines.guard>strike: {b} commits to a great cut — {a} turns it and ripostes.
lines.strike~feint: {a}'s cut meets {b}'s feint — a scramble of steel.
lines.strike=strike: Both swing at once — steel rings on steel.
lines.feint=feint: Two feints, two flinches. Nobody commits.
lines.guard=guard: Both hold their guard and circle, catching their breath.
lines.miss: {b} twists away at the last instant.
lines.tired: {a} is blown and the move comes slow.

arms._doc: Arms and armour (systems/arms.js). Every weapon, shield, helm and body armour the player can forge, buy, wear, wield and issue to troops. An item's stats: slot (main | off | head | body), class (dagger, sword, axe, mace, spear, polearm, bow, crossbow, shield, helm, padded, leather, mail, plate), material (bronze, iron, steel, wood, leather, cloth), hands (2 = no shield), cut / pierce / blunt (0-10: the duel's weapon damage is the best of the three / 2, its damage type the best of the three), reach (0-3: the longer weapon hits more often on strike and thrust), weight (kg: heavy weapons cost breath to swing, heavy harness costs stamina), attack (handling: added to the duel's attack), pen (0-1: the share of the defender's armour the blow ignores — maces and points go through mail), edge (true: the blade dulls and wants sharpening), wear (how fast it wears: 1 = normal), tier (what it is worth on a soldier: bronze 0.85, iron 1, steel 1.15), block / riposte (shields: duel guard and riposte), cover (shields: share of a missile or ambush blow it takes), prot (armour: share of each blow it stops) with vs (how well it stops cut / pierce / blunt), melee (false: a bow is no duelling weapon), repair (what mending it takes), sprite (for the renderers: weaponClass and the LPC layers under assets/lpc/Characters: layer, the piece in front of the body; behind, its frames where it passes behind the body; layers, the piece's composited layers bottom to top when there are several; paint, a shield's livery paint (a folder of colours). Body armour names the masculine build's sheets, the feminine build's sit at the same path under Clothing/Feminine, Thin. The art: scripts/make_arms_layers.py, make_arms_shields.py, make_arms_wear.py). Grades (core/grades.js) scale damage, block, cover and prot by their effect multiplier. troops: what each soldier must be issued (systems/arms.js issueKit) — per unit type, the slots with their weight in his worth and the classes that fill them; bare is what an unarmed man is worth against a fully armed one.

wear._doc: Condition (0-100) and edge (0-100) of the pieces the player wears and wields, and of a troop's kit. Duels: the weapon loses edge for every blow it lands and condition a little; armour loses condition for every blow taken; a spar (blunted) wears at sparShare. Harm on the road (PlayerEffects.scaleDamage) wears the armour by perHarm per point of harm. A battle wears the commander's own gear by battle and every surviving soldier's kit by kitBattle. Below `worn` condition a piece loses effect down to `brokenMult` at 0; at 0 it breaks and is lost. A dull edge (edgeMult at 0) cuts less. Mending at an anvil takes the item's repair goods (yourself: Smithing xp; at a town smith for a fee, the goods bought from the town's stock); a whetstone puts the edge back (it may crack: whetstoneBreak), or the town smith's grindstone for grindFee.

duel._doc: How gear plays in Duels: reachPerPoint (hit chance per point of reach over the foe's, on strike and thrust), heavyAt (kg: a weapon this heavy or more costs heavyCost extra breath a strike), staminaPerKg (harness weight off the bout's breath, after freeKg), riposte for a two-hander's own parry.

troops._doc: What a recruit must be issued, by unit type (systems/arms.js). slots: { slot: { w (his worth that rides on it; a kit's weights add to 1), classes (what fills it) } }. bare: what he is worth with nothing (a club, a knife, a jerkin of his own). market: the town goods bought for each slot when the pack has nothing fit, cheapest first. Unit types not listed fight as they come (siege engines, mages, ships). The worth of a filled slot = the item's tier x its grade's effect x its condition.

looks._doc: How the pieces are dressed on the LPC figures (systems/arms.js lookLayers, liveryLayers). shieldPaints: the livery colours the new shields' Paint folders hold (scripts/make_arms_shields.py PAINTS); a side's paint outside it shows defaultPaint. The heater keeps every colour of its own pack. liveryColours: the shirt colours the livery wear is made in (scripts/make_arms_livery.py): a man in mail or plate wears a tabard of his shirt's colour over it (tabardOver: the armour sheets that take one), a brigandine's cloth cover is his shirt's colour; a shirt colour outside the list shows no tabard and the brigandine's own red.

spoils._doc: A won battle strips the beaten: per `per` points of the enemy's strength, one piece of each of `goods` (the spears, munition swords and shields of the dead), at most `max` of each. Draws no RNG.

ammo._doc: Arrows and bolts (systems/arms.js): a bowman (archer, longbowman; a scout issued a bow) carries a quiver of arrows, a crossbowman (or anyone issued a crossbow) bolts: unit.ammo, filled from the packs (every day, and after a battle) and, when he is recruited where the town sells them, bought at its price. Every battle (the auto battle, the phased field battle, the battlefield on the ground) he looses perBattle (on the battlefield: fieldVolley per volley his company looses); a won field gives back recover of what was loosed (picked up off the ground, into the packs). Short of a battle's worth he fights weaker: his worth x (dryMult + (1 - dryMult) x quiver / perBattle). A unit with no quiver record (an older save, a recruit who came with his own) is filled once, free. goods: the ammunition by weapon class.

realms._doc: The crowns' armouries (world/realmArms.js, kingdom.armoury). A realm's army (kingdom.military, in men) needs a kit per menPerKit men: a weapon (main) for its foot and horse, a bow (ranged) for its archers (its composition's archer share), a shield (off) for the foot, a helm and a body armour for every man, and quiver arrows per archer kit. Every buyEvery days the crown buys what it lacks out of its own towns' market stock (at most marketShare of a town's stock at a time, the cheapest good of the slot first, at the town's price, paid from the treasury into the town's purse, booked as the army's arms line), spending at most spendShare of what the treasury holds above its reserve (reserveBase + reservePerMan x men). Pieces wear out: wear.peace of them a day, wear.war at war (this is the realm's draw on the towns' arms: the old warMult stand-in is gone). A battle: each side loses the arms of its fallen (the men lost x lostShare of the pieces); the side holding the field recovers recoverOwn of its own and strips strip of the beaten's; each side looses perBattle arrows per archer kit (the victor picks up arrowRecover of its own). A host sent against the player (systems/realmWars.js) takes its share of the armoury with it, brings back what survives, and loses it all when broken. More than keep x the need in store (after a demobilisation, a rich haul) is sold back to the realm's best-stocked market at sellShare of its price, as far as the town's purse pays. Battle power x the army's arms factor: (1 - archers) x the soldier's kit worth + archers x the archer's (troops.kits soldier/archer weights; a filled slot = its fill x the pieces' average tier; a bow without arrows at dryMult), clamped to [minFactor, troops.maxFactor]. A new realm starts with start of its need in its arsenals.

rivals._doc: The rival Houses' retinues in harness (systems/rivalHouses.js, rival.arms). A retinue is baseMen of the House's household men plus its hired guards; each needs the soldier's kit (troops.kits.soldier). When the retinue stands in a town (a trading stop, a court, home) the House buys what it lacks out of the town's market stock (the cheapest good of each slot), paying the town's price from the purse into the town's, never below invest.reserve gold and at most spendShare of the purse at once. The retinue's strength (its fights on the road, a waylaying, your attack) x its kit factor (as a soldier's: bare to troops.maxFactor). The pieces wear out (wear a week, share of them); a beaten retinue loses the arms of its fallen (the guards lost, and lostShare of the rest); a retinue scattered by you leaves lostShare of its arms on the road. The head fights a duel in the House's best blade and harness.

crafting._doc: Personal crafting at furniture stations (player/crafting.js). Each recipe: station (cook|craft|smelt|brew|tan|arms — the Weaponsmith & Armoury at an anvil: the weapons, shields, helms and harness of data/arms.json), skill (the craft skill it trains and leans on: data/craftGrades.json skills; default by station), ingredients, result, difficulty 1-5, xp, quality (false = an intermediate that comes out Common), smith (true = worked at the Forge minigame), attr (the attribute that steadies the hand). The grade of the work (Poor to Masterwork, data/craftGrades.json) is rolled from the skill, the workshop, tools, the inputs' grade, the forge and the seeded RNG; ranks (config.ranks) count all crafting xp.

config._tuning: The grade roll lives in data/craftGrades.json (roll). Failure here: base + difficulty x perDifficulty - skill level x perLevel - workshop - tools (+ the forge), clamped to [min, max].

mercenaryContracts._doc: How mercenary contracts (data/military.json contractTypes) play out — player/mercContracts.js. Each contract faces an opposition (strength, rolled within spread at signing); during the countdown a day may bring one event (weights per contract); at the end the force ratio decides victory and casualties. Employer reputation (player.mercRep[kingdomId]) moves pay, renege odds and whether a realm will hire you. contracts.<id>.items is the contract's loot table ([{ id, qty: [lo, hi], weight }]): a loot event finds goods with itemChance, a won contract takes spoils with spoilsChance. contracts.<id>.naval: the share of the war galleys' strength that counts (a pirate cove).

generalship._comment: A commission in a realm's army (player/generalship.js). The host is a share of the realm's own standing army (kingdom.military): its losses are the realm's losses. Wages come out of the crown's treasury (unpaid wages are owed as arrears), supplies out of the realm's town granaries (the crown pays the town for the grain), plunder out of the plundered town's purse and granary. Shares are 0-1; days are game days.

court._comment: The rival at court is the head of the realm's greatest noble House (world/estates.js noble holders) made an NPC lord (traits, honour, wit, memory). Every rivalCadence days he hatches a scheme the player sees coming; it bites on its day (schemeDays later) by his influence/50, half as hard when answered at court. Expose it (odds from diplomacy and stealth, less against a cunning or clever lord) or buy him off (gold into his House's purse; an honourable or proud lord will not be bought).

slander.text: is whispering against you before the crown.

credit.text: is telling the court your victories were won on his counsel.

supply.text: is working on the granary wardens to hold your wagons back.

wages.text: has a friend at the treasury who could sit on your pay chest.

recall.text: is petitioning the crown to recall you before you grow too strong.

court._comment: A successful coup seats a Royal Court as the Monarch start does (Scenarios.seatCourt): a guard out of the realm's host, sworn lords, the old officers on the council, the old line's heir a pretender, restless ambitious lords, and the old rival among them. A usurper is resented more than an heir.

escort._doc: The realm's household guard (player/realmEscort.js): a lord, a great lord or the crown rides with an escort the realm keeps. Its men are drawn out of the realm's own army (kingdom.military; never more than maxShare of it at once) and go back to it when the escort ends; each company is armed out of the realm's armoury (kingdom.armoury.stock: a piece for each slot of its kit, a quiver of arrows for its bowmen) and hands back what the survivors carry. The crown pays them: each company's wage (its unit type's upkeep x pay.mult) out of the treasury daily, booked on the crown's 'guard' line, into the men's pockets (spent in the towns they lodge in, pay.spendShare a day; what is left goes home with them to the capital); their bread is bought from a town's granary as the army's is (supply), the crown paying the town. What the treasury cannot pay is owed: morale falls, and after arrears.graceDays the unpaid slip away (their arms with them). The fallen are the realm's dead and their kits are lost with them. A rank: crown (the player rules the realm), great (Chancellor, the Great Lord start's House in its realm, or greatEstates estates there), lord (a Lord's office - Marshal, Spymaster - or lordEstates estates in the realm one is sworn to). units: the companies the rank rides with; extra: how many more the crown may send when asked (extraUnit each); refill: one lost company replaced every refill.days while the treasury and the army allow. ask: what asking for more costs (reputation with the realm, never below ask.minReputation; a ruler pays nothing) and the treasury it must hold after (reserveBase + reserveDays of the guard's wage). sendHome: days before a guard sent home is sent again unasked. loyalty: grows with days served and victories; at coupJoinAt or more the guard joins a general's coup, below it stands with the crown. deter: bands in sight are less eager to set on a party in a crown's livery (military.json encounters.pursuit.escortMult); a rival's thieves and assassins striking at you meet the guard (schemeFoil chances).

books._comment: Books on inner-map bookshelves (systems/books.js). A shelf offers the unread books its place could hold (tier: village 1, town 2, capital/temple/library 3); each reading advances the open book by one sitting (two sittings a day count at most); finishing it grants its reward once. Rewards: skills (capped at 10), stats (capped by devotion's statCaps.intelligence share via Devotion.raiseStat), knowledge (an extinct faith discovered, tiles revealed around the reader).

libraries._doc: A seat's own library (systems/library.js; founded by player/startKnowledge.js for the advanced starts). Its books are written from the world when it is founded (the realm's chronicle, the royal roll, maps, the faith's annals, the guild's rolls) and come first at a shelf inside one of the seat's buildings; each sitting reads out pagesPerSitting pages (sittings between minSittings and maxSittings). neighbours: how many neighbouring realms the royal library has maps and letters of.

feasts._comment: Feasts (systems/feasts.js). A feast is planned: guests (realm rulers within reach, notable townsfolk of the town), a menu tier whose courses are drawn from the host's own stores first and bought at the town's market for the rest, and entertainment. Each guest who comes judges it (menu, entertainment, their traits, their regard); incidents may follow. Effects: renown, reputation, town happiness, each guest's opinion (NpcLords.rememberDeed when present, reputation in their realm otherwise), a deed rumour. Cooldown between feasts; the same town tires of them.

fame._doc: Local fame (systems/fame.js): how the people of one realm see the player. good = renown*renownWeight + max(0,rep)*repWeight + max(0,karma)*karmaWeight + House honours; ill = max(0,-rep)*badRepWeight + max(0,-karma)*badKarmaWeight + heat*heatWeight. An ill-fame stage applies when ill reaches its threshold and is at least the good score.

rivalSeed._doc: In a realm ruled by a rival House, townsfolk start colder by feud*perFeud (to -max), and speak of the feud.

requests._doc: The famous are asked for help (systems/fame.js townRequest): arriving in a town where the crowd gathers, a celebrated/legendary player is begged for a favour with chance[stage], at most once per cooldownDays anywhere and townCooldownDays per town, with no more than maxOpen such favours open. The asker is a real townsperson (settlement.folk) where there is one. Each hook is a quest hook for Quests.createNpcTask (type: a Quests.NPC_TASK_OBJECTIVES key; task: a data/npcTasks.json task; reward: a Quests.NPC_TASK_REWARDS kind). Drawn on its own seeded stream. lines: the lead-in ({who}, {town}, {player}, {stage}).

hooks.text: Outlaws took my grandmother's locket on the road. They say nothing is beyond you. Please, get it back.
My boy went into the old forest after a dare and never came out. If anyone can find him, it is you.
A pack has been at our flocks every night. The watch shrugs. You would not.
Our shrine's relic was stolen and carried into the ruins. The priest says only a hero would dare.
A caravan of ours vanished on the road. We pooled what we have: find it, great one.
There is a bandit camp in the woods and the lord will not send men. Will you?
The old hermit in the hills needs his medicine and the road is not safe for us. You fear nothing, they say.

lines: {who} pushes through the crowd and falls to one knee: the tales of you reached {town} long before you did.
Before the cheering has died, {who} catches your sleeve: "You are {player}? Then you can help us."
{who} has waited at the gate all morning for a glimpse of you, and will not let you pass without a plea.

house._doc: The House: its tuning, family offices, Prestige sources and sinks, ambitions, and the demands made on a rich House (systems/house.js, systems/demands.js). systems/house.js keeps identical defaults for every table, used only when this data is not loaded; each table here is laid over them key by key. `config` is the Prestige/rival/role tuning; `roles` the five family offices (the member skill each scales off); `sources` the Prestige a notable deed earns (House.recordDeed) and `sourceScales` its multiplier by kind (a miracle, a festival's budget tier, an achievement's tier; 0 awards nothing); `sinks` the Prestige price of what gold cannot buy. An ambition's `requires` names the ambition that must be fulfilled first (its predecessor tier); `req` is a map of House._metrics keys to the minimum value (true for a flag). `reward` is paid when the capstone is reached: prestige, gold, renown, reputation (with every living realm), and an `honour` the House keeps forever — each honour's `fame` adds to the House's good fame in every realm (systems/fame.js).

betrothal_broken.label: the betrothal you broke
betrothal_broken.recall: You broke the promise between our Houses.

courtLetters._mailReplies: Replies to the letters the player sends by courier (systems/mail.js): weight 0 — never drawn by the daily tick; mail: true — their answers are applied by Mail.answerReply, and leaving one unanswered costs nothing but the letters marked lapseEffect.

office_offer.subject: An office at court
office_offer.body: {from} writes in a clerk's careful hand: the crown has need of a {title}, and your name was spoken. The seal of {realm} hangs from the ribbon.

accept.label: Accept the office of {title}
accept.tooltip: You are appointed {title}: a salary, and duties to keep.
accept.result: You take the office of {title}. {from} is pleased.

decline.label: Decline with thanks
decline.tooltip: A small slight: the lord remembers it.
decline.result: You decline the office. The reply is cool.

office_offer.ignored: No answer went back to {from} about the office of {title}. It went to another.

marriage_proposal.subject: A match for {child}
marriage_proposal.body: {from} proposes a match between {child} and a noble house of {realm}. They offer a dowry of {amount} gold, and the friendship of their crown.

accept.label: Accept the match for {child}
accept.tooltip: {child} weds into {realm}; you receive {amount} gold. Opinion rises.
accept.result: The banns are read. {child} will wed into {realm}, and {amount} gold comes with the bride-price.

refuse.label: Refuse the match
refuse.tooltip: They will take it as a slight.
refuse.result: You refuse. {from} does not hide the insult taken.

marriage_proposal.ignored: Your silence on {child}'s match was taken as a refusal in {realm}.

feast_invite.subject: An invitation to feast
feast_invite.body: {from} bids you to a feast at court: boar and venison, minstrels, and the great of {realm} at the long tables. A gift for the host is expected (about {amount} gold).

attend.label: Attend, with a gift ({amount}g)
attend.tooltip: Renown and standing in {realm}; the lord remembers you were there. You hear the court's news.
attend.result: You feast at {from}'s table, and hear much of {realm}'s affairs.

feast_invite.ignored: The feast at {from}'s court went on without you, and your empty place was noticed.

tournament_invite.subject: A tournament proclaimed
tournament_invite.body: Heralds of {realm} proclaim a tournament under {from}'s banner, with a purse of {prize} gold for the champion. Entry is {amount} gold.

compete.label: Ride in the lists ({amount}g)
compete.tooltip: Three bouts on the duel engine, fought on instinct. Prize, renown, bruises.

watch.label: Attend as a spectator
watch.tooltip: A little standing for being seen there.
watch.result: You watch from the stands and drink to the champion.

call_to_arms.subject: A call to arms
call_to_arms.body: {from} summons the sworn swords of {realm}: we are at war with {enemy}. Ride to the host, or send what you can.

ride.label: I will ride (fight {enemy} within {days} days)
ride.tooltip: A promise: win a campaign battle against {enemy} for your liege (Realm Politics → Campaign) within {days} days, or break your word.
ride.result: You swear to ride against {enemy}. {from} will be watching.

gold.label: Send gold instead ({amount}g)
gold.tooltip: The gold goes to your liege's war chest.
gold.result: Your gold goes to the war chest of {realm}.

refuse.label: Refuse the summons
refuse.result: You refuse the summons. It will be remembered.

call_to_arms.ignored: You never answered {from}'s call to arms. Your silence was louder than a refusal.

loan_request.subject: A request for a loan
loan_request.body: {from} writes, not without embarrassment, that the treasury of {realm} is pressed. Would you lend {amount} gold, to be repaid with {interest} in {days} days?

lend.label: Lend {amount} gold
lend.tooltip: Repaid with {interest} interest in {days} days — if the crown can and will. Opinion rises.

loan_request.ignored: {from}'s letter asking for a loan went unanswered.

loan_default.subject: The debt of {realm}
loan_default.body: {from} writes that the crown cannot repay the {amount} gold it owes you, and begs your patience.

forgive.label: Forgive the debt
forgive.tooltip: The gold is gone, but the lord will not forget the kindness.
forgive.result: You forgive the debt. {from} is moved.

demand.label: Demand what you are owed
demand.tooltip: Perhaps half comes back, if the treasury has it. The lord resents it.

loan_default.ignored: The debt of {realm} is written off in silence.

rival_truce.subject: {from} offers a truce
rival_truce.body: A sealed letter from {from}: the quarrel between your Houses has cost both too much. They propose a truce.

accept.label: Accept the truce
accept.result: You accept {from}'s truce. The feud cools.

rival_truce.ignored: {from}'s offer of truce went unanswered, and the feud festers.

rival_tribute.subject: {from} demands tribute
rival_tribute.body: {from} demands {amount} gold as the price of leaving your House in peace.

pay.label: Pay {amount} gold
pay.result: You pay. {from} is satisfied, for now.

insult.label: Send back an insult
insult.tooltip: Renown for your defiance, but the feud runs hot.
insult.result: Your reply is copied and laughed over in every tavern. {from} is not laughing.

rival_tribute.ignored: You ignored {from}'s demand. They take it as defiance.

rival_marriage.subject: {from} proposes a match to end the feud
rival_marriage.body: {from} proposes that {child} wed into their House, and the feud between you be buried at the altar.

accept.label: Wed {child} to end the feud
accept.tooltip: {child} marries into {realm}; the feud cools by {feudCut}.
accept.result: {child} weds into {from}. The feud is buried at the altar.

rival_marriage.ignored: {from}'s offer of a match went unanswered.

spouse_plea.subject: {from} pleads for {realm}
spouse_plea.body: {from} cannot sleep. Your realm is at war with {realm}, where {from} was born. "Speak for peace, I beg you. Those are my people."

plead.label: Speak for peace at court
plead.tooltip: Your liege thinks less of you; {realm} thinks more; the crowns' relations warm. {from} is grateful.
plead.result: You speak for peace. {from} weeps with relief.

terms.label: Offer {realm} terms ({amount}g)
terms.result: You buy peace with {realm}. {from} embraces you.

duty.label: Duty comes first
duty.result: You tell {from} that duty comes first. The silence is cold.

spouse_plea.ignored: You never answered {from}'s plea. It is not forgotten at home.

gift.label: Send love and a gift ({amount}g)
gift.tooltip: The court of {realm} thinks better of your House.
gift.result: Your gift goes to {child}'s household in {realm}.

intel.label: Ask what is said at court
intel.tooltip: Learn of {realm}'s ruler, army and treasury.
intel.result: {child} writes back what is said at court.

family_report._doc: Sent by systems/heirAgency.js and systems/regency.js: a child's or regent's account of a commission, a fosterage, a battle (weight 0: never drawn by the daily tick). Replying warms the realm named, if any; silence costs nothing.
family_report.subject: {subject}

reply.label: Write back
reply.tooltip: A few lines in your own hand.

child_hostage.subject: {child} is afraid
child_hostage.body: {child} writes from {realm}: now that our realms are at war, the court looks at me as a hostage. Bring me home, or trust my spouse's kin to keep me safe.

recall.label: Bring {child} home ({amount}g)
recall.tooltip: Bribes and an escort. {realm}'s crown takes it as an insult.

trust.label: Trust the kin of {child}'s spouse
trust.tooltip: The crown of {realm} appreciates it — but if it thinks ill of you, {child} may be held.
trust.result: You write that you trust {realm}'s honour.

coalition_ultimatum._doc: Sent by systems/coalitions.js when a league is sworn against the player (weight 0: never drawn by the daily tick). Its answers call Coalitions.concede / Coalitions.defy; left unanswered, the league marches on its own deadline.
coalition_ultimatum.subject: The terms of {league}
coalition_ultimatum.body: {from} writes in the name of {league} — {members}. {cause} Pay {amount} gold to the league's war chest, or bow before its courts ({prestige} Prestige), within {days} days. Otherwise every crown of the league will march.

concede.label: Pay the league {amount} gold
concede.tooltip: The league stands down. Its members are paid; the courts see you bend (a little Prestige).

bow.label: Bow before the league ({prestige} Prestige)
bow.tooltip: The league stands down; your House's Prestige pays for it.

defy.label: Throw their terms back
defy.tooltip: War from every crown of the league, at once. Their lords remember the insult.
defy.result: You send the envoys home with nothing. {league} marches.

coalition_ultimatum.ignored: No answer went to {league}. It marches.

file.label: File the letter
file.result: You file {from}'s letter with your papers.

mail_proposal.subject: {subject}

decline.label: Let it rest
decline.tooltip: Nothing is sealed; {from} is a little disappointed.

mail_proposal.ignored: {from}'s answer to your proposal went unanswered, and the moment passed.

pay.label: Pay {amount}g for {child}
pay.tooltip: {child} comes home; the gold goes to the crown of {realm}.
pay.result: The ransom is paid. {child} is on the road home.

refuse.label: Refuse the price
refuse.tooltip: {child} stays at {realm}'s court. You may write again.

mail_blackmail.subject: Your letter to {lover}
mail_blackmail.body: An unsigned hand writes: your letter to {lover} passed through my hands before it reached them. {amount} gold left at the post house buys my silence. Otherwise, your spouse and the whole town will read it.

pay.label: Pay {amount}g for silence
pay.tooltip: The letter is burnt, they say.
pay.result: You pay. The matter goes quiet.

refuse.label: Refuse
refuse.tooltip: The letter will be read aloud: a scandal, and your spouse's anger.

mail_blackmail.ignored: You never paid, and the letter was read aloud in the market.

courier_bag.subject: A sealed letter in your rider's bag
courier_bag.body: One of your riders at {courier} carries a letter under the seal of {lordName} of {realm}, bound for {dest}. The seal could be lifted and set again. Nobody would know, probably.

deliver.label: Deliver it sealed
deliver.result: The letter is delivered with its seal unbroken.

read.label: Read it first
read.tooltip: Learn {realm}'s affairs. If it comes out, your house and you are disgraced.
read.result: You lift the seal by candlelight.

sell.label: Sell it to {enemy} ({price}g)
sell.tooltip: Gold, and {enemy}'s gratitude. If it comes out, a scandal and {lordName}'s enmity.
sell.result: The letter is copied for {enemy}'s agents.

courier_bag.ignored: The rider delivered the letter sealed, as nobody told him otherwise.

stolen_mailbag.subject: A sealed letter in a stolen mailbag
stolen_mailbag.body: Among the {letters} letters in the bag you took from the rider of {courier} is one under the seal of {lordName} of {realm}, bound for {dest}. Nobody knows yet where it went.

burn.label: Burn it
burn.tooltip: No one will ever read it — or know you had it.

read.label: Read it
read.tooltip: Learn {realm}'s affairs. If it comes out, {lordName} will not forget whose hands it passed through.
read.result: You break the seal by candlelight.

sell.label: Sell it to {enemy} ({price}g)
sell.tooltip: Gold, and {enemy}'s gratitude. If it comes out, a scandal and {lordName}'s enmity.

stolen_mailbag.ignored: The letter rots in your saddlebag, unread.

couriers._doc: The post: courier houses based in towns (systems/couriers.js, state on world.post) and the letters the player sends through them (systems/mail.js, state on player.mail). A courier house has an owner (an NPC or the player), stations (towns it serves), riders, relay horses, guards, a speed tier, a postage price, a reputation and cash. Each week every town writes letters (demand from its size and its court), split among the couriers with a station there by price, speed and reputation; wages, horses and stations are paid; riders on dangerous roads (war, raiders, outlaw lairs) are robbed. NPC houses are founded where a town goes unserved, open stations when rich, cut prices when losing and go bankrupt. A crown may grant one house a Royal Post charter: only it carries that realm's mail. The player's letters travel real days by distance, roads and season, and may be lost, delayed, robbed or intercepted; the recipient's answer comes back to Journal -> Letters.
couriers._riders: Riders on the map (systems/courierRiders.js; the game's own day only, never the headless harness): each letter the player sends from the Letters panel rides as a 'courier_rider' unit along the road, due at the recipient's town on the letter's arrival day. A sample of the houses' traffic rides too: every everyDays days a house may send one rider (npcChance, at most npcPerHouse) between two stations when an end is within nearRange of the player, at most npcMax on the map; the player's own house sends up to ownHouseMax (ownHouseChance), shown even in the fog. On the road: a raider band or lair beast within hostileRange robs with chance its strength / (its strength + the rider's guards) x robShare; an active outlaw lair within lairRange with lairChance x (1 - guard cover); a realm at war with the recipient's realm reads a lord's, rival's or child's letter (warIntercept) or seizes a house rider's bag (warSeize). Guards: guardBase + guard cover x guardPer. Bags: bagLetters, bagGold coin, a lord's sealed letter (sealedChance). Robbed by the player: Underworld crime robbery.crime (data/underworld.json), robbery.reputation lost in the realm, the house's reputation -robbery.houseRep, a sealed letter to the inbox (courtLetters stolen_mailbag) worth robbery.sealedPrice to the lord's enemy.

courtesy.name: Courtesy & news
courtesy.desc: Compliments, news, a word to keep the friendship warm. Helps a little, and less each time you write the same person.
courtesy.subject: A letter of courtesy
courtesy.warm: {to} writes back warmly and thanks you for your news.
courtesy.hostile: {to} sends your letter back unopened in all but name: a single cold line.
courtesy.tiresome: {to} has had a great many letters from you lately, and the reply is short.

gift.name: A gift enclosed
gift.desc: Enclose gold or one of your goods. Riders are robbed on bad roads: what is stolen never arrives.
gift.subject: A gift, with your compliments
gift.warm: {to} thanks you handsomely for the gift.
gift.cool: {to} accepts the gift without much warmth.
gift.hostile: {to} keeps the gift and the grudge both.
gift.stolen: {to} writes that your letter came with its seal cut and nothing inside it.

favour.name: Ask a favour
favour.desc: Ask for help: a purse, an introduction, a good word. Only friends say yes, and asking costs a little goodwill. Once in a while per person. A companion away: ask them to come back to your company (those who still approve of you come; a governor hands over their post).
favour.subject: A favour asked
favour.cool: {to} regrets that they cannot help you at present.
favour.tiresome: {to} reminds you that you asked a favour only lately.

proposal.name: A proposal
proposal.desc: Lords: a pact of friendship (an alliance if you rule a realm). Rival Houses: a truce. A love: marriage. A merchant house: partnership.
proposal.subject: A proposal
proposal.cool: {to} will think on it, which is to say no.
proposal.hostile: {to} laughs at your proposal, and makes sure others hear of it.

apology.name: An apology
apology.desc: Make amends. Softens a grudge; does nothing where there is no grudge.
apology.subject: An apology
apology.cool: {to} notes your apology. The wound is not healed.
apology.puzzled: {to} writes back, puzzled: there was nothing to forgive.

threat.name: A threat or demand
threat.desc: Demand gold or obedience. The weak sometimes pay; everyone remembers. A threat that falls into an enemy's hands may please them.
threat.subject: A demand
threat.hostile: {to} answers your threat with one of their own.

love.name: A love letter
love.desc: Sweet words for a love or your spouse. If you are married and it is not to your spouse, an opened letter becomes a scandal.
love.subject: A letter of the heart
love.warm: {to} writes back with a pressed flower and more than a few kind words.
love.cool: {to} is touched, but careful in reply.
love.hostile: {to} asks you not to write such things again.

ransom.name: Negotiate a release
ransom.desc: Open talks for a child held as a hostage at that court: they name their price, or let the child go for friendship's sake.
ransom.subject: Concerning {child}
ransom.hostile: {to} names a hard price for {child}'s release.

warning.name: A warning or intelligence
warning.desc: Warn a lord of their enemy's strength. Valued, unless the enemy's spies read it first. A companion away: a word of danger about their road or their post, and they think the better of you.
warning.subject: A warning
warning.cool: {to} thanks you, though they knew most of it.

pirates._comment: Pirates and the open sea (systems/pirates.js): named pirate captains who persist and remember you, their havens on the map, the infamy a player-pirate earns and the hunters it sends after them, merchant prey, and the sea events of Explore the Waters (each a choice). Odds are fractions; [lo, hi] ranges are rolled.

seaEvents.title: A Drifting Derelict
seaEvents.text: A hulk wallows in the swell, sails in rags, no one at the wheel. Something went badly wrong aboard her.

options.label: Board and search her
options.hint: Whatever she carried may still be aboard — or whatever killed her crew.

success.text: In the captain's cabin: a strongbox and a few casks still sound.

failure.text: The stench below was the flux. Some of it came back aboard with you.

options.label: Strip her timbers and fittings
options.hint: Slow, safe salvage: certain but modest.

success.text: Your carpenters strip her of good timber and brass; your own hull gets a patch or two.

options.label: Leave her to the sea
options.hint: Some ships are better left alone.

success.text: You sail on. The crew mutters a prayer as she falls astern.

seaEvents.title: Smoke on a Sandbar
seaEvents.text: A thin column of smoke rises from a sandbar: castaways, waving shirts on oars.

options.label: Send the boat for them
options.hint: Hands for your crew and a good deed — if they are what they seem.

success.text: Shipwrecked sailors, grateful to the bone. Some sign on; one tells of land nobody charts.

failure.text: Mutineers marooned for cause: they knifed two of your men and made off with the purse before you put them ashore again.

options.label: Throw them a cask and sail on
options.hint: A small mercy without the risk.

success.text: You float a cask of water and biscuit to them. They will live a while yet.
The crew watch the smoke a long time.

seaEvents.title: Lights Over the Water
seaEvents.text: At dusk a green glow dances on the horizon, where the charts show nothing at all.

options.label: Follow the lights
options.hint: A day off your course. Sailors' tales say such lights mark uncharted land.

success.text: By moonlight you take a bearing on a dark shape the charts do not show.

failure.text: The lights led you onto shoals. You scrape free with a gash in the hull.

success.text: The glow fades. The crew sleep badly.

seaEvents.title: A Bottle in the Swell
seaEvents.text: A sealed bottle bobs alongside, wax still on the cork.

options.label: Fish it out and open it
options.hint: Letters, a will — or a map.

success.text: Inside: a stained chart with an X and a drowned man's last boast.

failure.text: A love letter, and a coin for luck.

success.text: The bottle drifts away on the tide.

seaEvents.title: Something Rises From the Deep
seaEvents.text: The sea boils. A tentacle as thick as a mast slaps the deck.

options.label: Fight it
options.hint: Harpoons, axes and your guns against the beast.

success.text: It sinks back, bleeding ink. Ambergris and a wrecked ship's gold tangled in its arms come aboard.

failure.text: It tears at the rigging and drags men under before it tires of you.

options.label: Pour burning oil on the water
options.hint: Costs your lamp oil, if you carry any; fire may drive it off.

success.text: The burning slick drives it under. You are away before it returns.

failure.text: It comes up through the flames.

options.label: Crowd on sail and run
options.hint: Speed against something that lives here.

success.text: You outrun it, the crew laughing like madmen.

failure.text: It catches your stern before you clear its water.

seaEvents.title: A Squall Line
seaEvents.text: A black wall of cloud comes down on you, the sea white under it.

options.label: Reef sails and ride it out
options.hint: Slow and careful; a little damage at most.

success.text: You ride it out under bare poles.

failure.text: Even reefed, the squall springs a seam.

options.label: Run before it
options.hint: Use the wind: miles gained, or a mast lost.

success.text: You fly before the gale; the crew whoop as the miles run past.

failure.text: A spar goes over the side, and a man with it.

seaEvents.title: Whales Off the Bow
seaEvents.text: A pod of whales breaches, close enough to wet the deck.

options.label: Heave to and watch
options.hint: A good omen, the old hands say.

success.text: The crew take it as a blessing.

options.label: Lower the boats and hunt
options.hint: Oil and meat — and a whale's tail can stove in a boat.

success.text: A long, ugly day's work, and the hold full of oil and meat.

failure.text: A flukes-blow smashes a boat; two men don't come back.

seaEvents.title: A Sail on the Horizon
seaEvents.text: The lookout calls a sail — and no honest flag.

hospitality._doc: Hospitality (systems/hospitality.js): guest houses (bed & breakfast), inns, grand hotels and roadside roadhouses (the motels of the realm). NPC houses are a hash of each town (no RNG) and roadhouses a hash of the roads; the player builds their own as properties (data/playerEconomy.json GUEST_HOUSE, INN, HOTEL, ROADHOUSE). Guests split among a town's houses by stars, price and reputation. Rooms set the night's rest (rest type 'inn'), the morning's comfort, cleanliness and health; services are paid on the spot.

clothes._comment: Clothes freshness (player.clothesFreshness 0-100, src/player/core/needs.js). Clothes lose dailyWear a day plus soilShare per point of hygiene lost; below freshAt they cap hygiene (capFloor at 0, rising with the square), so a bath alone cannot make you clean. Below smellyBelow they smell: people notice. Washed by a service with "clothes" (laundry, valet) or by hand (washByHand) at a river, the shore or a town well.

guest_house.name: Guest House
guest_house.blurb: A bed and breakfast: a few clean rooms in a family home, and breakfast at the kitchen table.

inn.name: Inn
inn.blurb: The town's coaching inn: a crowded common room, private rooms upstairs, a hot meal, a bath and stabling in the yard.

hotel.name: Grand Hotel
hotel.blurb: Marble stairs, liveried porters and suites fit for a count. Fine dining, a bathhouse, a valet — at a price.

roadhouse.name: Roadhouse
roadhouse.blurb: A wayside house on the open road: a long bunk room, a few cheap rooms, hot broth and a yard for horses. No questions asked.

common.name: A bunk in the common room

packed_lunch.name: A packed lunch for the road

valet.name: A valet: brushed, shaved and pressed

theft.text: A guest's purse was lifted in the night at {house}. Word gets round.

brawl.text: A brawl in the common room of {house}: broken benches and a smashed window ({cost} gold).

noble.text: A lord's retinue took every room at {house} for the night and paid handsomely ({gold} gold).

chronicler.text: A travelling chronicler stayed at {house} and wrote of it: {verdict}.

bedbugs.text: Bedbugs at {house}! Guests leave scratching, and tell everyone.

regular.text: A wool merchant swears {house} is the best bed between here and the coast, and books for the season.

keepers._doc: A town house's keeper is named once, when it is founded, and the townsperson the inner map makes its keeper takes that name (world/innerMap/hospitality.js), so the name in the panels and the one in the house's name never change. female: the first names that are a woman's (the keeper chosen from the town is a woman for these).

firstSteps._comment: First Steps: the guided first month (systems/firstSteps.js). Each step's `check` names a reader in code that looks at real player/world state; `go` names what the tracker card's button opens (ui/firstStepsCard.js): an action-menu action type (`action`) or a panel (`panel`). Rewards are paid once, on completion: gold (recorded on the ledger as `firstSteps`), renown; the final reward adds House Prestige.

steps.title: See a day through
steps.why: Everything in the realms moves by the day: wages are paid, food is eaten, wounds heal and news travels when the day ends.
steps.how: Press ⌛ End Turn at the bottom right of the screen.

steps.title: Scout the land
steps.why: The map is dark until you walk it. Every hex you uncover shows roads, towns, resources and danger.
steps.how: Click a hex next to you on the map to walk there. Uncover two new hexes to finish ‘A New Beginning’ (Quests tab).

steps.title: Earn an honest coin
steps.why: Day work is the surest income when you own nothing yet, and every job trains a skill.
steps.how: In a town or village: click your own hex → ⚔ Open Actions → 🔨 Look for Work, and take a job.

steps.title: Visit the market
steps.why: You must eat: bread and grain keep your hunger off. Prices differ from town to town, and buying cheap to sell dear is how merchants grow rich.
steps.how: In a town: Open Actions → ⚖️ Trade Goods, then buy or sell anything (start with some food).

steps.title: Talk to the townsfolk
steps.why: Friends lend help, carry news, find you work and may one day marry into your House.
steps.how: In a town: Open Actions → 👥 Meet People → 💬 Talk to anyone, and chat with them.

steps.title: Take on a task
steps.why: Bounties and quests pay far better than day work and build your name.
steps.how: In a town: Open Actions → 📋 Notice Board, and accept a bounty — or accept a quest from the Quests tab.

steps.title: Sleep under a roof
steps.why: A night on the road leaves you tired, dirty and open to sickness. An inn's bed and breakfast restore you.
steps.how: In a town: Open Actions → 🛏️ Find Lodgings (or Lodge at …), book a room, then end the day.

steps.title: Give your House an Ambition
steps.why: Your House outlives you. An Ambition is its long goal: its milestones earn Prestige, which your heirs inherit.
steps.how: Top bar → 🗝️ Counsel → beside ‘Your House has no Ambition’ press House, then choose one.

steps.title: Travel to a second town
steps.why: No town has everything. Other markets pay more for your goods, and other lords may favour you.
steps.how: Click a distant town on the map to set out (it may take more than one day), then enter it.

firstSteps._dawnSteps: A start at the Dawn of Man (world/dawn.js): no towns, markets or inns yet, so the guidance follows the clan instead.

dawnSteps.title: See a day through
dawnSteps.why: The world moves by the day: your clan eats, wanders and grows when the day ends.
dawnSteps.how: Press ⌛ End Turn at the bottom right of the screen.

dawnSteps.title: Sit at your clan's fire
dawnSteps.why: Your family and your people walk with you: their tents go up wherever the clan stops.
dawnSteps.how: Stand with your clan: click your own hex → ⚔ Open Actions → 🧭 Explore Interior, and walk to the campfire.

dawnSteps.title: Scout the land
dawnSteps.why: Good ground is near fresh water: a river, a lake, the shore. Fertile plains feed more mouths than forest or hills.
dawnSteps.how: Click a hex next to you on the map to walk there; your clan follows. Uncover two new hexes to finish ‘A New Beginning’.

dawnSteps.title: Make camp for good
dawnSteps.why: A clan that stays becomes a village: it grows, trades, sends out new clans — and in time a village with others about it becomes a chiefdom.
dawnSteps.how: Lead your clan to good ground (by a river is best), then Open Actions → 🔥 Make camp for good.

dawnSteps.title: Give your House an Ambition
dawnSteps.why: Your House outlives you. An Ambition is its long goal: its milestones earn Prestige, which your heirs inherit.
dawnSteps.how: Top bar → 🗝️ Counsel → beside ‘Your House has no Ambition’ press House, then choose one.

dawnSteps.title: Visit another village
dawnSteps.why: Other clans have settled too. Their people trade what yours lack, and one day one of you will rule the others.
dawnSteps.how: Enter your own village, then walk to another (the trodden paths lead there) and enter it.

final.title: First Steps taken
final.text: You have found your feet. From here, the Steward's 🗝️ Counsel tab names what matters most each day.

afterlife._doc: After the player dies (player/afterlife.js): who they can come back as, and how the world turns while they wait. stations: what each walk of life starts with as a new character (gold range, stat and skill bonuses on top of the base 5s and 1s). candidates: how many people are offered (at random, or of a chosen settlement); newcomer: a chosen settlement also offers someone just arriving from another town, with a mother tongue of their own.

scenarios._comment: Origins, difficulty and victory goals chosen at New Game (player/scenarios.js, core/difficulty.js, systems/victory.js). Normal difficulty is 1 on every knob and must stay so.

wanderer.name: The Wanderer
wanderer.blurb: No name, no lands, no debts. A few coins, the clothes on your back and the open road. Work, trade and fight your way up: the world is yours to read.
wanderer.welcome: You are a wanderer in a {mapDesc} world of {kingdoms} kingdoms. Click on the map to move, explore settlements, and forge your destiny.

disinherited.name: The Disinherited
disinherited.blurb: A younger child of royal blood, cast out when your elder sibling took the family's favour. A real but weak claim on a throne, a House with some name, little gold, and a sibling who wants you gone.
disinherited.title: Disinherited
disinherited.welcome: Your blood runs back to the throne of {kingdom}, but {rival} has your family's favour and wants you gone. Your claim is weak (strength {claim}): marry well, serve the crown, or buy heralds until it can be pressed.

apprentice.name: Guild Journeyman
apprentice.blurb: Bound to a guild of a busy town as a journeyman: guild rates on your inputs, a little stock to sell, the trade in your hands, and a master you still owe for your indenture.
apprentice.title: Journeyman
apprentice.welcome: You are a journeyman of the {guild} of {town}. You owe your old master {debt} gold, paid weekly from your purse: miss three payments and the guild will cast you out.

exiled_monarch.name: The Exiled Monarch
exiled_monarch.blurb: You wore the crown of a realm until a usurper took it. A strong claim, a few loyal swords, a chest of gold and a realm in turmoil. Raise your banners while the succession is still disputed.
exiled_monarch.title: Exiled Monarch
exiled_monarch.welcome: {ruler} sits on your throne in {kingdom}, and the realm is split over it. Your claim is strong (strength {claim}) and loyal swords ride with you. Open Claims & Crowns from the Dynasty menu to press it before the dispute settles.

pirate_widow.name: The Pirate's Widow
pirate_widow.blurb: Your late spouse sailed under no flag. You inherited the sloop, the crew and a name the sea-lords whisper. A coastal start with a ship of your own.
pirate_widow.title: Widow of the Sea
pirate_widow.welcome: The {ship} rides at anchor in {town}, crewed and yours. The sea remembers your late spouse: some captains will know your colours (infamy {infamy}).

sellsword.name: Sellsword Captain
sellsword.blurb: You lead a small free company: hard men, wages owed every day, and a debt to the crown that paid for their gear. Fight for coin, or find something better to fight for.
sellsword.title: Sellsword Captain
sellsword.welcome: Your company of {men} is camped by {town}. They want their wages every day, and you owe {debt} gold to {lender}: take a contract at a town's board before the purse runs dry.

origins._advanced: Advanced starts (group 'advanced'): you begin already high in the world. Each takes over what exists (a crown, a see, a noble house's estates, a guildhall), never new stock: player/scenarios.js. challenge numbers are scaled by the difficulty's hostility knob.

monarch.name: The Monarch
monarch.blurb: You inherit a living kingdom: its crown and capital, its treasury and army, its court, laws and lords. The old monarch is dead, their child says the throne is theirs, and half the great lords are listening.
monarch.welcome: {oldRuler} is dead, and you are crowned {title}. The treasury holds {treasury} gold, the royal host numbers {army}, and {lords} lords owe you fealty. But {pretender} says the throne is theirs, and {neighbour} backs the claim. Open the Royal Court and Claims & Crowns from the Dynasty menu.

high_priest.name: The High Priest
high_priest.blurb: You head an established faith: the great temple of a holy city, the church's own estates and tithes, a flock across the realm, and the ear of kings. A heresy is spreading in your own see, and a zealous rival faith wants you gone.
high_priest.title: High Priestess
high_priest.welcome: You are {title} of {faith}, seated at the {temple} in {town}. The faithful of {kingdom} tithe to your see{estatesLine}. But the {heresy} is spreading in {kingdom}, and the zealots of {rival} want you gone. Preach, denounce the heretics, and raise shrines from the Religion panel.

great_lord.name: The Great Lord
great_lord.blurb: Head of the realm's greatest noble house: its manors and their rents, household knights, a cadet claim on the throne and a seat at court. The crown fears an overmighty subject.
great_lord.title: Duchess
great_lord.welcome: You are {title} of {town}, head of the greatest noble house of {kingdom}: {estates} estates pay you rent, household knights ride with you, and your blood gives you a claim on the throne (strength {claim}). {ruler} watches you closely: the crown does not love an overmighty subject.

guildmaster.name: The Guildmaster
guildmaster.blurb: Elected master of a great town's guild: its hall, its purse and its privileges, guild rates and a stipend, and the trade at your command. The masters vote again soon, and a challenger is canvassing.
guildmaster.title: Guildmaster
guildmaster.welcome: The masters of the {guild} have elected you guildmaster. The hall's purse holds {treasury} gold, and the next election is on day {election}: {challenger} is canvassing against you. Keep your standing up, or lobby the crown for a monopoly.

general.name: The General
general.blurb: A General in a realm's army: the crown's soldiers at your command on a border at war, lieutenants who owe you their rank, wages from a treasury that may run dry, a rival at court and a ruler who watches a victorious general closely.
general.welcome: You are {rank} of {kingdom}, at the head of {men} of its soldiers camped at {town}. {warLine} {rival} whispers against you before {ruler}. The crown's first orders: {order} Open Army Command from the Dynasty menu.

crime_lord.name: The Crime Lord
crime_lord.blurb: Boss of an established gang in a great city: its crew and lieutenants, protection rackets and a dice den, a smuggling line, a hidden stash. The watch captain is on your payroll, the magistrate is not, and a rival gang wants your streets.
crime_lord.title: Boss
crime_lord.welcome: {oldBoss} is dead, and the {gang} of {town} answer to you now: {crew} crew, {lieutenants} lieutenants, protection on {turf}% of the streets, a dice den and {purse} gold in the hidden stash. {captain} takes your coin; {magistrate} does not. And the {rival} want your streets: it's war. Open the Underworld from the town menu.

knowledge._doc: What each advanced start knows on day one (player/startKnowledge.js): radii in hexes of land charted (tile.explored), livingMemory in years of the realm's world history already known (the rest is in the seat's library), fluency (0-100) in neighbouring/minority tongues, how many people are already acquainted (people.score: their regard). Libraries: data/books.json → libraries.

easy.name: Easy
easy.blurb: A richer start, kinder markets, fewer wars, softer foes, gentler sickness.

hard.name: Hard
hard.blurb: A leaner purse, sharper merchants, quicker wars, tougher foes, deadlier sickness.

brutal.name: Brutal
brutal.blurb: Next to nothing in your purse, a world that cheats you, hates you, outfights you and sickens you.

none.name: Sandbox
none.blurb: No goal: live as you please.

crown.name: Wear a Crown
crown.blurb: Rule a kingdom: win a throne by civil war, or found a realm of your own.

merchant_prince.name: Merchant Prince
merchant_prince.blurb: Reach a net worth of {target} gold (gold, deposits, goods, properties, works, ships, company and bank, less debts).

dynasty.name: Dynasty
dynasty.blurb: Keep your House alive for {generations} generations or {years} years.

monopoly.name: Monopolist
monopoly.blurb: Hold {target} trade monopolies at once (won by your company's lobbying or granted by your crown).

conqueror.name: Conqueror
conqueror.blurb: Hold {target} settlements in your own hands.

faith.name: Faith Ascendant
faith.blurb: Make {target} settlements devoted to your faith.

kingpin.name: Kingpin
kingpin.blurb: Be boss of the underworld in {target} towns at once (a gang of your own, or one you took).

annals._doc: The Annals (systems/annals.js): the story of the player's life and dynasty, told from what the systems already record — the House chronicle (house.history), the reign records (house.reigns, systems/legacy.js), the wealth marks (house.wealthMarks), traits, sagas, achievements, fame, lords' memories and the ledger. Every phrase list here is picked by a hash of (event, day) — never the shared RNG — so the same save always reads the same. Tokens in {braces} are filled by the composer; {Pronoun}/{pronoun}/{poss}/{obj} follow the ruler's gender. `tagWeights` decide what is notable: an entry's weight is the highest of its tags' weights, and only entries at or above `minWeight` make the book (a chapter with fewer than `minEvents` takes its best lesser entries too). `themes` map tags to the book's themes (first match wins).
annals._rewrites: Chronicle lines written as bare noun phrases, made into sentences: [pattern, replacement]; {name} is the ruler, $1.. the captures.
rewrites: {name} gained a claim on the throne of $1.

pastTense._doc: The book is written in the past: chronicle lines (house.history; most are written in the present, 'Bran weds Tamsin.') are put into the past tense after `rewrites`. `phrases` first ([regex, replacement], each applied everywhere), then `words` (whole lowercase words). A word that is too often a noun ('lies', 'rules', 'claims', 'returns') goes in `phrases` with its context instead. Text inside quotes is left alone.

founder: In the {season} of the year {year}, {name} set {poss} name to a new House, and {house} entered the annals.
The annals of {house} begin in the {season} of the year {year}, with {name}, aged {age}, and not much else.
It was the {season} of the year {year} when {name} first called {obj}self of {house}. {Pronoun} was {age} years old.
stranger: {name} was {station} of {town} when the old line ended, and in the {season} of the year {year} began a new House: {house}.
Out of {town} came {name}, {station}, aged {age}, to found {house} in the year {year}.
heir: In the {season} of the year {year}, {name} took up the mantle of {house}, aged {age}.
The year {year} gave {house} a new head: {name}, {age} years old.
{name} came to the head of {house} in the {season} of the year {year}, at the age of {age}.

openingDisputed: Not every voice in the House agreed{quelled}.
annals.openingRegency: A regency held the House in {poss} name until {pronoun} came of age.
traitEarned: It was in these days that {name} was first called {trait}.
By now the talk in the taverns named {name} {trait}.
overflow: Of lesser matters that year the annals keep {n} more.
And {n} lesser matters besides, which the scribes did not think worth the ink.
quietYears: The years {from} to {to} passed quietly, and the annals keep little of them.
Of the years between {from} and {to} the scribes wrote little.
For {n} years after, the annals fall quiet.
achievement: The heralds cried a new honour for {name}: "{deed}".
The bards made a song of it, and called it "{deed}".
"{deed}", the heralds named the deed of {name}.
saga: The tale of {saga} came to its end: {title}. {name} had a hand in it{won}.
So ended {saga}: {title}. {name} was part of that story{won}.

war: The tally of {poss} wars: {battles} battle{battlesS} won{settlementsClause}.
summary.warSagas: {beasts} beast{beastsS} of legend fell to {poss} hand.
rise: {name} gained {titles} office{titlesS} and {prestige} Prestige for the House.
The House rose under {obj}: {titles} office{titlesS} won, {prestige} Prestige gained.
riseLost: The House's standing fell under {obj}: {prestige} Prestige lost.
It was not a reign that raised the House: {prestige} Prestige lost.
summary.crownLost: The crown of {crown} was {how} after {days} days.
justice: {name} sat in judgement {ruled} time{ruledS}; the rulings remembered: {rulings}.
Of the {ruled} petition{ruledS} {name} heard, these were remembered: {rulings}.
wealthRange: {name} came to the House's purse with {start} gold and left it with {end}.
The coffers held {start} gold when {name} took them and {end} at the last.
wealthPeak: At the height of {poss} fortune, in the year {year}, {name} counted {peak} gold.
The fortune peaked in the year {year}, at {peak} gold.
summary.wealthLow: The lean years came in {year}, when the purse fell to {low} gold.
wealthSource: Most of the coin of late came from {source}.
Of late the House lived chiefly on {source}.
summary.wealthSpend: The heaviest spending of late was on {sink}.
familyChildren: {Pronoun} fathered a line: {names} — {count} child{childrenS} in all.
familyChildrenF: {Pronoun} mothered a line: {names} — {count} child{childrenS} in all.
summary.familyLost: Of them, {lost} did not live to see {poss} death.
faithPious: {name} was known for {poss} faith: {prayers} prayer{prayersS} and {pilgrimages} pilgrimage{pilgrimagesS}.
Few doubted {poss} faith — {prayers} prayer{prayersS} said, {pilgrimages} pilgrimage{pilgrimagesS} made.
summary.infamyCrimes: The watch knew {obj}: {crimes} crime{crimesS}, caught {caught} time{caughtS}.
summary.infamyTraits: Men called {obj} {traits}, and did not say it kindly.

closed: {name} died of {cause} in the {season} of the year {year}, aged {age}, after {years} year{yearsS} at the head of the House.
Death came for {name} in the year {year}: {cause}. {Pronoun} was {age}, and had led the House {years} year{yearsS}.
In the {season} of the year {year}, {cause} took {name}, aged {age}.
closedNoCause: {name} died in the {season} of the year {year}, aged {age}, after {years} year{yearsS} at the head of the House.
The annals mark {poss} passing in the year {year}, at the age of {age}.
live: {name} lives still, aged {age}, in the {nth} year at the head of the House.
The annals of {name} are not yet closed: {pronoun} lives, aged {age}.

legacy.title: Legacy
headline: So stands {house}, {generations} generation{generationsS} on: {rank}.
Such is the measure of {house} after {generations} generation{generationsS}: {rank}.
ended: The line of {house} ended in the year {year} with {last}. {rank}.
With {last}, in the year {year}, the line of {house} ended. The scribes judged it {rank}.
legacy.holdingsNone: The House holds no land of its own.
wealth: The family fortune rose from {first} gold to a peak of {peak} in the year {peakYear}; it stands at {last}.
From {first} gold the purse grew to {peak} at its height (year {peakYear}), and holds {last} now.
legacy.wealthFell: From {first} gold the purse has fallen to {last}; its best was {peak}, in the year {peakYear}.
legacy.childrenNone: No child of its blood lives now.
legacy.achievements: {won} deeds sung by the bards, of {total}.

scribe.system: You are the court scribe of a medieval House, writing its annals. Rewrite the notes you are given into one chapter of flowing chronicle prose, past tense, solemn and vivid. Use ONLY the facts in the notes: never invent people, places, numbers, battles or events, and keep every name exactly as written. No headings, no lists, no preamble.
scribe.user:
Write the chapter "{title}" from these annals:

{text}

coalitions._doc: Directed opposition (src/systems/coalitions.js, src/systems/rivalAgents.js). The realms weigh the player's power each week; past formAt (× difficultyScale) the ones who fear and envy them most band into a named league. Tuning notes in GAMEPLAY_MANUAL.md → Coalitions & Threats.

casusBelli.conquest: To win back the towns {house} tore from its neighbours.
casusBelli.crown: To cast down the upstart crown of {realm}.
casusBelli.power: To check the overmighty {house} before it swallows them all.

saboteur.label: Saboteur
saboteur.deed: set fires among the works of {house}

rivalHouses._doc: Rival Houses in the flesh (src/systems/rivalHouses.js): each rival House's head, purse, family and retinue on the map. Each errand (trade, court, shadow the player, invest in land, home) is scored by what it is worth now: weights × the best bargain's gain / think.tradeNorm (capped), the best estate's yield / invest.minYield, standing at court / standing.favourite; trait weights add; the ambition's errand is multiplied by think.ambition. Money is gold; days are game days.
rivalHouses._invest: Land: a rival buys listed estates (systems/landMarket.js) within range it can pay for keeping reserve gold, spending at most maxShare of the purse, yielding at least minYield a year; rents reach the purse weekly. Below sellBelow gold it lists its cheapest estate at sellAt of value.
rivalHouses._standing: Court favour per realm: fades by decay every decayDays; at favourite or more the crown pays standing × pension gold a week from its treasury, and the rival's whispers there cut whisper + standing/whisperPer reputation. Renown adds renown/renownPer favour per visit.
rivalHouses._guard: After the player falls on a retinue it hires up to step guards at cost each (max in all), each adding per strength and wage gold a week. A House at waylay.feud or more that is too weak to waylay you hires one a week (keeping invest.reserve + 3 × cost) when enough guards could match waylay.edge × your army. Once forgetDays pass without an attack or a hiring, one is let go each week.
rivalHouses._waylay: A rival at feud >= feud, with no hunt in `every` days, within `range` hexes, and whose retinue is at least edge × your army's strength may ride out to waylay you: its retinue turns hostile (WorldUnit.isHostile) and the road-encounter choices apply. It hunts for `days` days. Robbed you (or beat your army): feud robFeud. Beaten off: feud +beatenFeud and it keeps beatenGuards of its guards; you take attack.lootShare of its purse with no reputation or karma lost.
rivalHouses._ties: The rival Houses' regard for each other (-100..100, both ways), starting in `start`. Ousting another as a court's favourite: oust. Each week, Houses whose realms are at war change by `war`, allied realms by `allied`, and two Houses both at feud >= commonFoeFeud with you by `commonFoe` (a shared enemy). Each year it fades `drift` toward 0, and two Houses at matchMin or more wed grown children with chance matchChance (+match). At allyAt or more they are allies: feud you earn with one adds spill × as much with the other; at enemyAt or less, it eases the other's feud by spill/2 × as much.
rivalHouses._ambitions: Each head pursues one ambition (weighted by traits' ambitions; revenge only at feud >= revenge.feud). Fulfilled → +renown and a new one; abandoned after giveUpDays. wealth: purse + land value reaches max(min, now + min(now × (grow − 1), maxMore)); land: holds `more` estates more; favour: a court's favourite; revenge: pays for `plots` more plots.

rivalVoice._doc: How the rival Houses' heads look and talk (systems/rivalHouses.js persona, systems/rivalAudience.js lines). A head's MANNER comes from their first trait: proud → haughty, courtly → silken, scheming → soft, grasping → brisk, homebody → plain. STANCE comes from their regard for you (−feud + what they remember): warm ≥ 30, civil ≥ −10, cold ≥ −50, else hostile. Each list is picked by hash of the day and the head, so the same meeting reads the same. Placeholders: {you} your name, {yourHouse} your House, {first} their first name, {myHouse} their House, {seat} their seat, {passion} their passion, {other} another House, {place} a town, {good} a good, {gold} an amount, {realm} a realm, {child} a child's name, {days} days. *Asterisks* are stage directions.

hairYoung: with a young man's first beard
features: a hawk hooded on the wrist
a cough they try to hide
a jeweled dagger they toy with
a limp from an old fall

passions.name: falconry
passions.line: My falcon took a heron on the wing last week. You should have seen it stoop.

passions.name: the hunt
passions.line: There is a boar in the woods above {seat} that has killed two of my hounds. I mean to have him.

passions.name: verse
passions.line: I have been writing verses. Badly, my wife says. She is right.

passions.name: dice
passions.line: I lost forty gold at dice last night to a tanner. A tanner!

passions.name: horses
passions.line: I have a grey mare out of the southern studs. Fastest thing on four legs between here and the sea.

passions.name: the faith
passions.line: I have endowed a chapel at {seat}. A man should think of his soul.

passions.name: chess
passions.line: Do you play chess? No? A pity. You would understand me better.

passions.name: building
passions.line: I am raising a new hall at {seat}. Oak beams, a gallery for the musicians.

passions.name: the sea
passions.line: I would sooner be on a deck than in a saddle. The sea is honest.

passions.name: old books
passions.line: I bought a chronicle of the old kings from a monk. Half of it is lies, the best half.

memoryLabels.repelled: your failed attack on their retinue
memoryLabels.spokeForThem: how you spoke for them at court
memoryLabels.loanDemanded: how you pressed them for a debt

warm: *inclines their head, just so* {you}. You may approach.
Ah, {you}. One of the few worth my time on these roads.
civil: *looks you over from the saddle* {yourHouse}. You wished to speak with {myHouse}?
Well. {you}. I suppose the road is common to all.
cold: *does not dismount* You have a moment. Use it well.
{yourHouse}. *the name sounds like something spat out* Speak.
hostile: *a gloved hand rests on the sword* You dare stand in my road?
I would not cross the street to piss on {yourHouse} if it burned. What do you want?

warm: *a warm smile, both hands open* {you}! The roads are kind today.
My dear {you}. I was only just speaking of you, and well.
civil: *a courtier's bow* {you}. What a pleasant surprise. Mostly pleasant.
{yourHouse}, on the open road. How the world turns.
cold: *the smile stays, the eyes do not* {you}. How… unexpected.
Ah. {yourHouse}. One hears so much about you at court. Very little of it kind.
hostile: *the smile is a blade* {you}. I had hoped the roads would be safer this season.
How brave of you, to come so close. Or how foolish. Say your piece.

warm: *speaks low, almost fondly* {you}. We should talk more, you and I.
Friend {you}. Sit a moment. Tell me what you know.
civil: *watches you with half-closed eyes* {you}. I wondered when our roads would cross.
*quietly* {yourHouse}. I know a great deal about you. Tell me something I don't.
cold: *says nothing for a long moment, then* …{you}.
*a soft voice, a hard face* You have walked a long way to stand within reach of my men.
hostile: *barely above a whisper* I have been thinking about you, {you}. Every night.
*smiles without warmth* Strange. My men said you would avoid this road.

warm: {you}! Good. Business is good, the roads are dry. What do you need?
Ha, {you}. Walk with me, I am pricing wool.
civil: {yourHouse}. I have a cart of {good} going bad in this heat. Be quick.
*glances at your purse before your face* {you}. Talk.
cold: Every hour I stand here costs me money. What is it?
{yourHouse}. You cost me a good deal at market. Say what you want.
hostile: You have no idea what your meddling has cost me. None. Get out of my road.
*counting coins, not looking up* If you came to beg, the answer is no. If you came to threaten, the answer is also no.

warm: {you}, well met! Come share the fire, there is stew.
*a broad grin* I hoped I would see you. How are your people?
civil: {you}. Fair road to you. What brings you?
*nods* {yourHouse}. I am bound home to {seat}, and glad of it.
cold: *folds their arms* {you}. I have nothing to say that you'll want to hear.
Say it plain, {you}. I've no patience for courtly talk.
hostile: You've got some nerve. Say what you came to say and be gone.
*spits* {yourHouse}. My father would have had you whipped from this road.

bereaved: *wears mourning black* My {parent} is a month in the ground. Forgive me if I am short.
*the black armband is new* We buried my {parent} at {seat}. The House is mine now. All of it.
attacked: *a fresh bandage on the arm* You have the gall to show your face, after what you did on the road?
*the retinue bristles at the sight of you* My men still bear the marks of your ambush.
insulted: *jaw tight* I have not forgotten your words. Nor has anyone who heard them.
shamed: *does not meet your eye* You need not gloat. I know how it went.
ousted: *sourly* You'll have heard, no doubt. {other} has the crown's ear now. A passing fancy.
poor: *the retinue looks thinner, the cloaks patched* These are lean days for {myHouse}. Lean days.
loss: *grumbling* I bought dear and sold cheap. Every fool in the market made money but me.
gloat: *a thin smile* You look a little lighter in the purse than when last we met.
triumph: *in high spirits* You find me on a good day, {you}. A very good day.
favour: *smoothing a new cloak* The crown has been generous. I find I like court.
wedding: *flushed with wine* My {child} is wed! There was dancing for three nights.
birth: *beaming* I have a new child, {you}. Named {child}. Loud as a bugle.
land: *pleased* I have bought land. Good land. Tenants who pay.
profit: *in a good humour* The {good} sold well. A fine week.
hunting: *the retinue rides armed, and close* You are a hard {you} to find.

recall.gift: Your gold reached my coffers. I have not decided what it bought you.
recall.parleyOk: Last time we spoke, you were almost reasonable.
recall.parleyFail: Last time you spoke to me, you wasted my afternoon.
recall.insult: I remember what you called me before the crowd.
recall.attacked: I remember the road where your men fell on mine.
recall.repelled: You tried your steel on my retinue once. You remember how that went.
recall.ambushBeaten: *colouring* We need not speak of the road.
recall.robbedYou: I hope the purse you lost to my men was not too dear to you.
recall.match: Our children are wed. That counts for something, even between us.
recall.flattered: You have a silver tongue. I have not decided whether I trust it.
recall.threatened: The last time we met, you threatened me. I do not forget threats.
recall.helped: You did me a service. I keep accounts of those, too.
recall.spokeForThem: You spoke for me at court. I have not forgotten.
recall.loanGiven: You lent me gold when I needed it. That was decently done.
recall.loanDemanded: You pressed me for coin in front of my own men.
recall.bloodPrice: The blood price you paid was fair. I have kept my side.
recall.duelYouWon: You bested me with the blade. I still feel it in this arm.
recall.duelYouLost: I drew first blood, the last time we crossed swords.
recall.declined: You refused my offer. I wonder that you came back.
recall.estateSold: You sold me good land at a fair price. Few can say that of you.
recall.truceBroken: *shifts in the saddle* There was a truce. Things happened.

haughty: *a long pause* …Very well. I will think less ill of you.
You speak better than I expected. Let it be calmer between us.
silken: *laughs softly* You are charming when you want something. Very well.
Peace? How refreshing. Let us try it, for a season.
soft: *nods slowly* Perhaps. Perhaps we have both been fools.
I will remember you said that. In the good way.
brisk: Fine. A feud is bad for trade anyway.
Fair words. I will take them, they cost me nothing.
plain: *sighs* Aye. Maybe it's gone on long enough.
That's plain spoken. I can respect that.

silken: *the smile thins* How very sincere. I am almost moved.
Darling {you}, you will have to try harder than that.
soft: You think I don't see what you are doing?
brisk: Talk is cheap. I don't deal in cheap.
plain: Pretty words. I've heard them before.
*shakes their head* No. Not after everything.

haughty: *a servant takes it; they do not look at it* Acceptable.
silken: Oh, you shouldn't have. *tucks it away at once*
How generous. I will speak warmly of you, for a week or two.
soft: *weighs the purse in one hand* And what does this buy, I wonder?
I'll take it. I won't forget who gave it.
brisk: *counts it, there and then* All there. Good.
That'll cover the tolls to {place}. My thanks.
plain: *surprised* I didn't expect that. Thank you.

haughty: Again? You think {myHouse} can be bought by the month?
silken: Another? My dear, people will talk.
soft: *narrows the eyes* Twice. Now I really wonder what you want.
brisk: I'll take it. But don't think it's buying what you think.

haughty: *goes white, then red* You will answer for that. By the gods, you will answer for it.
*a deathly calm* Say that again. I want my men to remember it exactly.
silken: *laughs, too loudly* How droll. Everyone heard that, did they? Good.
Oh, that will be all over court by Sunday. Thank you.
soft: *smiles, slowly* I will remember that. I will remember it for a very long time.
brisk: Insults cost nothing, and they're worth what they cost.
You'll pay for that. Not today, but you'll pay.
plain: *fist clenched* Say that again and we'll settle it here.

insultAgain: Again? You have no other song?
*wearily* You said that before. It was not clever then, either.

ok: *preens a little despite themselves* Well. You are not wholly without eyes.
*a reluctant smile* Flattery. And yet I find I don't mind it.
fail: Do you take me for a child, to be sweetened with honey?

cowed: *glances at your host and back* …There's no need for that. Let us both keep to our own roads for a while.
defiant: *laughs* Threats? I have more swords than you have friends.
Come and try it, then. I'll be at {seat}.

warm: Go well, {you}. My door at {seat} is open.
Fair roads. Send word if you need anything.
civil: *a curt nod* Until the next time.
cold: *turns the horse without a word*
We are done here.
hostile: Watch your back on the roads, {you}.
*to their men, loud enough to hear* Remember that face.

business.trade: I'm carrying {good} to {place}. Prices there are a scandal, which is to say: good for me.
business.buying: I'm bound for {place} to buy {good}. Don't you dare get there first.
business.court: I'm for court at {place}. One must be seen, or one is forgotten.
business.shadow: *evasively* I have business in {place}. Private business.
business.home: Home to {seat}. My bed, my dogs, my own roof.
business.invest: There's land for sale near {place}. Good land. Mine, soon.
business.none: Deciding where to go next. The roads are long.

ambition.wealth: I mean to see {myHouse} rich again, as rich as my grandfather's day. Richer.
ambition.land: Land is the only wealth that stays. I want more of it.
ambition.favour: A House without a crown's ear is a House no one remembers. I will be heard at court.
ambition.revenge: *looks straight at you* I have one ambition left, {you}. You know what it is.

topics.noNews: Nothing worth telling. The roads, the weather, the price of bread.
topics.familyNone: I have no wife, no children. Only the House.
