topics.heirLine: {child} will have it all after me. Pray the gods give them better sense than I had.
topics.askYours: And your {child}? I hear they are coming along.

you.warm: I think you are better than your House's name, {you}. I didn't always.
you.civil: I think you are a rival. Nothing personal. Mostly.
you.cold: I think you have done {myHouse} more harm than you know.
you.hostile: I think about you more than I think about my own children. That should tell you.

topics.butBad: But I have not forgotten {reasons}, either.

otherHouse.ally: {other}? Family, now, near enough. Speak ill of them and you speak ill of me.
otherHouse.friend: {other} are decent people. We understand one another.
otherHouse.neutral: {other}? I don't think about them much.
otherHouse.enemy: {other} are snakes. I'd sooner deal with you than with them, and that's saying something.

bloodPrice.pitch: *looks at you a long while* There is a way to end the worst of this. {gold} gold, a blood price, paid now. And I call off my men for {days} days.
bloodPrice.accept: *takes the purse* It is done. For {days} days, {myHouse} keeps its blades sheathed. You have my word.
bloodPrice.decline: Then we go on as we are.

loan.pitch: *lowers the voice* I am short of coin this season. Lend me {gold} gold, and I'll repay {owed} in {days} days.
loan.accept: *clasps your forearm* I'll not forget this. {days} days.

speak.pitch: The court of {realm} listens to you. Speak for me there. It will cost you a little of their good opinion, and earn you a great deal of mine.
speak.accept: *genuinely moved* That's a real kindness. I won't forget it.
speak.decline: I see. Your own name first. As it should be, I suppose.

buyEstate.pitch: You hold {estate}, near {place}. I'll give you {gold} gold for it. More than it's worth.
buyEstate.accept: *shakes your hand* Good land. A good bargain for both of us.
buyEstate.decline: Your loss. The offer won't come again soon.

match.pitch: My {theirChild} is of an age, and so is your {yourChild}. Let them wed. I'll waive the dowry. Blood binds better than words.
match.accept: *embraces you, to everyone's surprise* Then we are kin, or near it!
match.decline: *hurt, then hiding it* As you like.

against.pitch: {other} wrong us both. Shame their lord to their face, or fall on their retinue. Do that, and our quarrel is all but done.
against.accept: *a slow smile* Good. I'll hear of it, wherever I am.
against.decline: Then you're no use to me in that.

duel.pitch: *draws the sword halfway* Enough words. Let us settle this with steel, first blood. Here, now, before both our people.
duel.decline: *sheathes the blade with contempt* I thought as much.

realmIntel._doc: Who may read a realm's private books (src/systems/realmIntel.js). roles: the offices (player.currentTitle / kingdomTitle, in the realm you are sworn to) that read each kind; '*' = any office. bands: the street's word for a number, highest first; a null minimum is the floor. Rulers and spies placed in the realm read everything.

containers._note: What chests, crates, barrels and shelves hold, and what it costs to help yourself. systems/containers.js rolls a container's contents from the world seed, the place and the restock period, so the same chest holds the same things until it restocks; only what the player removes is saved. 'loot' rows are [goodId, chance, min, max]; a building-type table under 'byBuilding' replaces the furniture default there.

townProps._note: Props a town is dressed with — wells, stalls, carts, barrels, fences, fields — built from LPC sheet cells by world/townProps.js and registered as editor objects (CustomObjects). 'rect' is [col, row, w, h] in 32px cells of the sheet; the bottom-left cell is the anchor. 'solid' is how many bottom rows block movement (0 = walk over). Names drive what you can do with them (a 'Barrel' or 'Crate' can be looked into, a 'Well' drawn from).

fence.name: Fence
fence._gateDoc: A gate opens and shuts (world/townProps.js setGate; world/innerMap/gates.js): shut (cell) it blocks like the fence, open (the open cell: the leaf swung back against its left post) it is walked through. Gates stand shut; the player opens one from its menu or by walking into it, and it stays as they leave it (world.gates, saved); townsfolk open a shut gate as they pass and shut it behind them.
fence._joinDoc: Fence pieces joined by their neighbours (world/townProps.js joinFences): the ThatchedHouses fence sheet is a full set — each key names the sides (n, e, s, w) a cell has fence on, and its cell carries the rails out to just those sides, so corners, T-joins, crossings and run ends meet. gateLeft/gateRight are the run pieces either side of a gate, with its gateposts. The legacy h/v pieces above stay registered so old saves still draw until the town is entered.

townProps._growthDoc: Town fields grow through the year (world/townProps.js growFields): each cycle is [dayOfYear, field kind] steps (Spring 1-30, Summer 31-60, Autumn 61-90, Winter 91-120); a field keeps the last step reached, a few days early or late by where it lies. Kinds not in a cycle (plowed: fallow land) stay as they are.
townProps._harvestDoc: A ripe town field can be brought in (ui/innerMapFields.js): help the farmer for a share of the crop (workShare, hours by the field's size), or steal a handful at the theft odds (systems/containers.js). Its crop is perCell x cells; once it is all taken the field lies harvested (plowed) till the new year.

felling._note: Trees felled on the inner map (world/innerMap/felling.js; player/gathering.js). Each tree's own fell block names its stump (left where it stood, sheet stumps_<season>.png, scripts/make_stump_sheet.py), its hardness (the def's resistance: % less a blow does, so a great oak takes more swings than a birch), wood (its log count when it is not a wild tree) and gives (more besides the logs: { item, qty [min, max], chance, seasons }). A stump's grub block is grubbing it out: hardness, firewood, gives. Felled trees are kept on world.felled[hex] (saved): the stump stands sproutDays, then a sapling (sapling, or palmSapling for a palm) grows there, a tree again treeDays after the felling; a stump grubbed out leaves the ground clear for good. fallSeconds: how long the tree takes to come down.

granary._note: Grain at a town's granary (ui/innerMapGranary.js): it sells from the town's food store, keeping back reserveDays of the people's needs, at priceMult of the market's ask, in these lots; it buys grain into the store at buyMult of the ask, as long as there is room (the store holds Economy.FOOD.stockDays of needs).

buildingFloors._note: Floors above the ground (world/innerMap/floors.js). A building has between minFloors and maxFloors floors (by its type), never more than its builders can raise: the player's own by the techs they know (baseFloors, raised by techFloors), a town's by its size (townCraft); a camp of the Dawn of Man raises none. Which count a town building has is fixed by its place. upperRooms: what each floor above the ground holds, by type (the last repeats); rooms: what goes in each kind of room.

mapTasks._note: Jobs done in person on the street map (systems/mapTasks.js, ui/innerMapTasks.js). Each job is one of the templates; 'jobs' sets a job's own spots and wording, 'byStat' covers jobs not listed. Spots: 'doors' are building types ('*' any, 'house'), 'props' are town-prop id prefixes. parHours is how long a good worker takes, in game hours (one real minute is an hour). Glyphs are ui/icons.js names.

farm_hand.say: Carry the grain sacks from the fields to the barn.

stable_boy.say: Muck out the stalls and fetch fresh straw.

well_digger.say: Dig the trial pits where the dowser marked.

woodcutter.say: Chop and stack firewood for the hearths.

shepherd.say: The flock has strayed. Find them and bring them back to the fold.

herb_picker.say: Gather the healer's herbs from the meadows round the village.

tannery_hand.say: Scrape the hides and turn them in the pits.

smith_striker.say: Strike where the smith taps: heats at the forge and the stock round the smithy.

brewhouse_hand.say: Carry the malt to the brewhouse vats.

physicians_aide.say: Take the physician's draughts round the sick in their houses.

dock_worker.say: Unload the wagons: crates from the warehouse to the market stalls.

courier.say: Run the parcels round town before the bells.

mason_helper.say: Carry bricks and mortar to the builders.

tavern_bouncer.say: Keep the peace round the taverns tonight.

market_crier.say: Cry the merchants' wares at the busy corners.

scribe_assistant.say: Count the stock at the stores and report the tally.

rat_catcher.say: Rats in the cellars. Corner them before they bolt.

night_watch.say: Walk the watch round the town and deal with any trouble.

cargo_hauler.say: Move the goods between the market districts.

herald.say: Read the royal proclamation at the square and the crossroads.

arena_fighter.say: An exhibition bout in the square. Give them a show.

tax_collector.say: Knock on the doors that owe and collect what's due.

tutor.say: Take the children round the market counting, then hear them recite.

pit_fighter.say: Bare knuckles behind the tavern. Win, or at least stand.

spy_errand.say: Deliver the sealed letter. Don't let the watch see you.

sowing_hand.say: Broadcast seed along the plowed fields.

flood_bank.say: Carry sandbags out to the banks.

camp_sutler.say: Run provisions out to the soldiers' billets.

haymaker.say: Scythe the hay and stack it.

harvest_reaper.say: Bring in the grain with the reaping gang.

grape_picker.say: Strip the orchards before the frost.

granary_loader.say: Haul the new harvest up into the granary.

snow_clearer.say: Dig the streets and square out of the drifts.

woodcutter_winter.say: Cut and carry firewood to the hearths.

itemArt._doc: The painted things a job shows on the street map (ui/jobItems.js): carried loads, the item over a work spot, the heaps at pick-ups and drop-offs, the strays. sheet is built by scripts/terrain_modern/build_job_items.py; items are [x, y, w, h, scale] in it (128px a tile; scale > 1: drawn that much bigger, the cell shrank it). byGlyph: the item a task glyph shows (a job's own 'item' wins for its glyph); a glyph with none keeps its plate. carry: how it is held (arms | shoulder | hand | tool; arms if unlisted).

performTasks._note: Street performance, devotion rites and meditation done in person on the street map (systems/performing.js, ui/mapTasks/performTasks.js). Busking acts: pick a pitch, perform timed sets (setSeconds, real seconds = game minutes) while folk within 'pull' tiles drift over; anyone standing within 'listen' tiles during a set counts. The crowd a town should give is expectedPerCrowd × the town's crowd multiplier (data/earlyJobs.json busking). Glyphs are ui/icons.js names.

juggling.say: Find a pitch, then juggle set after set. Each set draws more of the street. Fumble and they drift off.

singing.say: Find a pitch and sing. Choose songs that suit the hour: hymns for the morning, ballads by day, drinking songs at night.

storytelling.say: Find a pitch and tell a tale in parts. Listeners stay to hear the end. Don't give them the same kind of turn twice running.

fortune_telling.say: Walk up to the passers-by marked for you and read their fortunes. Look for the tell: hands, clothes, bearing. A reading that fits them earns a coin.

preaching.say: Preach from the church steps or the square. Stir them up, but not into a fright: keep the fervour high without tipping it over.

pitchLabels.square: Set up your pitch in the square
pitchLabels.crossing: Set up your pitch at the crossing

beats.label: The wolves close in on the camp…
The bridge gives way beneath the hero…
The bishop's mule eats the bishop's hat…
The miller mistakes the duke for a sack of flour…
The old soldier never came home…
She waited at the harbour for forty years…
A door opens in the hillside where no door was…
The stars spell out a name…
Their eyes meet across the burning hall…

tones.label: The promise of the life to come

tells.farmer: Earth under the nails, a sunburnt neck.
tells.merchant: A fat purse and a quick eye on yours.
tells.guard: A scar on the knuckles, a hand that rests on a hilt.
tells.priest: Ink-stained fingers and a worn string of beads.
tells.villager: Patched sleeves, a ring on the finger, a glance toward home.
tells.noble: Rings on every finger and a bored look.
tells.traveler: Dust to the knees and a pack that has seen roads.

fortunes.text: The rains will be kind to your fields this year.
A long road ends with a heavy purse.
A blade hangs over you, but your arm is the stronger.
Someone at home is thinking of you this very hour.
A great house will fall, and yours will rise.
You'll be taller than your father, and twice as clever.
A stranger's coin will change your luck.
Love waits at the next well you drink from.

busking.readingAsk: {name} the {type} holds out a palm. ({tell}) What do you see?

lines.pitchSet: You set out your hat at the {pitch}.
lines.setDone: {n} stopped to watch. Coins clink in the hat.
lines.drop: You fumble a club! A few drift off.
lines.askSong: What will you sing? (The bells say it is {hour}.)
lines.askBeat: What happens next in the tale?
lines.askTone: How will you preach? (The crowd's fervour: {fervor}.)
lines.beatRepeat: They've had that already. It falls flat.
lines.beatFresh: A fresh turn. They lean in.
lines.songOff: Odd choice for the hour; a few drift off.
lines.fervorCold: They shuffle their feet. The sermon is cold.
lines.fervorSweet: Amens ring out. They are with you.
lines.fervorFrightened: Too much! They back away in fright.
lines.readFits: "That's it exactly!" A coin for your trouble.
lines.readMisses: They frown, unconvinced, and toss you a copper.

say.church: Light a candle at the church door, walk the circuit of stations around it, then kneel at the steps.
say.holy: Light a candle at the shrine, walk the pilgrims' circuit, then kneel.
say.wayside: There is no church here. Light a candle at the square, walk a circuit of the town, then kneel.

lines.station: Pause and pray at the station ({i} of {n})
lines.kneel: Kneel at the steps and pray
lines.disturbed: {name} brushes past and breaks your prayer.
lines.candleLit: The candle catches. You begin the circuit.

say.field: Find a quiet spot away from the bustle and sit still a while. Passers-by will break your focus.
say.holy: Find a quiet spot at this holy place and sit still a while.

spots.label: Sit in the quiet at the edge of town

lines.sitting: You settle and close your eyes.
lines.disturbed: {name} passes close by. Your focus slips.
lines.broke: You got up. The stillness is broken.

wildTasks._note: Wild work done in person on the inner map (ui/mapTasks/wildTasks.js, systems/wildTasks.js): foraging, hunting, fishing, winter trapping and ice fishing, smuggling and pickpocketing. The rewards stay with the old handlers (player/foraging.js, player/seasonalWork.js, ui/actionMenu); this file holds the wording and the feel of each task. Radii are in inner-map tiles, times in real seconds unless named Hours. {name} style fields are filled in by the task.

prompt.inPersonHint: Do it in person on the map: the better you do, the better it goes.
prompt.quickHint: A plain day's result, no walking.

forage.title: Foraging
forage.say: Gather what you find. Marked patches are plain to see; search near cover to turn up the rest.
forage.nearby: You spot signs of something to the {dir}.
forage.empty: You searched but found nothing of value today.

hunt.title: Hunting
hunt.say: Follow the sign to the {name}. Creep up: walking near it alarms it, standing still calms it. Loose when you are close.
read: A tuft of fur on the thorns.
hunt.bolted: The {name} bolts! It runs a way off and stops, ears up.
hunt.gone: The {name} bolts into cover and is gone.

bow._doc: Shooting game with a bow (player/huntingBow.js; the stalk in ui/mapTasks/wildTasks.js, the quick hunt in ui/actionMenu/jobs.js). Hunting at range needs a weapon of `weapons` (the best grade held is the one in hand: data/craftGrades.json) and at least one of its ammunition (the weapon's own `ammo`, else `ammo`: a crossbow shoots bolts); every shot uses one. hit chance = base - max(0, dist - freeTiles) x perTile - alert x alert + clamp(log10(kg / sizeRef) x perSizeDecade, sizeMin, sizeMax) - (fleeSpeed - speedRef) x perSpeed x (0.5 + alert) + the Hunting & Butchering rank (0..4) x perRank + steadiness x perSteady (steadiness: 35 - Hunting.hitThreshold, i.e. combat x 2 + strength + the better of the Hunting and Archery aim; Archery's steady perk counts half) + (the bow's grade effect - 1) x perGradeEffect + the weapon's aim + (the arrow's grade effect - 1) x perArrowEffect (+ wounded when the beast is already hurt), clamped to [min, max]. A hit kills outright on the kill chance (base + rank x perRank + (grade effect - 1) x perGradeEffect - log10(kg / sizeRef) x perSizeDecade + close within closeTiles + wounded on a beast already hit), else the beast is wounded and runs (boltSeconds x woundedBolt) and must be shot again. A miss spooks it (it bolts), unless Archery's second arrow lets you loose again first; after missesBeforeGone misses it is gone. recover: the share of missed arrows that land whole (laid on the ground where they fell, to pick up; the quick hunt fetches them for you) and of arrows pulled whole from a kill (each one in it). wear: each shot adds perShot x the weapon's wear / the grade's effect x (0.5 + a roll) to the bow's wear (out of 100, kept on player.bowWear by bow and grade); at 100 it breaks, and past 100 - snapBelow each shot has snapChance to snap early. fumble: a miss's chance of a slip that hurts you (damage hp). quick: the quick hunt's shots at most, at dist and alert (alert rises by alertPerMiss). Species weight (kg) and fleeSpeed come from data/animals.json species (a quarry with none: defaultKg, defaultSpeed).

words.noBow: You need a bow to hunt game at range: make one at a workbench (wood and sinew or cord) or buy one from a bowyer or blacksmith. Snares and traps need no bow.
words.noArrows: You have a bow but no arrows (or a crossbow but no bolts). Fletch arrows at a workbench (wood, feathers and a stone or iron head), turn bolts (wood and iron), or buy a sheaf at market.
words.hit: The arrow strikes home: the {name} is down.
words.wounded: The arrow strikes the {name}, but it runs on, hurt. Follow it and loose again.
words.miss: Your arrow flies wide. The {name} bolts.
words.secondArrow: Your first goes wide, but you nock again before the {name} can run.
words.gone: The {name} is gone, and your arrows with it.
words.worn: Your {bow} is badly worn: it may not last much longer.
words.arrowLies: Your arrow lies in the grass where it fell: pick it up.
words.recovered: You pull {n} arrow(s) whole from the carcass.

fish.title: Fishing
fish.say: Go down to the water and cast. When it bites, strike!
fish.quiet: Nothing biting… the water is quiet.
fish.snapped: The line snapped! The {name} got away.
fish.shy: The fish here have gone shy. Try along the bank.
fish.left: You reel in and walk off.

trap.title: Trapping
trap.runSay: Paw prints mark the game runs. Set your snares on the runs, under cover, then walk back round and check them.
trap.setSay: Lay a trap line: set the snares on the game runs, under cover. Where you set them decides what the line takes.
trap.tendSay: Walk your trap line from snare to snare. Only the snares you reach are emptied.
trap.tooClose: You already have a snare here.

setNote.good: A good spot: right on the run, with cover.
setNote.poor: Open ground: little will pass this way.

trap.set: Set a snare on the run
trap.allSet: The snares are set. Walk back round and check them.

iceFish.title: Ice Fishing
iceFish.shoreSay: Cut a hole near the bank and fish through it.
iceFish.farSay: Walk out to where the ice is thin, cut a hole and fish.
iceFish.cutShore: Cut a hole in the ice
iceFish.cutFar: Out on the thin ice: cut a hole

smuggle.title: Smuggling
smuggle.say: Carry the {item} to the fence's door. Keep out of the watch's sight.
smuggle.hand: Hand the goods to the fence
smuggle.seen: {name} of the watch is looking your way!

pickpocket.title: Pickpocket
pickpocket.say: Get close to the {name} and lift the purse while they're not looking. Step back when they turn round.

dawn._doc: The Dawn of Man (world/dawn.js): a world begun before any town. Wandering clans settle good ground, villages grow into towns and bud new clans, towns gather villages into chiefdoms that become the realms. Years are 120 days.

lines.settle: The {clan} clan made camp {where} and stayed: {name} is founded.
lines.bud: Families of {name} set out as the {clan} clan, looking for land of their own.
lines.town: {name} has grown from a village into a town.
lines.chiefdom: {ruler} of {name} gathers the villages about it: the {realm} is born.
lines.path: A trodden path now joins {a} and {b}.

dawn.welcome: The world is young. No town stands, no crown is worn. You were born to the {clan} clan, wandering the wild with your kin — {kin}. Lead them to good ground and make camp for good, and watch the first villages rise.

birth._doc: Who the player is born among at the dawn (player/dawnBirth.js): a father, a mother and siblings, all of the clan; they walk with the player while the clan does and settle in its village.

hearth._doc: Kin share their pot (DawnBirth.kinMeal): with no food in your packs, at your clan's camp or in your home village, your family feeds you — up to maxOwed meals you haven't paid back. Come home with more food than keepFood and they take it into the pot, a unit for each meal owed.

lines.fed: You eat from your family's pot: {kin} share what they have.
lines.fedOwed: Your kin feed you again, but with a look: {owed} meals now that you have not paid back. Bring food to the pot.
lines.refused: Your kin have fed you {owed} times and you have brought nothing back. Tonight there is nothing for you in the pot: hunt, forage or bring food home.
lines.repaid: You add {qty} food to your family's pot.
lines.settled: Your clan makes camp for good. {name} is your people's home now — {kin} with you.

cultures._doc: Cultures and their languages (world/cultures.js, systems/languages.js). Every settlement keeps the culture it was founded with (settlement.culture), and so the tongue its people speak, whoever rules it later. Languages of one family are half-understood by each other's speakers (familyShare). Fluency runs 0-100: see `levels`. `build` is what a culture's towns are made of (wall and roof materials of the composed buildings, data/buildingKit.json, and a bias on house styles), used for worlds made since terrainGen 3.
cultures._learning: How the player and the rival Houses learn (systems/languages.js). Immersion: a day spent where a language is spoken (in its settlement, or its realm's land) gains `immersion` fluency, scaled by `pace` for the band you are in (it gets slower as you get better), less with a translator doing the talking. Talking to people gains `talk` (a few times a day). A tutor's lesson in a town costs `tutor.cost` and gives `tutor.gain` in the town's tongue or another its scholars teach. Old saves: the player speaks the tongue where they stand and is `legacyFluency` in those of realms they are known to.
cultures._translator: An interpreter hired in a town: speaks its tongue, yours, and one or two more of the realms about. A hiring fee, a daily wage (they leave when unpaid), and a comprehension of `fluency` in what they speak.
cultures._effects: What not understanding costs (by your level in the tongue spoken where you are). trade: added to the trade bonus (buy and sell). audience: the fluency (or a translator) a lord's audience needs. dialog: which conversation choices need which level.
cultures._realms: Courts: a realm's court speaks its own tongue and learns the tongues of the realms it deals with (`courtLearn` a contact). Diplomacy between courts with no common tongue goes harder (`diplomacy` by the best level either court has in the other's tongue); same family helps.
cultures._rivals: Rival Houses on business in a town of another tongue: they hire a translator for `fee` when the purse allows (else trade at `badDeal` and win half the favour at court), and learn `learn` fluency a visit.
cultures._dynasties: House names for the cultures the character code has none for (world/characters: Imperial, Woodland, Nomadic, Religious and Maritime keep theirs).

lines.noWords: *You share no words with {name}. They speak {language}.*
lines.someWords: *You catch a word here and there of their {language}.*

architecture._note: How each culture builds its towns, for worlds made since terrainGen 4 (world/townPlanner.js, world/cultures.js). `families` are the culture's own buildings, composed from the building kit (data/buildingKit.json kit) by scripts/compose-buildings.js into data/buildings.json with their culture stamped on (a family with buildingTypes makes each of those types: halls, trades, workshops). `mix` is which house styles stand where (core: the middle of town, mid, edge: the outskirts). `plan` is the town's shape: straight or winding streets (wind), lanes close or far apart (laneGap), houses shoulder to shoulder or apart (gap, setback), the square (plaza: square, green or long; its centre piece and corner pieces, stall count), how the streets are surfaced (streets: the top-left cell of a 2x2 block of streetSheet, painted by scripts/terrain_modern/build_streets.py, or none for dirt tracks), lamps (none, square, street, all), props along the streets, and things standing about town (scatter). `interior` is what their houses are made of inside (data/innerMapRenderer.json interiorArt).

Imperial.summary: Red brick and terracotta in a grid of straight streets; a great paved square with a fountain and columns, lamp posts everywhere, rows of tall townhouses shoulder to shoulder.

Religious.summary: Pale limestone and whitewash under slate, arched double doors and pointed windows; a cloister-like square of cream flagstones round a white column, planters and a calm grid of streets with gardens.

Arcane.summary: Dark stone and grey brick under violet shingles and verdigris tiles, tall ornate windows lit at all hours; dark slate streets lined with lamp posts on every lane, a black obelisk in the square.

Woodland.summary: Black-and-white timber framing and golden thatch, flower boxes and porches; winding dirt lanes, cottages set apart in their gardens, oaks left standing in town and a village green with a great oak instead of a paved square.

Swamp.summary: Low huts of tarred and weathered boards under dark, mossy thatch; few windows, crooked dirt paths wandering between scattered homes, a well and a fire in a trampled clearing, trees crowding in.

Nordic.summary: Long low halls of Falu-red and tarred log siding under green turf roofs, carved rune-stones; dirt lanes bending round a village green with a rune-stone, pines between the houses.

Mountain.summary: Squat, thick-walled houses of fieldstone and dark granite under heavy slate, few small windows; a tight, walled-in huddle with narrow straight lanes paved in dark flags, a deep stone well in a small square.

Nomadic.summary: Low mud-brick houses with flat roofs and brown tile; dusty unpaved tracks, homes spread wide apart, and a long open bazaar street crowded with stalls instead of a square.

Desert.summary: Whitewashed and sand-coloured adobe with flat parapet roofs, carved lattice and pointed windows, arched double doors; houses packed wall to wall along sandy lanes, a great bazaar square round a pool with a date palm at each corner, potted trees along the lanes and palms standing about the town.

Maritime.summary: Clapboard and plaster houses painted blue, teal, yellow, white and rose under blue slate; one long cobbled harbour street with a market strung along it, lamps, barrels and crates at every door.

shipHulls._doc: Ships as bluecarrot16 composed them in the LPC Ship tileset's Tiled map ("[LPC] Ship" by bluecarrot16, commissioned by Sander Frenken, OGA-BY 3.0+ / CC-BY 3.0+ / GPL 2.0+; assets/lpc/lpc-ship/CREDITS-ship.txt). Generated by scripts/extract-ships.js — do not edit by hand. Each ship: w x h cells of 32px, `waterline` the hull's lowest row, `tiles` in drawing order (col/row from the top-left; a 64px tile is anchored at its bottom-left cell).

commissions._doc: Hired work (systems/commissions.js): bring your own goods to a town's tradesmen — the miller grinds your grain, the baker bakes your bread, the smith forges your tools — and pay for their time with gold (a fee) or with part of the product (a cut). The town trades are data/markets.json `recipes` (where the place is big enough for the trade); the craftsmen's work is data/crafting.json `recipes` by station, done by whoever in town keeps that station (`stations`: the smallest place that has one, and how hard a recipe they'll take on). A job takes as many days as the trade's hands need (`perDay` runs a day for a craft; a town trade works `tradeShare` of its daily capacity for you, at least `minPerDay` — a mill grinds a cartload in a day), and is collected at the same town.
commissions._supply: Order a piece (Commissions.commission with opts.supply): the craftsman finds the stuff himself. The inputs, and the parts they are made of (a grip is wood and leather), are bought out of the town's market stock at its price on top of his fee; what the town has none of cannot be ordered.

deckLife._doc: Life aboard ship on the inner map (systems/deckLife.js, world/innerMap/deckLife.js, ui/innerMapDeck.js). The ship's crew stand on deck as people with a role and a station; where they go and what they do follows the situation at sea (fair, night, storm, an event, boarders). maxOnDeck caps the hands drawn (the rest are below). Orders are once a day each (ship.deckDay). Boarding: a pirate fight from a voyage event, met on deck, is fought hand to hand; its outcome is the event's own win/lose block (Ships.finishBoarding).

animals._doc: Living animals of the inner map (world/innerMap/animals.js places and moves them; ui/innerMapAnimals.js draws them, hooks them into hunting, fights and butchering). Sheets: walk / attack / death, each a 4x4 grid of 128px cells, a row per direction (up, left, down, right), four frames a row; every sheet of one animal shares the cell and the feet anchor, so they line up. Built from the hand-out sheets by scripts/build-animal-sheets.py, which also gives each drawTiles (the cell's width in tiles). Speeds are tiles a second; distances are tiles; hp and bite as the player's health. temper: skittish (flee), defensive (flee; may turn and fight when hurt or cornered: fightChance), territorial (warn inside threatRadius, charge inside chargeRadius or if you stay), hunter (notice: stalk — rolls aggression, more by night; packs decide together). fleeBelow: the health share it breaks off at; maxBites: a bout's bites before it backs off (0 = no limit). livestock: a settlement's flocks — killing one is theft (value: its worth).

carcass._doc: A kill lies where it fell until butchered (ui/innerMapAnimals.js; kept on world.wildlife.carcasses, so it is there when you come back). It keeps freshDays whole days, then each day takes rotPerDay off what butchering yields (never below minYield); after lifetimeDays the scavengers have had it. Carried: a beast up to maxCarry kg (plus perStrength kg for each point of strength over 5) can be carried, up to shoulderKg over the shoulders and heavier ones dragged; the walk slows by slowPerKg a kg, never below minSpeed. Butchering takes seconds of work at the spot (secondsBase + secondsPerKg a kg, at most secondsMax) and minutes on the clock (minutesBase + minutesPerKg a kg, at most minutesMax).

swimming._doc: Swimming on the inner map (world/innerMap/swimming.js: where; player/swimming.js: what it does). A stroke is one tile of water the player can't stand in. pathCost: how much dearer a water tile is than a step when choosing a route (so a walk round wins when not much longer); speed: a stroke's pace against a step; the Swimming skill (systems/practiceSkills.js, data/practiceSkills.json: XP each stroke, levels) cuts the energy a stroke costs and quickens it. A swim washes you up to hygieneMax and soaks the clothes (comfort). Cold water (cold.seasons, or a cold hex) hurts each stroke. Below tiredBelow energy you struggle (struggleHealth a stroke), below spentBelow you go under (drownHealth). Too laden (pack fuller than ladenShare) or too spent, you can't take to the water.

diving._doc: Diving under the water of an inner map (player/diving.js: breath, costs and the finds on the bottom; ui/innerMapDiving.js: going under, moving, picking up and surfacing; ui/innerMapLayers/underwater.js: the view below). Dive Under on water you can swim in (or the V key while swimming): you swim about under the surface by clicking, through water only, at underwaterSpeed of a swim. Breath: seconds by the Diving skill's level (systems/practiceSkills.js, data/practiceSkills.json skills.diving: perks breath, coldResist against cold.breathMult, speed under the water; XP for each dive at surfacing); it drains drainPerSecond a second (cold.breathMult in cold water). After surfacing the breath must come back before the next dive (recovery): a dive that left windedShare of the breath or less leaves you winded for the skill's winded seconds (blackoutMult times that after a blackout); an easier one takes catchBreath seconds plus a share of the difference by how much breath was spent (to the power curve). Out of breath, each second costs overHealthPerSecond health (cold.mult in cold water) and risks a blackout (blackout.perSecond, plus perOverSecond for every second past, plus cold.blackout): you come up, take blackout.health hurt and lose everything picked up on this dive. Health gone under the water is drowning. Each second under costs energyPerSecond (less for a good swimmer: practiceEnergyCut at the top Swimming level). Going under washes you a little (hygiene) and chills you (comfort; cold.comfort more). The bottom of each map is scattered once a day (bed): a share of its divable water cells (perTile, at most max finds) each get a find from tables[kind][depth] (a 'nothing' draw leaves the cell bare) or, rarely, treasure (treasure.chance by kind and depth, by luck, times wreckMult within wreckRange tiles of a wreck); seeded by the world, the map and the day; what is taken stays taken until the next day. bed.looks: how a find is drawn on the floor. spear: spear fishing for the fish below, with a fishing spear (its own _doc).

fish._doc: Fish swimming about under the water while diving (ui/innerMapLayers/underwaterFish.js; caught only with a fishing spear: spear below). Each species: colours (back, belly, fin, mark), pattern (bars|spots|stripe|none), length in tiles, height (of its length), speed in tiles a second, school [min, max] (a shoal keeps together), weight (how often it is the one met) and the waters it lives in. perCell: fish to each divable cell near the diver (by water kind), up to max; they live within radius tiles of the diver and are met anew past it. Within shy tiles of the diver a fish darts away at fleeSpeed times its speed. dorsal: extra pixels of back fin (a shark's).

spear._doc: Spear fishing under the water (player/spearFishing.js: the odds, the catch, the spear's wear; ui/innerMapSpearFishing.js: aiming, the F key, the right-click entries, the reticle and the flight of the spear). Needs a fishing spear (good id item) in the packs; without one the player is told so. Under the water, point at a fish and press F (or right-click it): a fish within the strike reach is thrust at, one farther off but within the throw reach has the spear thrown at it on its line; past that it is out of reach. aimRadius: tiles from the cursor a fish may be to be the one aimed at. modes.strike / modes.throw: reach (tiles), base (the chance at point-blank), near (tiles before distance starts to tell), perTile (chance lost each tile past near), breath (seconds of breath it costs), cooldown (seconds before the next strike: the arm back, the line hauled in), wear (wear on the spear for the strike). hit: speedPer = chance lost per tile a second the fish is moving (a darting fish is quick: underwaterFish fleeSpeed), sizePer = chance gained per tile of the fish's length over sizeRef (a big fish is an easier mark), levelPer = chance gained per Fishing level over 1 (the Fishing skill of the rod: data/skillPacks/food.json, systems/foodSkills.js), gradePer = chance gained per point of the spear's grade effect over 1 (core/grades.js: Poor 0.8 … Masterwork 1.65), min / max the bounds. wear: durability = wear a Common spear takes before it breaks, times its grade's effect to the power gradePow (a finer spear lasts longer); hitWear = more wear when a fish is struck (it fights on the point); snapPerLength = the chance a struck fish snaps the shaft, per tile of its length, divided by the grade's effect. The wear is kept on the player (player.spearWear: { grade, wear }) for the best spear held, which is the one used; a broken spear is gone from the packs. A miss scares the fish within scare.radius tiles of where the spear went off for scare.seconds (they bolt from it at underwaterFish fleeSpeed). catches: the good a species becomes when speared ({ item, rarity }: rarity sets the Fishing XP from the fishing skill's xp table); a species not listed goes by its length (bySize: up to each max length, that item). The Fishing skill's bigger perk may make it the bigger kind (its bigger map). xp: Fishing XP for each strike (perStrike), plus the rarity's XP for a catch; a catch also counts as a find on the dive (Diving XP), and is lost with the rest of the haul in a blackout.

practiceSkills._doc: Practised skills (systems/practiceSkills.js): skills that rise in levels by doing them, for the player and for NPCs alike. A holder keeps total XP by skill on holder.practiceSkills ({ diving: 120, swimming: 40 }); the level comes from the XP: reaching level L+1 from L takes round(xp.base * xp.growth^(L-1)) XP, up to maxLevel. levelNames: the word for each level (1-based). Each skill has perks, one value per level (index 0 = level 1); text says what a rise gives ({d}: the gain, {a}: its size either way, {v}: the new value) and show describes the value ({v}). Diving (player/diving.js): breath = seconds on one breath; coldResist = % of the cold's extra breath drain shrugged off; speed = % faster underwater; winded = seconds to recover after a dive to the limit (or a blackout); catchBreath = seconds after a dive with plenty of breath left (between the two by how much breath was spent). xp: perSecond under; limitMult on the whole dive when you surface with limitShare of breath or less (or black out); find / treasure for each common find / treasure off the bottom; swimmingPerSecond: swimming XP for time under. Swimming (player/swimming.js): energySaved = % less energy a stroke; speed = % faster strokes; xp per stroke swum. migrate: an old save's player.swimPractice (0..400 strokes of practice) becomes this many XP per point in each skill. npc: NPC skill levels seeded from who they are (systems/townsfolk.js persons and walking NPCs): base level by skill, plus by role, plus coastal (a town by the sea or a lake) for the water skills (and there coastalTrades: a share of some roles work the water as fishers, sailors or pearl divers, picked by a hash of who they are), plus up to spread more by a hash of who they are, and ageBonus a level per that many years over 20 (at most ageMax); children (under adultAge) get half. They grow by work: dailyXp by role (coastal ones for the water trades), reckoned each townsfolk season. notableLevel: the least level shown on an NPC's card.

milestones.title: Your Years: 25
milestones.text: The quick learning of youth is behind you: skills come at a steady pace now.

milestones.title: Your Years: 40
milestones.text: Forty: the body's skills come a little harder to learn now; crafts and words as readily as ever.

milestones.title: Your Years: 50
milestones.text: Seasoned: the crafts, healing and dealings you have practised are a level better for the years behind them.

milestones.title: Your Years: 55
milestones.text: Your knees aren't what they were: climbing, swimming, diving, blades and stamina are a level down, and come harder now.

milestones.title: Your Years: 60
milestones.text: Sixty: hard work tells — sailing, felling, mining, hunting and the fields are a level down.

milestones.title: Your Years: 61

gathering._doc: player/gathering.js: which skill a swing at an object trains (by objectType, or the resource it gives), the energy a swing costs before the skill's effort perk, the extra share of the resource the logs / stone perk adds, and the rarer finds a broken rock may give by the hex's terrain (weights; qty [min, max]).
gathering._axesDoc: The best edge in your packs makes every blow at a tree or a stump land harder (×mult; player/gathering.js toolFor/damageMult) and is named when the tree comes down. Tools (an iron axe among them) or steel tools; with neither, your knife and a borrowed hatchet. On rock the same goods are the pick (picks).
gathering._xpDoc: xpPerHardness: more Woodcutting / Mining XP for a harder tree or rock, per point of its hardness (resistance), on top of the skill's perFell / perBreak.

wrecks._doc: A ship struck down on the town map breaks into salvage (world/innerMap/harbour.js scatterWreck): `pieces` [min, max] by hull, floating on the water where she lay and up to `spread` tiles round (each a ground item you swim or wade to and pick up). `loot` picks a piece's goods by weight (kind = how it floats: planks, rope, sail, crate, chest; drawn from the LPC lumber, crate and chest sheets). A crate carries goods from her hold when she had any, else one of crateGoods; a strongbox (chest) holds gold, only on the hulls listed in its `hulls`.

furniture._note: Furniture for the player's homes (systems/furnishing.js, world/innerMap/furnishing.js). Each piece draws with an interior furniture type (its art in innerMapRenderer.json → interiorArt.furniture, its glyph in ui/icons.js) and does what that type does (ui/objectActions/data.js FURNITURE_ACTIONS: a bed sleeps, a chest stores, a hearth cooks). footprint [w, h] in tiles; a piece longer one way turns (R) to lie the other. minSettlement: the smallest place whose furniture maker makes it. comfort: added to the comfort need each hour spent in a home it stands in (all pieces together capped at comfortCap). restBonus: a bed's sleep restores this much more (0.2 = +20%).

crops._doc: Crops the player sows on land they tilled on the inner map (systems/crops.js; ui/innerMapFarming.js). Each crop: its seed good (a GOODS entry in playerEconomy.json, sold in markets of the listed settlement types at qtyMult x population), the product good and yield range per tile, the growth days of each stage after sowing (sown -> sprout -> growing -> ripe; their sum is the days to ripen on a well-watered day each), the seasons it may be sown in, hardy (survives winter frost, growing at winterGrowth), water need (low/medium/high -> dry days it bears before it wilts), and the art of each stage on an LPC sheet ([col, row] in 32px cells; h: 2 for a sprite two cells tall, its row the lower cell). A day of rain or a watering counts as a wet day (full growth); a dry day grows dryGrowth. A ripe crop keeps spoilDays before it rots in the ground. Yield: a roll in the range x care (wet days / days grown, floored at careFloor) x the farming level's yield (data/skillPacks/food.json: also more dry days borne, frost days lived through, quicker work).

craftGrades._doc: Quality grades of made goods and the craft skills that set them (core/grades.js, player/crafting.js, world/marketGrades.js). A held stack keeps plain qty in player.inventory; the units above or below Common are counted in player.craftGrades[good] = { poor, fine, excellent, masterwork } (Common is whatever is left). price: what a unit of the grade fetches and costs against a Common one. effect: how much more it does (nourishment, healing, protection, a weapon's cut, how long clothes stay fresh, how much tools help at the bench). below: the quality score under which a roll lands on this grade (the last has none).
craftGrades._skills: Craft skills: each recipe in data/crafting.json names its `skill` (or takes its station's). Levels 0-10 live on player.skills like the other skills and rise with crafting xp (OddJobs.gainXp, x xpScale). titles: the name of a level band (the highest `min` not above the level).

craftGrades._legacy: Old saves kept one crafting rank (player.crafting.xp): the first time a craft skill is read it starts at legacyPerRank x that rank.
craftGrades._roll: A craft's quality score = base + level x perLevel + workshop (0, 1 or 1.2 in one you own) x workshop + tools x tools x the tools' power x their grade's effect + (attribute - 5) x perAttr - (difficulty - 1) x perDifficulty + the inputs' average grade above Common x perInputGrade + the forge minigame ((score - 50) / 50 x forge), plus a triangular noise of +-noise from the seeded RNG. The grade is the first whose `below` the score is under.
craftGrades._tools: What counts as tools at the bench, and how much each helps (the best you carry is used; it wears by its grade: a Fine set lasts longer).
craftGrades._wear: Goods worn on the body: the best grade held of a kind sets how much it does. clothing: freshness lost a day is divided by the grade's effect (player/core/needs.js).
craftGrades._gradeable: Goods that come in grades: every product of a data/crafting.json recipe (unless the recipe says quality: false) plus these, which the towns' own trades make.
craftGrades._market: The towns' craftsmanship (world/marketGrades.js): a level 0-10 = typeLevel + a fixed local knack (+-knack, by the town's name) + guild (a town guild that guards the good) + perWorksLevel x the level of the player's works making it. Its market stock comes in grades: poor = poorBase - poorPerLevel x level, fine = fineBase + finePerLevel x level, excellent = excellentPerLevel x (level - excellentFrom), masterwork = masterworkPerLevel x (level - masterworkFrom), shares of the stock (each at least 0); the stalls are restocked in grades every `restockDays`.

market._labels: The word for a town's craftsmanship (the highest `min` not above its level)

craftGrades._soap: A cake of soap in the pack is used when you bathe or wash your clothes by hand (player/core/needs.js): this much more hygiene and clothes freshness, x its grade's effect.
craftGrades._hired: Hired work (systems/commissions.js) comes out in the town's grades: its craftsmanship level for the product, with the trade's skill (a commission is not rolled: the shares are the market's mix, rounded down, the rest Common).

livestock._doc: The player's own beasts (systems/livestock.js; market and herds panels in ui/actionMenu/livestock.js; drawn on the inner map at their keeping place by ui/innerMapAnimals.js). Bought and sold by the head at a town's livestock market, kept at a place of yours that suits them (places), fed or grazed, bred, aged, shorn and milked by the day. Days: a year is 120 days (world/seasons.js), so ages and lifespans are in game days. space: room one head takes at a place. feed: gold a head a day when it cannot graze (grazing places: the share of feed still bought each season). products: per adult (femaleOnly: hens and milkers) a day, times the season; they go into the herd's store, collected like a property's goods. A livestock property (works) turns its working beasts into its own output instead (the Pasture's wool, the Dairy's cheese, the Ranch's meat, the Horse Ranch's horses): its output scales with the working head kept there against its target (a founding herd of that size comes with the property). slaughter: what butchering one yields (by hand on the inner map, or at the yard from the herds panel). breeding: daily chance for each adult female in its seasons (a male of her kind must be kept with her), young per birth, rest days before the next. market: who sells it (minType, chance by settlement type, likes: terrain where it is common and cheaper; resource: a map resource nearby that always brings it), stock heads by settlement type; price by type, season and how many are left (scarcity). fallback: the inner-map species drawn (and fought) until data/animals.json has one of the same id; scale shrinks it.

fodder._doc: Fodder bought for a herd comes out of the nearest town's food store (foodPerGold units for each gold of fodder) and its price goes into that town's purse. A town with no food to spare sells none: the herd goes hungry.

places._doc: Where beasts can be kept. capacity: space units. species: who may be kept there. grazing: they find their own fodder outside winter (feedShare by season). works: a livestock property's working beasts (weight each) and its target head — the founding herd it starts with and the head at which it yields its old output; maxFactor: most an overstocked one gives. draft: a farm whose horses (and pigs' manure) lift its harvest, at most draftMax.

market._doc: typeStock: stock multiplier by settlement type. typePrice: price multiplier. seasons: price by season (spring dear, autumn's cull cheap). liked: price where the land suits it; foreign: where it shuns it. scarcity: price = base x (1 + scarcity x (1 - stock/target)), within [scarcityMin, scarcityMax]. restockDays: days to refill from empty. sellShare: what the market pays you of its asking price; young / old / sick: further multipliers. droveFee: gold a head a hex to drive bought beasts to a place elsewhere (small, medium, large); droveMax: farthest hexes a drover goes.

health._doc: Daily: illness strikes a herd (chance x (1 + crowding x over capacity share)), spreads to another (spread), kills (deathPerDay) or passes in sickDays. Hunger: unfed beasts lose hungerLoss health a day and give nothing; at 0 they die. Old age: past the lifespan, oldDeath a day. Predators: a beast taken from a keeping place outside a settlement, by the hex's herds of data/animals.json terrain (that herd's chance x rate a day), of the sizes named.

map._doc: How many of a herd stand on the inner map at its place (the rest are out of sight), and how far apart.

graves._doc: Graveyards and the trade in death (world/graveBook.js, world/graveArt.js, world/townPlanner.js, world/innerMap/graves.js, systems/graveyards.js, ui/innerMapGraves.js, ui/actionMenu/graveyards.js). Every town keeps a burial ground on settlement.graveyard: its churchyard (planned beside the church or temple, or on the edge of a village) with yard[type] = [width, depth] tiles (the planner shrinks it to fit): an iron railing along its street front with a gate in the middle, plots one tile wide and two deep (the marker at the head, the mound or open pit on the tile below it), a path between them and a walk after each row. A grave is one townsperson who died (systems/townsfolk.js), with their name, dates, cause and a marker for their station. Graves are leased for a term; when one runs out and no kin renews it, the plot is cleared and the bones go to the charnel house. The player can consecrate a building lot of theirs as a burial ground and lease its plots to the town's families.
graves._classes: A dead townsperson's station, from their role (or retired trade): it decides the marker, the coffin, the lease the family wants and the goods buried with them.
graves._terms: Grave leases: years (null = in perpetuity) and the price as a multiple of a ten-year lease. A family that can't pay its usual term takes the next shorter.
graves._pricing: A ten-year plot costs plotBase[type] x scarcity, scarcity = (targetYears / years of room)^elasticity clamped to [min, max], years of room = free plots in town (the churchyard's and every private ground's) / the town's deaths a year. The parish charges parishMult of that; a private ground charges its owner's policy (cheap/fair/dear).
graves._markers: What a grave is marked with, and how it ages. inputs: what raising it takes from the town's market stock (a cross from wood, a headstone from stone). Wooden markers rot to a bare mound after rotYears, then to nothing (unmarked) after goneYears; stone weathers to headstone_old after oldYears and headstone_broken after brokenYears. tiles: its footprint [w, h] on the map (an art manifest overrides it).
graves._art: The painted sprites: artDir/<id>.png, 128 px a tile, each fitted to its tiles box and stood on its bottom, centred (scripts/make_graves.py). build:data merges artDir/manifest.json in as `art` ({ id: { w, h, tilesW, tilesH } }); a marker with no art yet is drawn as the old dug-grave mound until it lands. A grave dug in the last freshYears shows its mound beside the marker.
graves._coffins: A coffin takes `planks` planks a size from the town's stock (the coffin-maker's timber); none to be had, the dead go in a shroud.
graves._seed: A town's churchyard is not new when the player first sees it: seedFill of its plots hold the dead of the years before (seedRecent of them recent, on leases still running; the rest old graves held in perpetuity).
graves._town: When the churchyard is full, the sexton clears the graves whose leases have run out (the bones to the charnel house). Still full for newGroundAfterYears, and its purse holds twice newGroundCost[type], the town opens a new ground beside the old (newGroundShare more plots). With nowhere to lie, the dead go in the common pit.
graves._consecrate: Consecrating a lot of yours as a burial ground: a fee to the town's temple (into the town's purse), refused where your standing in the realm is below minStanding. Its plots are laid in rows within the lot.
graves._leasing: Your ground's leases: each lapse is renewed by kin still in town at the class's renew chance (if the purse can pay); unrenewed, it lies lapsed until cleared. A sexton you hire clears one for sextonFee[type] (to the town's purse); or dig it up yourself on the town map.
graves._bones: Bones: one set from every grave cleared. The charnel house of any town takes them for nothing (piety); a city's or capital's bone-grinder buys them (boneBase x glut, paid from the town's purse; the glut eases glutDecay a day). The charnel sells its own to you at charnelPrice.
graves._mill: A bone mill of your own, built on a lot of yours: cost gold (the builders' wages, into the town's purse) and inputs (bought from the town's market stock at its price), standing after days. It grinds grindPerDay sets of bones a day into mealPerBone bone meal each.
graves._meal: Bone meal sells to the town's farmers (mealBase x farmFactor[type] x glut, from the purse). Every unit spread on their fields raises the town's soil by soilPerUnit (to the harvest's soil max): next harvest's yields follow the soil.
graves._ossuary: An ossuary shrine on a lot of yours: cost gold and stone, and foundBones sets of bones to found it (more may be laid in after). The town's people come to pray for their dead: perVisit[type] each, visitors a day = min(maxVisitors[type], bones / bonesPerVisitor), paid from the town's purse.
graves._gravedigger: The sexton's work, a day labour: each burial and each clearing in town leaves a grave to dig; you dig up to maxPerDay of them for payPerGrave[type] each from the town's purse, at an energy cost. The town's own sexton digs sextonPerDay a day when you don't.
graves._kin: Your own dead (children, a spouse, the heads of your House before you): laid to rest in a ground of yours (no lease: they lie in perpetuity) or the parish churchyard at its fee; a coffin and marker of your choice bought from the town's stock at its price. kinMarkers: what you may raise over them.
graves._robbery: Robbing a grave (taking its goods, or digging it up without the right): a theft (systems/containers.js stealOdds and stealGoods: the odds by witnesses, guards, the hour and the worth; the fine, the record and the cells), with `reputation` standing lost on top if caught; what you take is hot. Digging up a lapsed grave on your own ground is no crime.
graves._goods: The goods of death, registered into the player's goods table: bones and bone meal trade only through the charnel house, the bone-grinder, your mill and the farmers (noMarket); grave goods (trinkets buried with the dead) sell anywhere.

BONES.name: Bones
BONES.description: A set of bones from a cleared grave. The charnel house keeps them; a bone-grinder buys them; a bone mill grinds them to meal.

BONE_MEAL.description: Bones ground fine: a fertiliser the farmers spread on tired fields.

ambient._note: Ambient life on the inner map (ui/ambientModel.js, ui/innerMapLayers/ambient.js): fires that flicker and spit embers, smoke from chimneys, steam, lamps at night, and moving parts drawn from art in artDir when it exists. Units: tiles and seconds. Positions ('at') are in tiles from the anchor tile's top-left (an object's anchor is its bottom-left cell). Particles are effects drawn in code (soft puffs, glints); anything that is an object (a waterwheel, sails, a bucket) comes from art listed in <artDir>/manifest.json, merged in as `art` by build:data.
ambient._windDoc: A map's wind for the day: strength from `calm` [min, max] by hash of the place and day, times the weather's factor. `lift`: how much it blows toward/away from the view rather than across.
ambient._weatherDoc: Wet or snowy air: smoke hangs thicker (alpha) and breaks up sooner (life).
ambient._kindsDoc: Particle kinds. color [r,g,b]; life [min,max] s; rise tiles/s at birth (riseDecay -1..1: above 0 it slows with age, below 0 it gathers speed, so the plume is thick at the mouth; gravity pulls it back down); size [start,end] tiles; alpha at its fullest; fadeIn share of life; drift how much the wind takes it; wobble/wobbleHz a sideways sway; spread tiles either side of the source; fling a sideways throw; twinkle Hz; glow true = drawn additively after the night lighting (it shines in the dark).
ambient._schedulesDoc: How hard a kind of fire burns by the hour: hours [[hour, level]] (linear between); season multiplies by season; cold adds up to that share on cold days (below 15°C, full by -10°C); max caps it. A building or fire is lit once the level passes its own threshold (so houses light one by one), and burns harder as it rises.
ambient._buildingsDoc: By building type (buildings.json buildingType): chimney = emitters on each chimney pot (noChimney: where on the roof they rise instead when the building has no chimney drawn, [share of width, tiles below its top]; without it, no chimney, no smoke); roof = emitters across the roof (at [share of its width, tiles below its top]); schedule from `schedules`; share = the part of such buildings that burn at all. `_default` serves any type not listed (a type set to {} gives nothing).
ambient._objectsDoc: Map objects by def id. frames: play the sheet cells to the right (count, step in cells [dx, dy], fps) — the campfire sheet already holds 4 flame frames. emit: particles at 'at'. glow: a soft warm halo (radius tiles, day/night strength, flicker). light: a light in the night light map (radius tiles). lit: a schedule that turns the whole thing on (a lamp lit only in the dark).
ambient._furnitureDoc: Inside a building, by furniture type (data/furniture.json types; interiorArt sprites). Same fields as objects.
ambient._breathDoc: Breath in the cold: below `belowC` °C each person outdoors breathes out a small puff every `every` seconds (only the player and those on screen). head: the mouth's height above the tile centre (tiles); side: how far before the face, toward the way they look.
ambient._partsDoc: Moving parts drawn from art in artDir (each an entry in its manifest.json: file, w, h, tilesW, tilesH, frames, pivot). Nothing shows until the art is there. on: buildingTypes / objects; place: 'waterSide' (beside the building's gable wall over water, the lower part in it: at [out from the wall, down from its foot row's top] when the map stood the mill on the bank, world/innerMap/mills.js); waterline: tiles below the hub the water stands; submerged: how much of the wheel shows under it (alpha; clipped at the waterline); squash: narrower than tall, seen a little from the side, 'roof' (top middle of its roof), 'object' (at the object's anchor); at: offset tiles; spin: turns a second (rotation about the pivot, clockwise; below 0 the other way; 0 = none); scale: its size against the manifest's tiles; fps: frame rate when it has frames; every: play the frames once every so many seconds (else loop); sway: degrees of rocking; spray: particle kind thrown up where it meets the water; unlessWater: only where 'waterSide' finds no water.

autoUpkeep._doc: The day's last hours (src/player/autoUpkeep.js). When the player ends the day with action points left, their character spends them on their own upkeep, most pressing need first, using the game's own actions at their own costs: eat from the pack, bathe, wash clothes, make camp, take a room, talk with the locals, sit by a campfire, a hotel's bathhouse or supper. Coin goes to the town that gave the service. The setting (Settings > Gameplay > The Day's Last Hours) chooses 'full' (upkeep and leisure), 'upkeep' (only needs that matter: food, clean body and clothes, a bed) or 'off'.

below._comment: A need under this value is worth seeing to (0..100). Clothes: freshness.

weight._comment: How much each need's shortfall counts when choosing what to do first.

coin._comment: The most the character spends on itself in an evening: maxPerDay, and never more than purseShare of the purse. 'upkeep' mode spends only on rooms, baths and laundry.

coldBath._comment: A wild bath colder than this (comfort, data/hospitality.json bathing.cold) is only taken when hygiene is under 'unless'.

chat._comment: Talk with the locals (the Talk to Locals / tavern-talk action: 1 AP, its own need effects). At most 'times' a night.

campfire._comment: Build a campfire (the Build Campfire action: 2 AP, 2 wood, its warmth and its need effects).

services._comment: Inn and hotel services (data/hospitality.json services) the character may buy for itself, by what they are for. Rooms: the cheapest tier at or above 'room'.

meta.description: LPC terrain spritesheet — tile classification and mapping
meta.note: The terrain sheets are 512x832 = 16cols x 26rows of 32x32 tiles. Tiles are organized into autotile transition groups. This file separates FILL tiles (uniform solid ground) from EDGE tiles (transition/corner tiles that blend two terrains). Only tiles in 'fills' should be used for ground rendering.

_note: Documents the spritesheet's autotile transition groups.
Each terrain type occupies a 6-col x 3-row block:
Additional 3x3 blocks at cols 6-8, 9-11 are TRANSITION BLENDS
between two terrain types — these contain mixed-color edge tiles.
The center tile of a transition blend IS the target terrain fill.
FILL  = fully opaque, uniform color (stddev < 8) — safe for ground
TXTR  = fully opaque, textured (stddev >= 8) — may be fill or edge
TRANS = partially transparent — definitely an edge/overlay tile

groups.name: grass
groups.description: Grass autotile. Outer edges at cols 0-2 (all TRANS). Inner corners at [0,3-5] (TRANS). Fill variants at [1,3-5] (TXTR grass-colored) and [2,3-5] (FILL). Center fill at [1,1].

groups.name: grass_dirt_transition
groups.description: Grass-to-dirt transition edges. ALL tiles are TXTR with blended green+brown colors. No fills — edge-only.

groups.name: grass_sand_transition
groups.description: Grass-to-sand transition edges. Center [1,10] is FILL sand. Corner tiles [0,9],[0,11],[2,9],[2,11] are TXTR with blended sand+green — NOT dirt fills despite brownish color.

groups.name: dirt
groups.description: Dirt autotile. Outer edges at cols 0-2 (TRANS). [4,1] is EMPTY (inverse center). Fills at [3,3-5] and [4,3-5] (all FILL dirt).

groups.name: sand
groups.description: Sand autotile row. Edges at cols 0-2 (TRANS). Fills at [5,3-5] (FILL sand).

groups.name: dirt_sand_transitions

groups.description: Dry dirt/clay autotile. Edges at cols 0-2 (TRANS). Fills at [6,3],[6,4] (FILL). Rows 7-9 cols 3-5 are EMPTY.

groups.name: dry_dirt_transitions
groups.description: Dry dirt transition blocks. Center fills at [6,10] (FILL) and [9,9],[9,10] (FILL). Tiles at [8,9],[8,10] are TXTR edges — NOT fills despite similar color.

groups.name: water_group_1
groups.description: Water autotile transition blocks (4 x 3x3 blocks). Center fills at [11,1] (FILL water). [11,4] is EMPTY (inverse). All other tiles are TXTR transitions blending water with grass/other.

groups.name: water_group_2
groups.description: Additional water transition blocks. Multiple 3x3 groups. No additional verified fills in this area.

groups.name: stone_fills
groups.description: Stone and dark stone fill block. 4x4 grid of textured but uniform fills. Rows 12,15 = lighter stone (~101,113,100). Rows 13,14 = darker stone (~97,107,97). All TXTR but same-terrain throughout — safe to use as fills.

groups.name: water_fill_block
groups.description: Water fill block. All 8 tiles are verified FILL (~42,132,151). Uniform shallow water.

groups.name: water_group_3
groups.description: More water transition variants. Center fill at [21,1] (FILL water). All others are TXTR transitions.

groups.name: deep_water
groups.description: Deep water autotile transitions. Only [24,1] is FILL (~23,58,85). Multiple 3x3 transition blocks span cols 0-2, 5-7, 10-12. Tiles at cols 3-4, 8-9, 13-14 are TXTR edges with shifted colors (25-28,63-82,90-113) — NOT fills.

fills._note: Each entry lists ONLY tiles verified as solid uniform fills (FILL) or same-color textured fills. NO edge, corner, or transition tiles. Pixel coords = col*32, row*32.

rejectedTiles._note: Tiles previously listed as fills that are actually edge/transition tiles. Documented here to prevent re-adding them.

meta.description: LPC tree sprite sheets — seasonal tree variants extracted from 512×576 sheets
meta.note: Each sheet is laid out as a grid. Column 0 contains shadow blobs. Actual tree sprites start at column 1. The grid is 4 cols × 4 rows of 128×144 blocks. Within each block, the tree sprite is approximately 96×120, offset from the block origin.

layout.description: Column 0 = shadow sprites (skip). Columns 1-3 × Rows 0-3 = tree sprites.

shadows.description: Column 0 contains dark/gray shadow ovals per row — not trees

deciduous_round.description: Row 0 — Round-canopy deciduous trees (green in summer, pink/orange in autumn)

deciduous_blossom.description: Row 1 — Blossom/flowering trees (pink canopies in spring/autumn)

deciduous_bushy.description: Row 2 — Bushy/dense deciduous trees, includes bare winter tree at col 0

conifer.description: Row 3 — Coniferous/evergreen trees (pine/spruce), col 0 has stump

bare_tree.description: Leafless bare tree (winter sheet col 0, row 2)

meta.description: LPC vegetation sprite sheets — plants, flowers, mushrooms, and rocks

wildflowers_summer.note: Width is 144 not 128 — extra partial column

rocks_grass.note: Rocks are 2×2 tiles (64×64 px). 3 color variants: dark brown (rows 0-3), tan (rows 4-7), blue-grey (rows 8-11). Each variant has 6 rocks in a 3×2 grid.

rocks_cliffs.note: Rocks are 2×2 tiles (64×64 px). 6 cliff rocks in a 3×2 grid.

plants.description: Standalone plant sprites from seasonal plant sheets. Non-autotile cells that have transparent edges.
plants.note: Plant sheets mix autotile transition tiles with standalone sprites. Standalone sprites have transparent borders and are suitable for object-layer placement. The runtime analyzer identifies these automatically.

wildflowers.description: Individual wildflower sprites from seasonal wildflower sheets

flowers.description: Flower sprites from the flowers.png sheet (352×160)

rocks.description: Rock sprites from 'Rocks, Grasslands.png' (192×384). Each rock is 2×2 tiles (64×64 px). Sheet has 3 color variants (dark brown rows 0-3, tan rows 4-7, blue-grey rows 8-11), each with 6 rocks arranged in a 3×2 grid of 64×64 blocks.

rocks_cliff.description: Cliff rock sprites from 'Rocks, Cliffs.png' (192×128). Each rock is 2×2 tiles (64×64 px). 6 rocks arranged in a 3×2 grid of 64×64 blocks.
